Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:31: Gardens of Perpetuity which they enter, beneath which rivers flow; therein they have whatever they desire. Thus Allah rewards the mindful(of Him) :
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:32: those whom the angels take up(at death) while they are goodly, saying, “Peace be upon you; enter the Garden(of Paradise) on account of what you used to do.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:33: Are they but waiting for the angels to come to them, or for the command of your Lord to come? Those before them did likewise. And Allah did not do them any injustice, but to themselves they used to do injustice.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:34: So the evils of what they had done afflicted them, and they became surrounded by what they used to ridicule.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:35: And those who had associated(others with Allah) said, “Had Allah willed, we would never have worshiped anything apart from Him—neither us, nor our forefathers, nor would we have prohibited anything without(permission from) Him.” Those before them did likewise. So are the messengers responsible for anything but evident proclamation?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:36: For very truly, in every community We sent a messenger: “WorshipAllah and avoid false masters.” So some of them Allah has guided, and some of them have deserved misguidance. So journeythrough the earth and look what the outcome was for the disbelievers.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:37: (Even) if youare concerned about their guidance,(still) Allah surely does not guide whomever He leads astray, and they will have no helpers.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:38: And they have sworn by Allah their most solemn oaths that Allah does not resurrect whoever dies. Yes indeed, it is a promise binding on Him, but the majority of mankind does not know.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:39: (This is) to clarify for them what they differ over, and so that those who have denied know that they were liars.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:40: Indeed, Our only saying to anything, once We have wanted it, is to say to it, “Be,” and so it is .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:41: And those who emigrated for Allah after they had been dealt with unjustly—We will surely settle them in a good place in the Earlier(Life) , and the reward of the Hereafter is truly greater, if they only knew.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:42: Those are the ones who endured patiently, and in their Lord they placetheir trust.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:43: And never did We send as messengers before youexcept men to whom We reveal . So askthe people of the Reminder if you do not know.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:44: (We sent them) with evident proofs and books. And We sent down to youthe Reminder, that you may clarify to mankind what was bestowed upon them from on high, and that they may reflect.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:45: Do those who have schemed evils feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to cave in beneath them, or that the punishment will not come upon them from where they are unaware?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:46: Or that He will not seize them(suddenly) during their movement so that they cannot thwart(Him) ?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:47: Or that He will not seize them gradually? Yet indeed, your Lord is truly Compassionate, Bestowing of mercy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:48: Have they not seenall things that Allah has created—their shadows revolving from the right and the left, prostrating to Allah as they shrink away?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:49: And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth of every treading creature, as well as the angels, and they do not act arrogantly—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:50: fearing their Lord above them and doing whatever they are commanded.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:51: And Allah has said: “Donot take two gods; He is but One God, so of Mealone be in awe.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:52: And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and religion is His forever. Are you then mindful of anyone other than Allah?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:53: And whatever blessing youhave is from Allah, then when harm touches you, it is to Him that you cry for help.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:54: Then when He lifts off harm from you, a group of you associate(others) with their Lord,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:55: so as to deny what We have given them. So enjoy yourselves, for you will come to know.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:56: And they set up to what they do not know a share of what We have provided for them. By Allah, youwill surely be asked about what youused to fabricate.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:57: And they set up to Allah daughters—Highly Exalted is He—and unto themselves whatever they desire.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:58: But when one of them is given the glad tidingsof a female(infant) , his countenance remains darkened as he suppresses his anguish.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:59: He hides himself from people because of the evilness of the glad tidings he has been given. Should he keep it, in shame, or bury it(alive) in the dust? Undoubtedly, evil is the way they judge!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:60: For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is an evil example, while to Allah belongs the highest example. And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:61: And if Allah were to hold mankind for their injustices, He would not leave upon it a single treading creature, but He defers them to a stated term. Then, when their term has arrived, they cannot delay it by one hour nor can they advance it.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:62: And they set up for Allah what they themselves hate, while their tongues describe the lie that theirs is the best(reward) ; without doubt, for them is the Fire and(without doubt) they will be driven to it quickly .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:63: (I swear ) by Allah, We sent messengers to communities before you, but Satan adorned their deeds for them, so that he is their master today, and they will have a painful punishment.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:64: And We have not sent down to youthe Scripture but that you may clarify for them what they have differed over, and as a guidance and a mercy for people who believe.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:65: And Allah has sent down, from the sky, water with which He revived the earth after it was lifeless; indeed, in this is a sign for people who hear.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:66: And indeed, there is a lesson for youin livestock: We give you to drinkof what is in their bellies—from between filth and blood—pure milk, palatable to the drinkers.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:67: And from the products of date-palms and grapevines you make an intoxicating beverage and good food. Surely, in that is a sign for people who reason.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:68: And yourLord revealed to the bee: “Take for yourselfhomes of the mountains, and of the trees and of whatever they trellis,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:69: then eat of all products and go along the ways of your Lord, made smooth”. From their bellies comes out a drink of diverse colors, wherein is a cure for mankind. Surely, in that is a sign for people who reflect.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:70: And Allah created you, then He takes you(at death) . Yet among you is the one who is turned back to the most abject age, so that he no longer knows anything after having acquired knowledge; indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:71: And Allah has favored some of you over others in provision, yet those who were favored do not give their provision to those whom they rightfully possess, to the extent of making them equal partners in it. Do they then repudiatethe blessing of Allah?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:72: And Allah has set up for you spouses from among yourselves, and has assigned for you from your spouses, children and grandchildren, and has provided you with good things. Yet is it in falsehood that theybelieve, while it is the blessing of Allah that they deny?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:73: And yet they worship apart from Allah what possesses no provisions for them in the heavens or the earth, nor are they capable(of doing anything) .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:74: So donot set forth any parables for Allah; indeed, Allah knows and you know not.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:75: Allah set forth a parable: an owned bondman who has no power over anything, and(on the other hand) someone to whom Wehave given goodly provision from which he gives, secretly and openly. Can they be equal? All praise be to Allah; rather, most of them know not.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:76: And Allah set forth a parable of two men: one of them a mute who has no power over anything, and he is wholly dependent upon his patron; wherever he directs him, he achieves nothing good. Can he be equal to one who commands to justice and is on a straight path?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:77: And to Allah belongs the hidden realm of the heavens and the earth, and the matter of the Hour is only as the twinkling of the eye or even nearer; indeed, Allah is Powerful over everything.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:78: And Allah brought youout of your mothers’ bellies not knowing anything, and He assigned for you hearing and sight(s) and burning hearts, that you may give thanks.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:79: Have they not seenthe birds subjected in the midst of the sky? None holds them up except Allah. Surely, in that are signs for people who believe.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:80: And Allah has made for you, of your houses,(places of) rest and has assigned for you out of the skins of livestock(portable) homes which you find light on the day you travel and on the day you encamp and, from their wool and fur and hair, furnishings and an enjoyment for a while.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:81: And Allah has made for you shades out of what He created, and has made for you shelters of the mountains, and has made for you garments to protect you from the heat and garments to protect you from your violence; thus He completes His blessings upon you, that you may submit.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:82: So if theyturn away, then certainly youronly duty is evident proclamation.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:83: They recognize Allah’s blessing then they deny it, as most of them are the deniers.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:84: And on the day when We raise up a witness from every community —then those who denied are not permitted, nor are they allowed to make amends.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:85: And when those who did injustice see the punishment,(they will realize that) never shall it be lightened for them, nor shall they be given respite.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:86: And when the ones who associated(others with God) see their associates, they will say, “Our Lord, these are our associates whom we used to call upon apart from You.” So they castto them the statement, “Very truly, you are liars.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:87: And they cast forth to Allah, on that day,(their) submissiveness, and whatever they used to fabricate strayed away from them.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:88: Those who denied and barred from the way of Allah—Weadded punishment to their punishment on account of the corruption they used to cause.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:89: And on a day when We raise in every community a witness against them from among them, and We broughtyouas a witness against these. For We have bestowed upon you the Scripture from on high, as an explanation of everything and guidance and mercy and glad tidings for the Muslims.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:90: Indeed, Allah commands to justice and excelling in doing good and bringing(charity) to the relative, and He forbids obscenity and what is deplorable and oppression. He admonishes you, that you may remind yourselves .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:91: And fulfillAllah’s covenant when you make a covenant, and do not violate your oaths after ratifying them, for surely you have made Allah your guarantor; indeed, Allah knows what you do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:92: And donot be like she who unravels her yarn, breaking it into pieces after she has spun it strongly, by using your oaths as a means of deception among you because one community is more prosperous than another community. Indeed, Allah is testing you thereby, and He will most surely clarify to you on the Day of Resurrection whatever you used to differ over.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:93: And had Allah willed, He would have made you one community, but He leads astray whom He wills, and He guides whom He wills, and you will most surely be asked about what you used to do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:94: And do not use your oaths as a means of deception among you, lest a foot slip after being firm and you taste misery for barring(others) from the way of Allah, and for you there will be a great punishment.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:95: And donot purchase, in exchange for Allah’s covenant, a small price; indeed, what is with Allah is better for you, if you only knew.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:96: What you have runs out, but what is with Allah remains. And We will most surely repaythose who were patient their reward in accordance with the best of what they used to do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:97: Whoever has acted righteously, whether male or female, while being a believer—We will most surely grant him a good life, and We will most surely repay themtheir reward in accordance with the best of what they used to do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:98: So when yourecite the Recitalseek refuge with Allah from Satan, the outcast.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:99: Indeed, he has no authority over those who have attained faith and in their Lord they place their trust.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:100: Indeed, his authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who through him associate(others with God) .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:101: Yet whenever We substitute a sign in place of another sign—and Allahknows better what He bestows from on high —they say, “Indeed, you are nothing but a fabricator.” Rather, most of them do not know.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:102: Say, The Holy Spirit has bestowed it from on high from yourLord, with the truth, in order to strengthen those who have attained faith, and as guidance and glad tidings for Muslims.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:103: And most surely, We know that they say, “Indeed, it is a human being who is teaching him.” But the tongue of the one they allude to is foreign, while this is an evident Arabic tongue.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:104: Indeed, those who do not believe in Allah’s signs—Allah does not guide them, and for them is a painful punishment.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:105: Indeed, it is those who do not believe in Allah’s signs who fabricate falsehood, and those are the liars.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:106: Whoever has denied Allah after attaining faith—except for someone who was compelledwhile his heart rests securely in faith, but(rather) whoever(willingly) opens a chest to denial—upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:107: That is because they have sought the love of the Earlier Life over the Hereafter, and because Allah does not guide the denying people.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:108: Those are the ones whose hearts and hearing and sight(s) Allah has sealed, and those arethe oblivious ones.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:109: Without doubt, in the Hereafter they are the losers.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:110: Then surely yourLord—for those who emigrated after being persecuted, then strove and patiently persevered—indeed, your Lord thereafter is surely Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:111: On the day when every single self comes arguing for itself, and every soul is paid in full(for) what it has done, and they are not done any injustice.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:112: And Allah set forth a parable: a town that was safe(and) secure, its provision coming to it abundantly from everywhere. Yet it denied Allah’s blessings, so Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear on account of what they used to do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:113: And very truly, a messenger from among them had come to them, but they disbelieved him, so the punishment seized them while they were unjust.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:114: So eatof the lawful and good things Allah has provided for you, and be thankful for Allah’s blessing, if it is Him that you worship.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:115: Indeed, He has only forbidden youcarrion and blood and the flesh of swine and anything consecrated to other than Allah; but if anyone is compelled by necessity without being deliberate or transgressing, then Allah is indeed Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:116: And do not say lies concerning that which your tongues describe: “This is lawful and this is unlawful,” in order to fabricate lies and attribute them to Allah; indeed, those who fabricate lies and attribute them to Allah do not succeed.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:117: A brief enjoyment, then for them is a painful punishment.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:118: And for the ones who Judaized We have prohibited what We related to youbefore, and in no way did We do them any injustice, but to themselves they used to do injustice.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:119: But indeed yourLord, towards those who did evil in ignorance and then repented afterwards and reformed—indeed, yourLord thereafter is surely Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:120: Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devout towards Allah, turning away from all that is false, for never was he of the polytheists.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:121: (He was) thankful for His blessings. He elected him and guided him to a straight path.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:122: And Webrought him goodness in the Earlier(Life) , and in the Hereafter he is surely of the righteous.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:123: Then We revealed to you: “Followthe creed of Abraham, who turned away from all that is false, for never was he of the polytheists.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:124: Indeed, the Sabbath was ordained upon those who differed over it. And most surely, yourLord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection regarding whatever they used to differ over.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:125: Callto the way of your Lord with wisdom and good admonition, and debate with them by that which is better. Indeed, it is your Lord Who knows better of those who stray from His way, and it is He Who knows better of those who are guided.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:126: And if youpunish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished. But if you resort to patience, it is surely better for the patient ones.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:127: So be patient, for your patience is solely from Allah. And do not grieve over them and do not be distressed because of what they scheme.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.16:128: Indeed, Allah is with those who are mindful(of Him) and those who excel in doing good.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:1: Highly Exalted is the One Who took His servant on a journey by night from the Inviolable Mosqueto the Farthest Mosque, whose precincts Wehave blessed, in order to show him of Our signs; indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:2: And We brought Moses the Scripture and made it guidance for the Children of Israel: “Take none for trustee other than Me,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:3: (O) offspring of those We carried with Noah; indeed, he was a constantly thankful servant.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:4: And We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Scripture: “You will most surely corrupt in the land twice, and you will most surely rise to a great height.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:5: Then when the promise of the first of the two times came true, We sent against youservants of Ours possessing intense force, and they ransacked the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:6: Then We gave youback your turn against them and supplied you with wealth and offspring and made you more numerous.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:7: If you excel in doing good, you excel in doing good to your own benefit; and if you do evil, you do so against yourselves. Then when the promise of the second time comes true, they will defileyour faces, and they will enter the Mosque as they entered it the first time, and they will utterly destroy all that falls into their power.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:8: Hopefully yourLord will have mercy on you. But if you revert, Wewill revert. And We have made Hell a prison for the deniers.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:9: Indeed, this Recitalguides to what is most upright and gives glad tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that for them there is a supreme reward,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:10: and that those who do not believe in the Hereafter—We have prepared for them a painful punishment.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:11: And man calls for evil as he calls for good, and man has always been very hasty.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:12: And We have made the night and the day as two signs, then We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day as an eye-opener, that youmay seek grace from your Lordand that you may learn the number of years and the calculation; and everything have We explained in detail.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:13: And for every person We have attached his augury to his neck, and on the Day of Resurrection We will bring out for him a record which he will find spread open .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:14: “Reciteyour record; today your own self is sufficient as a reckoner.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:15: Whoever is guided—he is only guided to his own benefit, while whoever goes astray—he goes astray to his own detriment. And no bearer of burden carries the burden of another, for never do We punish until We have sent a messenger.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:16: And when We want to annihilate a town We command its affluent ones(to be righteous) , yet they defiantly disobey(Our commands) in it, so it deserves the decree and We annihilate it completely.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:17: And how many generations have We annihilated after Noah? Thus sufficient is your Lordas All-Aware, All-Seeing of the misdeeds of His servants.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:18: Whoever has been wanting the hasty(life of this world) —We hasten for him therein whatever We will to whomever We desire. Then We assignedfor him Hell where he roasts, condemned, defeated.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:19: But whoever wanted the Hereafter and, as a believer, pursued it as it should be pursued, those—their pursuit has always been thanked.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:20: To all—these and these(as well) —We extend from the gifts of yourLord, for the gifts of your Lord have never been restricted.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:21: Lookat how We have favored some of them over others, yet the Hereafter is more superior in degrees(of rank) and more superior in preference.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:22: Donot set up another god with Allah, lest you remain condemned,damned.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:23: And yourLord has decreed that youshall worship none but Him, and(He has decreed) excelling in doing good to both parents. If either of them or both of them reach old age with you, then do not say to them “Fie” nor scold them, but speak to them using noble words.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:24: And lower to them the wingof humility, out of mercy, and say, “My Lord, have mercy on both of them as they raised me when I was a child.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:25: YourLord knows better what is within yourselves. If you are righteous—indeed, He has always been Oft-Forgiving to the ones who often turn(to Him) .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:26: And givethe relative his rights, and the destituteand the traveler in need, and do not squander wastefully.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:27: Indeed, the squanderers have always been brethren of the Satans, for Satan has always been a staunch denier of his Lord.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:28: But if youdisregard them, seeking mercywhich you expect from your Lord, then speak to them using gentle words.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:29: And do not keep your hand tied to your necknor spread it out fully, lest you end up blamed, regretful.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:30: Indeed, your Lord extends provision for whomever He wills and He restrains(it) ; indeed, He has always been All-Aware, All-Seeing of His servants.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:31: And donot kill your children for fear of poverty; We provide for them and for you. Indeed, killing them has always been a grave offense.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:32: And donot come near fornication; indeed, it is an obscenity and an evil way.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:33: And donot kill the self which Allah has made inviolable, except in the course of justice. And if someone is killed unjustly, We have given authority to his kinsman who seeks retribution, but he should not be excessivein killing; indeed, he is bound to be aided.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:34: And donot come near the orphan’s wealth except with that which is better(for him) , until he has attained his full strength. And fulfill every covenant; indeed, the covenant has always been a responsibility.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:35: And givefull measure when you measure, and weigh with accurate scales; that is fair and the best determination.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:36: And donot follow what you have no knowledge of; indeed, the hearing and the sight and the burning heart—all of those—(one) is bound to be questioned about.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:37: And donot walk merrily on earth; youwill surely not pierce the earth, nor will you match the mountains in height.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:38: All of that—its evil has always been disliked by your Lord.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:39: That is some of the wisdom yourLord has revealed to you. And do not set up with Allah another god, lest you be thrown in Hell, blamed, banished.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:40: Has yourLord favored you with sons and taken for Himself from the angels females? Youare certainly saying a greatsaying.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:41: And very truly, We have explained in this Recitalin various ways, that they may constantly remember , but it only adds to their aversion.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:42: Say, “If there were other gods with Him as they say, they would have sought a way to the Possessor of the Throne.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:43: Highly Exalted is He. He is Most High, far above what they say.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:44: Exalting Him are the seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them. And there is not a thing that does not exalt Him with praise, but youdo not comprehend their exaltation. Indeed, He has always been Forbearing, Oft-Forgiving.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:45: And when yourecite the Recital, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter an invisible barrier.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:46: And We have placed veils over their hearts preventing them from comprehending it, and heaviness in their ears. And when you mention your Lordalone in the Recital, they turn their backs in aversion.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:47: We know better what(intention) it is that they listen with as they listen to you and as they secretly converse, as the unjust say, “Youare following nothing but a man bewitched.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:48: Lookat how they have set forth parables for youand gone astray, so they cannot find a way.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:49: And they said, “Can it be thatwhen we have become bones and fragments—can it be that we will really be resurrected as a new creation?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:50: Say,“ Becomerocks or iron
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:51: or any sort of creation which is greatly admired in yourchests.” Then they will say, “Who will restore us?” Say, “The One Who originated youthe first time.” Then they will nod their heads at youand say, “When will it be?” Say, “Hopefully, it will be soon,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:52: on the day when He calls you, then you respond with His praise and you think that you stayed only a little.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:53: And tellMy servants to say what is better. Indeed, Satan spurs(discord) between them; indeed, Satan has always been, to man, an evident enemy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:54: YourLord knows better about you. If He wills, He bestows mercy on you; and if He wills, He punishes you. Thus We never sent youas a trustee over them.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:55: And yourLord knows better about whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And Wehave most surely favored some prophets over others, and to David We gave a Book.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:56: Say, “Call upon those you claimed apart from Him. But they have no power to lift off harm from you, nor can they change it.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:57: Those whom they call upon are themselves seeking means of access to their Lord—whichever of them will be nearer—and hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment; indeed, the punishment of your Lord has always been dreaded.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:58: So there is no town but We are to annihilate it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment; this has been inscribed in the Scripture.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:59: And nothing prevented Us from sending(miraculous) signs except that the ancients disbelieved in them. So We gave Thamûdthe she-camel as an eye-opener, but they mistreated it. For We never send signs except to frighten(people of destruction) .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:60: And recall when We said to youthat your Lordhas encompassed mankind. And We did not make the vision We showed you except as a means of trial for mankind, and(recall) the tree which is cursed in the Recital. And We frighten them, but that increases them in nothing but supreme transgression.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:61: And recall when We said to the angels, “Prostrate to Adam,” so they prostrated—but not Iblis. He said, “Shall I prostrate down to someone You created of clay?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:62: He said, “Do You see this one whom You have honored more than me? If You reprieve me until the Day of Resurrection, I will most surely bridle his offspring, except for a few.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:63: He said, “Go! Whoever of them follows you—then indeed, Hell is yourrepayment, an ample repayment.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:64: And entice whomever of them youcan with your voice, and rally against them your cavalry and your infantry, and share with them in wealth and children, and promise them.” But Satan promises them nothing but a deception.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:65: “You surely have no authority over My servants.” And sufficient is your Lord as a trustee.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:66: YourLord is the One Who propels for you the ships at sea, that you may seek of His grace; indeed, to you He has always been Merciful.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:67: And when harm touches youat sea,(all) those you call upon become lost except for Him. But when He deliveredyou to the shore, you disregarded(Him) ; thus man has always been a staunch denier.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:68: Are youconfident that He will not cause a side of the shore to collapsebeneath you or unleash a tornado against you, and then you find no trustee?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:69: Or are youconfident that He will not return youto it once again and unleash a hurricane of wind against you anddrown you for your denial, and then you find no attending followers against Us?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:70: Yet very truly We have honored the Children of Adam and carried them on land and sea and provided them with good things and greatly favored them over many of those We have created.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:71: On the day when We call every group of people by their leader, then whoever is given his recordin his right hand—those will read their record, and they will not be dealt with unjustly by as much as the hair upon a date-stone.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:72: But whoever is blind in this(life) —he will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray from the way.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:73: And they almost lured youaway from what We have revealed to you so that you would fabricate something else in Our name, and in that case they would have taken you for a close friend.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:74: Had We not given youstability, you were about to incline towards them a little.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:75: Then We would have made youtaste double in life and double at death, then you would have found for yourself no supporter against Us.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:76: They almost provoked youso as to evict you from the land, and in that case they would not have lasted after you except briefly;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:77: such has been Our rule with the messengers We have sent before you, and you never find any change in Our rule.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:78: Establishthe prayer at the decline of the sun until the dusk of the night, as well as the Recitationat dawn; indeed, Recitation at dawn has always been witnessed.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:79: And keep vigil with it during parts of the night as an extra(deed) ; hopefully yourLord will raise you to a laudable position.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:80: And say, “My Lord, let me enter through an entry of truth and let me exit through an exit of truth and grant me from You a supporting manifestation.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:81: And say, “Truth has come while falsehood has withered away; indeed, falsehood is bound to wither away.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:82: And We bestow from on high of the Recitalthat which is a healing and a mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the unjust except in loss.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:83: And when We bless man, he disregards(Us) and distances himself . But when evil touches him, he staunchly despairs.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:84: Say, “Each does according to his disposition, but yourLord knows better of the one who is more guided to the way.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:85: And they ask youabout the Spirit; say, “The Spirit is by the command of my Lord, and youwere not given of knowledge but little.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:86: And if We will, we can surely take away what We have revealed to you, then you would find for yourself no trustee against Us—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:87: except through a mercy from your Lord; indeed, His grace upon you has been supreme.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:88: Say, “Most surely, if all humans and all unseen beingswere to come together to bring forth the like of this Recital, they could never bring forth the like of it, even if they backed up one another.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:89: And most surely, We have diversified for mankind in this Recitalevery kind of parable, but most of mankind refused anything but constant denial.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:90: And they said, “We will not believe in youuntil you make a spring gush forth from the ground for us;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:91: or possess a garden of palms and vines, then cause rivers to gush forth, pouring through them;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:92: or make the sky fall on us in pieces, as you claimed; or bring Allah and the angels before us;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:93: or possess a house of gold; or ascend into the sky. Even then, we will not believe in your ascension until you bestowupon us from on high a scripture that we can read.” Say, “Highly Exalted is my Lord. Have I been anything except a human messenger?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:94: And what prevented mankind from believing when guidance came to them, except that they said, “Did Allah send a human messenger?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:95: Say , “If there were angels on earth walking around in peace, We would have bestowed upon them from heaven an angel messenger.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:96: Say, “Allah is an adequate witness between you and me; indeed, He has always been All-Aware, All-Seeing of His servants.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:97: And whomever Allah guides is the guided one, and whomever He leads astray—for themyou will find no guardians apart from Him, and We will herd them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind and dumb and deaf; their shelter is Hell; whenever it abates, We intensify the blaze for them.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:98: That is their repayment for having denied Our signs and for having said, “Can it be thatwhen we have become bones and fragments—can it be that we will really be resurrected as a new creation?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:99: Have they not seen that Allah, Who created the heavens and the earth, is Able to create the likes of them? And He has assigned for them a term in which there is no doubt. But the unjust refused anything but constant denial.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:100: Say, “If youwere to possess the treasuries of my Lord’s mercy, you would withhold them for fear of spending(them) .” And man has always been stingy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:101: And very truly We gave Moses nine evident signs, so ask the Children of Israel about when he went to them, then Pharaoh said to him, “Indeed, I think that you, O Moses, are bewitched.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:102: He said, “Youhave most surely knownthat nonesent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth,(as) insights. And indeed I think that you, O Pharaoh, are doomed to demise.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:103: So he wanted to provoke them to leave the land, but We drowned him and those with him, all together.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:104: And after him, We said to the Children of Israel, “Settle in the land; yet when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth in a mixed multitude.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:105: And with the truth We sent it down, and with the truth it descended. Thus We have not sent you but as a bearer of glad tidings and as a warner.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:106: And a Recitalwhich We apportioned, that youmay recite it to mankind leisurely. And We surely bestowed it from on high.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:107: Say, “Believe in it or do not believe.” Indeed, those who were brought knowledge before it—when it is recited to them, they fall to their chins, prostrating.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:108: And they say, “Highly Exalted is our Lord. The promise of our Lord is sure to be fulfilled.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:109: And they fall to their chins weeping, and it adds to their humility.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:110: Say, “Call upon Allah or call upon the All-Merciful; whichever you call upon, to Him belong the most beautiful names.” And be neither loud in your prayer nor silent in it, but follow a way in between.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.17:111: And say, “All praise be to Allah, Who has not taken any offspring(for Himself) , nor has He ever had an associate in the dominion, nor has He ever had an ally out of humbleness. And glorify Him constantly.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:1: All praise be to Allah, Who sent down the Scripture upon His servant and has not made therein any crookedness;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:2: most upright, to warn of a severe chastisement from Himself, and(to) give glad tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that for them is an excellent reward,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:4: and(to) warn those who have said, “Allah has taken(for Himself) offspring.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:5: They have no knowledge of it, nor did their forefathers; massive is the word that comes out of their mouths! They say nothing but a lie!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:6: So perhaps youwould decimate yourself, sorrowing after them, if they do not believe in this discourse.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:7: Indeed, We have made whatever is on earth as an ornament for it, to test them as to which of them excels in work.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:8: And indeed, We will turn what is on it into barren soil.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:9: Or did youthink that the fellows of the cave and the Inscriptionwere among Our signs a wonder?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:10: Recall when the young men took shelter in the cave, then said, “Our Lord, bring us mercy from Yourself and furnish us with prudence in our affair.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:11: So We drew(a seal) upon their ears in the cave for a number of years.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:12: Then We resurrected them to know which of the two parties could better enumerate the length of their stay.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:13: We relate to youtheir story in truth; they are indeed young men who believed in their Lord and We increased them in guidance.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:14: And We strengthened their hearts when they stood up and said, “Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth; we will never call upon any god apart from Him; most surely then we would have spoken untruthfully.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:15: These, our people, have taken for themselves gods apart from Him. If only they would come forth with a clear manifestation of them. So who is more unjust than one who fabricated lies against Allah?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:16: Now that youhave withdrawn from them and from whatever they worship but Allah, take shelter in the cave, and your Lord will unfold His mercy for you and will set your affair towards ease.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:17: And youseethe sun when it rises, veering away from their cave towards the right, and when it sets, moving away from them to the left as they lie in a hollow therein; that is of Allah’s signs. Whomever Allah guides is the(truly) guided one, but whomever He leads astray—for him youwill find no guiding guardian.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:18: And youthink them awake, although they are asleep. And We turn them over to the right and to the left, with their dog stretching its paws across the threshold. Had you looked at them, you would surely have turned away from them in flight and been filled with fear of them.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:19: And thus We made them rise again so that they may ask one another. A speaker among them said, “How long have youstayed?” They said, “We have stayed a day or part of a day.” They said, “YourLord knows better how long you have stayed. So send one of you to the city with this silver(coin) of yours and let him look for whichever of them has the purest food and let him bring you some provision thereof. And let him go with discretion so that no one becomes aware of you.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:20: If they prevail over you, they will surely either stone you or force you back into their creed, and then you would never succeed, ever.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:21: And thus We caused them to be discovered, that theywould know that the promise of Allahis true and that of the Hour there is no doubt. As they were disagreeing with each other about their affair, they said, “Build over them a structure.” Their Lord knows better about them. Those who prevailed over their affairsaid, “We will set up over them a mosque.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:22: Some will say, “Three, their fourth being their dog.” And some will say, “Five, their sixth being their dog,” —guessing at the unknown. And some will say, “Seven, and their eighth being their dog.” Say, “My Lord knows better of their exact number”. None knows(the reality about) them except a few. So enternot into controversies concerning them except on a matter that is clear, and do not consult any of themabout them.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:23: And never say about anything, “I will do that tomorrow”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:24: without(saying) , “God willing.” And remember your Lord if you forget(to say it) and say, “Hopefully my Lord will guide me to something nearer to prudence than this.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:25: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years, adding nine.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:26: Say, “Allah knows better how long they remained; to Him belongs the hidden realm of the heavens and the earth. How clearly He sees and how finely He hears! They have no guardian apart from Him, and He does not associateanyone in His judgment.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:27: And readwhat was revealed to you from the Scripture of your Lord; none can change His words, and you will find no refuge apart from Him.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:28: And keepyourself patient in the company of those who pray to their Lord morning and evening, seeking His Countenance, and do not turn your eyes away from them, seeking the adornment of the Earlier Life, and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembranceso that he has followed his own whim and his affairs have become confused.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:29: And say, “Truth comes from your Lord. So whoever wills—let him believe, and whoever wills—let him disbelieve”. We have indeed prepared for the unjust a fire whose curtains have hemmed them in, and when they cry for relief, they are relieved with water like molten brass which scalds the faces. What a miserable drink, and what a bad place of rest!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:30: Indeed, those who have attained faith and have done righteous deeds…—indeed, We do not waste the reward of whoever excels in work.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:31: For those, there are the Gardens of Eden,rivers flowing beneath them. In it, they areadorned with bracelets of gold and wear green garments of silk and brocade, reclining therein on couches. What a wonderful recompense, and what an excellent place of rest!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:32: And setforth for them a parable of two men. To one of them We gave two gardens of grapevines, and We bordered them with palm-trees and We placed between them vegetation.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:33: Each of the two gardens brought forth its crops in full and failed not in the least therein, and We caused a river to burst forth throughout them.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:34: And thus he had riches, so he said to his fellow as he conversed with him, “I am wealthier than you and greater in manpower.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:35: And he entered his garden while unjust to himself. He said, “I do not think that this will ever perish,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:36: and I do not think that the Hour is ever coming. And even if I am taken back to my Lord, I will most surely find something better than it as a destination.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:37: His fellow said to him as he conversed with him, “Have you denied the One Who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then formed you as a man?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:38: But as for me, He is Allah, my Lord, and I never associate anyone with my Lord.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:39: Now, if only when you had entered your garden you had said, ‘As Allah wills; there is no power except through Allah,’ although you see me inferior to you in wealth and children.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:40: Hopefully my Lord will give me better than your garden and send upon it thunderbolts from the sky so that it becomes slippery soil,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:41: or its water sinks into the ground so that you become unable to draw it.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:42: And ruin closed in on his riches and he began wringing his hands over what he had spent therein, as it lay fallen upon its trellises, saying, “I wish I had never associated anyone with my Lord.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:43: And he had no battalion to support him apart from Allah, and he was unable to help himself.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:44: In that situation, protection belongs to Allah, the Truth; He is better in rewarding and better in requiting.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:45: And setforth for them a parable for the Earlier Life:(it is) like water that We sent down from the sky, then the plants of the earth were mixed with it, so it became debris scattered by the wind . And Allahhas always had absolute power over everything.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:46: Wealth and children are the adornments of the Earlier Life, while abiding deeds of righteousness are more rewardable by yourLord and worthier of being hoped for.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:47: And on the day when We set the mountains in motionand yousee the earth emerging; and We herdedthem together and left none of them behind.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:48: And they were presented, lining up before yourLord. “Very truly, youhave come to Us as We created you the first time. No indeed, you claimed We would never set an appointment for you.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:49: And the recordwas placed, and youseethe criminals fearful of whatever is in it, and they say, “Woe to us! What is with this record that leaves nothing, small or big, but it has enumerated it?” And they foundwhatever they had done present(before them) , for yourLord is never unjust to anyone.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:50: And recall when We said to the angels, “Prostrate to Adam.” So they prostrated—but not Iblis. He was one of the unseen beings, so he defied the command of his Lord. Will you take him and his offspring as guardians apart from Me when they are an enemy to you? What a miserable bargain for the unjust!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:51: I did not make them witnessthe creation of the heavens and the earth, nor their own creation, and never was I to takethe misguiding people for assistants.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:52: And on the day when He says , “Call on My associates whom you have claimed.” So they calledon them, but they did not respond to them. And Weplaced between them a barrier.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:53: Then the criminals saw the Fire, so they realized that they were bound to tumble into it and they found no escape from it.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:54: And We have elaborated in this Recitalfor mankind every kind of parable, but man has always been the most argumentative being.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:55: And what prevented mankind from attaining faith when guidance came to them and from seeking their Lord’s forgiveness? Unless they are waiting for the rule of(God regarding) the ancients to come upon them or to have the punishment come upon themin many types .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:56: And We do not send emissaries except as bearers of glad tidings and as forewarners. But those who have denied argue using falsehood in order to defeat the truth thereby, and they tookMy signs and what they were warned of for a joke.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:57: And who is more unjust than the one who was reminded of his Lord’s signs then disregarded them and forgot what his hands had put forth? Indeed, We have placed veils over their hearts, preventing them from comprehending it, and heaviness in their ears. And if you call them to guidance they will not be guided, ever.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:58: And yourLord is the Forgiver, the Possessor of mercy. Were He to call them to account for what they have earned, He would hasten the punishment for them. Rather, for them is an appointment from which they will find no escape.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:59: And those towns—We annihilated them when they committed injustices, and We set an appointment fortheir moment of annihilation .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:60: And recall when Moses said to his young assistant, “I will not give up until I reach the junction of the two seas, even if it takes me eons.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:61: So when they reached the junction between them, they forgot about their fish, and so it found its way into the sea, slipping away.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:62: Then when they went further, he said to his young assistant, “Bring us our lunch; very truly, we have encountered in our travel much fatigue.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:63: He said, “Did you see when we rested by the rock? I forgot about the fish, and none except Satan made me forget it. And it found its way to the sea, wondrously.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:64: He said, “That is what we were looking for.” And so they turned back, retracing their footsteps.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:65: Then they came upon a servant of Our servants whom We had given mercy from Us and whom We had taught knowledge from Our Own.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:66: Moses said to him, “May I follow you so that you may teach me some of the prudence you were taught?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:67: He said, “Indeed, youwill not be able to endure patiently with me.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:68: And how can you endure patiently what you have not encompassed with knowledge?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:69: He said, “You will find me patient, Allah willing, and I will not disobey you in any command of yours.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:70: He said, “So if youfollow me, then do not askme about anything until I bring about a mention of it to you.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:71: So they both set out until, when they had boarded the ark, he holed it. He said, “Did you hole it so as to drown its people? You have done something awful.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:72: He said, “Did I not tell you that you would not be able to endure patiently with me?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:73: He said, “Do not rebuke me for forgetting, and do not make my matters difficult.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:74: Then they both set out until, as soon as they encountered a boy, he killed him. He said, “Did you kill a sinless selfwhich killed no one? Most surely, you have done something dreadful.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:75: He said, “Did I not tell you that you would not be able to endure patiently with me?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:76: He said, “If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep company with me; certainly, by then you would have had enough of an excuse from me.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:77: So they both set out until, when they reached the people of a town, they asked them for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. There they found a wall tending to collapse, so he repaired it. He said, “If you wanted, you could have charged a reward for it.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:78: He said, “This is the parting between you and me. I will tell you the interpretation of what you were unable to endure patiently.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:79: As for the ark, it belonged to some destitute people working at sea, so I wanted to make it defective, for there was a king coming after them, seizing every ark by force.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:80: And as for the boy, his parents were believers and we feared he would overwhelm them with transgression and denial.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:81: So we wanted their Lord to replace him with someone of better purity and nearer to mercy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:82: And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphaned boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure that belonged to them, and their father was a righteous man, so your Lord desired that they attain their full strength and(then) extract their treasure—a mercy from your Lord. And I never did it of my own accord. This is the interpretation of what you were unable to endure patiently.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:83: And they ask youabout Zul-Qarnayn. Say, “I will read for you an account of him as a reminder.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:84: Indeed, We empowered him in the land and brought him all kinds of means.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:85: So he pursued a certain course
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:86: until, when he had reached the setting of the sun, he found it setting in a murky spring, and found a people in its vicinity. We said, “O Zul-Qarnayn, you may either punish or else treat them kindly.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:87: He said, “As for the one who has committed injustices, we will punish him, then he will be returned to his Lord and He will punish him with a dreadful punishment.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:88: But as for the one who has attained faith and has acted righteously, then for him is the excellent(reward) as repayment , and we will speak to him with ease regarding our command.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:90: until, when he reached the rising of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had provided no shelter from it.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:91: So it was. And surely We encompassed what he had with knowledge.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:93: until, when he reached the point separating the two barriers, he found beside them a people who could barely comprehend any word.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:94: They said, “O Zul-Qarnayn, Gog and Magog are corrupting the land, so can we make for you a tribute on condition that you build a barrier between us and them?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:95: He said, “What my Lord has empowered me with is better.(Just) assist me with(man) power, and I will set a barricade between youand them.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:96: Bring me blocks of iron.” Then when he had leveled up between the two cliffs, he said, “Blow.” And having turned it into a fire, he said, “Bring me tar to pour over it.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:97: So neither could they climb it, nor could they penetrate it.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:98: He said, “This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord comes true, He will turn it into a flat surface . And the promise of my Lord has always been true.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:99: And We leftthem surging upon one another on that day, and the Trumpet was blown and We gathered them together.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:100: And We displayed Hell to the deniers on that day in full display—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:101: those whose eyes were covered from My Reminder and were unable to hear.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:102: Did those who have denied think that they could take My servants for masters apart from Me? Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the hospitality of the deniers.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:103: Say, “Shall We inform youof the biggest losers regarding deeds?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:104: Those whose efforts in the Earlier Life have gone astray, while they assume that they are doing well.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:105: Those are the ones who denied the signs of their Lord and the meeting with Him, so their deeds were nullified, and on the Day of Resurrection We will consider them of no weight.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:106: That is their repayment—Hell—on account of their denial and their taking My signs and My messengers in mockery.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:107: Indeed, those who have attained faith and have done righteous deeds—the Gardens of Paradise have always been there for their hospitality,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:108: abiding therein, never seeking to leave it.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:109: Say, “If the sea were to become ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would run out before the words of my Lord ran out, even if We were to bring the like of it in replenishment.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.18:110: Say, “Indeed, I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your god is One God, so whoever expects to meet his Lord, let him do righteous work and never associate anyone in the worship of his Lord.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:2: A reminder of yourLord’s mercy towards His servant Zechariah,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:3: when he called out to his Lord a call in seclusion.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:4: He said, “My Lord, my bones have become feeble and my hair is aflame with gray, and never, in calling upon You my Lord, have I been wretched.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:5: And indeed, I am afraid of what my protégés will do when I am gone, for my wife has always been barren. So grant me from Yourself a guardian
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:6: to inherit from me and inherit from Jacob’s folk, and make him, my Lord, pleasing.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:7: “O Zechariah, indeed, We give you glad tidings of a boy whose name is John; We have never made anyone similar to himbefore.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:8: He said, “My Lord, how can I have a boy when my wife has always been barren and I have become decrepit with old age?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:9: He said, “Thus said your Lord, ‘It is easy for Me, and I have certainly created youbefore when you were nothing.’”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:10: He said, “My Lord, give me a sign.” He said, “Your sign is that you do not speak to people for three nights,(despite) being in perfect shape.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:11: So he came out to his people from the sanctuary and signaled to them to exalt(God) , morning and evening.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:12: “O John, hold on to the Scripture firmly,” and We gave him wise judgment in his youth
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:13: and tenderness from Us and purity, and he was mindful(of God) ,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:14: and was very kind to his parents, and he was never a disobedient coercer.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:15: And peace be upon him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he is resurrected alive.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:16: And rememberin the Scripture Mary, when she secluded herself from her family in an eastern location.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:17: And she took a cover for herself away from them, and We sent to her Our spirit, so He appeared to her as a human being in perfect shape.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:18: She said, “I seek refuge from you with the All-Merciful, if you are mindful(of God) .”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:19: He said, “I am only a messenger of your Lord to grant you a pure boy.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:20: She said, “How can I have a boy when no human being has touched me, nor have I ever been a harlot?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:21: He said, “Thus said your Lord, ‘It is easy for Me, and We will make him a sign for humanity and a mercy from Us, and it has been a matter already decreed.’”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:22: So she carried him and secluded herself with him in a remote place.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:23: Then the birth pangs compelled her to come to the trunk of the palm tree. She said, “If only I had died before this and been a thing forgotten, completely forgotten!”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:24: So he called her from beneath her : “Be not sad; your Lord has made a stream beneath you.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:25: And shake the trunk of the palm tree towards you—it will drop ripe datesupon you.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:26: “So eat and drink and let your eye be comforted, but if you see any human being, say, ‘I have vowed a fast to the All-Merciful, so I will not speak to any human today.’”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:27: Then she came to her people, carrying him. They said, “O Mary, you have done something terrible.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:28: O sister of Aaron, neither was your father an evil man, nor was your mother a harlot.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:29: So she pointed to him. They said, “How can we speak to an infant in the cradle?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:30: He said, “I am Allah’s servant. He has brought me the Scripture and has made me a prophet.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:31: And He has made me blessed wherever I may be and has enjoined upon me prayer and purifying charityso long as I live.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:32: And He has made me very kind to my mother and has not made me a wretched coercer.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:33: And peace be upon me the day I was born and the day I die and the day I get resurrected alive.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:34: That is Jesus, son of Mary—the word of truth about which they are skeptical.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:35: Never was it for Allah to have any offspring—Highly Exalted is He; whenever He decrees a matter, He only says to it, “Be,” and so it is.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:36: “And indeed, Allah is my Lord and yourLord, so worship Him; this is a straight path.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:37: But the parties differed among themselves, so woe to those who have denied from the spectacle of a great day.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:38: How well they shall hear and see on the day they come to Us! But the unjust are today in evident misguidance.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:39: And warnthem of the Day of Regret, when the matter has been concluded. Yet they are in oblivion, and they do not believe.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:40: Indeed, We—We alone—will inherit the earth and everyone on it, and to Us they are returned .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:41: And mentionin the Scripture Abraham; he was indeed an unwavering believer(and) a prophet.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:42: Recall when he said to his father, “O my father, why do you worship what can neither hear nor see nor avail you anything?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:43: O my father, most surely there has come to me of knowledge what has never come to you, so follow me and I will guide you to a straight path.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:44: O my father, do not worship Satan; indeed Satan has always been disobedient to the All-Merciful.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:45: O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the All-Merciful may touch you so that you would become an ally for Satan.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:46: He said, “Are you renouncing my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will certainly stone you, so leave me for a long while.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:47: He said, “Peace be upon you; I will ask my Lord to forgive you; indeed, He has always been gracious to me.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:48: And I shall withdraw from youand from what youcall upon apart from Allah, and I will call upon my Lord; hopefully, in calling upon my Lord, I shall never be wretched.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:49: So when he withdrew from them and what they worshiped apart from Allah, We granted him Isaac and Jacob, and each We made a prophet.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:50: And We granted them of Our mercy and gave them a high and true renown.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:51: And mentionin the Scripture Moses. He was indeed a sincere, chosen one , and he was a messenger(and) a prophet.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:52: And We called out to him from the right side of Mount Tûr, and brought him near in communion.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:53: And We granted him, of Our mercy, his brother Aaron as a prophet.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:54: And mention in the Scripture Ishmael; he was indeed true to his promise, and he was a messenger(and) a prophet.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:55: And he used to command his family to prayer and purifying charity, and with his Lord he was always rendered pleased.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:56: And mention in the Scripture Enoch; he was indeed an unwavering believer(and) a prophet.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:57: And We raised him to a high position.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:58: Those are the ones whom Allahblessed ofthe prophets from the offspring of Adam, and from those Wecarried with Noah, and from the offspring of Abraham and Israel, and from those We guided and selected. Whenever the signsof the All-Mercifulwere recited to them, they would fall down prostrating and weeping.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:59: Then they were succeeded by generations who wasted the prayers and followed desires, and thus they will encounter(the sequel of their) delusion—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:60: except for whoever repented and believed and acted righteously, for those shall enter the Garden and shall not be dealt with unjustly in any way—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:61: the Gardens of Eden which have been promised by the All-Merciful to His servants in the hidden realm; indeed, His promise has ever been coming true.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:62: Therein they hear no idle talk, but only peace. And therein they have their own provision, morning and evening.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:63: Such is the Garden(of Paradise) which We give as inheritance to whoever of Our servants who has been mindful(of God) .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:64: “And wedo not descend except by the command of yourLord; to Him belongs whatever is before us and whatever is behind us and whatever is between them, and your Lord has never been forgetful.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:65: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, so worship Him and persevere in worshiping Him. Do you know of anyone similar to Him?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:66: And man says, “Can it be that when I am dead,I willbe brought out alive?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:67: Does man not remember that We created him earlier when he was nothing?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:68: By yourLord, We will surely herd them and the devils, then We will surely bring them around Hell on their knees.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:69: Then out of every sect We will surely snatch those most defiant to the All-Merciful.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:70: Then(they will realize that) We surely know better of those who are most deserving to roast in it.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:71: But every single one of you is bound to approach it; this has been an unavoidable decree of your Lord.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:72: Then Wedeliver those who were mindful(of God) and leave the unjust in it on their knees.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:73: And when Our signsare read to them, evident, those who have denied say to those who have attained faith, “Which of the two groups is better in position and fairerin company?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:74: And how many a generation have We annihilated before them who surpassed them in riches and splendor?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:75: Say, “Whoever has been in utter misguidance, may the All-Merciful fully extend for him.” Until, when they see what they were promised—either punishment or the Hour—then they will know who was in a worse position and weaker as an army.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:76: And Allah increases in guidance those who seek guidance. And abiding deeds of righteousness are more rewardable by your Lord and better in return.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:77: Have youseen the one who denied Our signs and said, “I will most surely be given wealth and children”?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:78: Has he viewed the hidden realm, or has he taken with the All-Mercifula covenant?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:79: But no! We will write what he says and keep extending the agony for him exceedingly,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:80: and we will inherit from him whatever he says, and he will come to Us solitary.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:81: And they took, apart from Allah, other gods to be a source of might for them.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:82: But no! They will deny their worship of them and become opponents against them.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:83: Have younot seen that We have dispatched the devils against the deniers, exciting them with incitement?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:84: So do not hurry about them; indeed, We are only counting(down) for them precisely.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:85: On a day when We herd the ones who were mindful(of God) to the All-Mercifulas a delegation,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:86: and flock the criminals into Hell, thirsty,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:87: with no power of intercession—except for the one who had taken with the All-Merciful a covenant.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:88: And they said, “The All-Merciful has taken(for himself) offspring.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:89: Youhavecome up with something monstrous!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:90: The heavens almost rupture at it, and the earth splits and the mountains fall, crumbling:
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:91: that they have attributed a son to the All-Merciful!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:92: And in no way is it fitting for the All-Merciful to take(for Himself) a son.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:93: There is none in the heavens and the earth but is bound to come to the All-Merciful as a servant.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:94: He has enumerated them and counted them precisely.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:95: And each one of them is bound to come to Him on the Day of Resurrection solitary.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:96: Indeed, those who have attained faith and have done righteous deeds—the All-Merciful will give them love.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:97: So indeed, We have made it easy in yourtongue, that you may give glad tidings to the ones who were mindful(of God) and warn with it a hostile people.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.19:98: And how many a generation have We annihilated before them? Can you feel a single one of them or hear from them the slightest whisper?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:2: We have not sent down the Recitalupon youfor you to be wretched,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:3: but only as a reminding for one who fears.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:4: A bestowal from on high by the One Who created the earth and the highest heavens—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:5: the All-Merciful; on the Throne He settled.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:6: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the ground.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:7: And if youspeak aloud, indeed, He knows the secret and the most hidden.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:8: Allah—there is no god but He; to him belong the most beautiful names.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:9: And has the story of Moses reached you?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:10: When he saw a fire, so he said to his family, “Stay; I have noticed a fire; perhaps I can bring youa torch therefrom or find some guidance by the fire.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:11: So when he reached it, he was called, “O Moses.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:12: Indeed, I—I am your Lord. So take off your sandals; you are indeed in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:13: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:14: Indeed I—I alone—am Allah. There is no God but I, so worship Me and establish the prayer for My remembrance.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:15: The Hour is indeed coming—I almost hide it—so that every single self is paid for what it endeavors.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:16: So let not the one who denies it and has been following his own whim bar you from it, lest you fall(into doom) .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:17: And what is that in your right-hand, O Moses?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:18: He said, “This is my staff. I lean on it, and I beat down(leaves) for my sheep with it, and I have other uses for it.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:20: So he cast it, and thereupon it became a moving serpent.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.20:21: He said, “Pick it up and be not afraid; We will restore it to its original condition.
