Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.53:53: And He brought down the Ruined Cities
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.53:54: and covered them by that which He covered.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.53:55: So which of yourLord’s marvels do you enter into controversies about?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.53:56: This is a warning just like the first warnings.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.53:58: none apart from Allah can unveil it.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.53:59: Do youmarvel at this discourse,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.53:60: and laugh and do not weep,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.53:62: So prostrate yourselves to Allah and worship!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:1: The Hour has drawn near and the moon has ruptured.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:2: Yet whenever they see a miracle, they disregard(it) and say, “Continuous magic!”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:3: And they disbelieved and followed their whims. And every matter is bound to settle[1666]
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:4: And most surely there have come to them tidings containing a deterrent—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:5: profound wisdom, but warnings are of no avail.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:6: So turn awayfrom them. On the day when the Summoner summons to something terrible,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:7: with their sight(s) (subdued) in reverence they come out of the tombs like swarming locusts,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:8: scrambling towards the Summoner; the deniers say, “This is a hard day.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:9: The people of Noah disbelieved before them, so they disbelieved Our servant and said, “A madman!”, and he was rebuked.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:10: So he called upon his Lord, “I am overcome, so bestow help!”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:11: So We opened the gates of the sky with water pouring down,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:12: and We made the earth burst with springs, so the waters met for a matter already determined.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:13: And We carried him on a craft of planks and nails,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:14: sailing before Our eyes—a repayment for the one who had been denied.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:15: And most surely We have left it as a sign, so is there anyone to remind himself?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:16: So how were My punishment and My warnings!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:17: And most surely We have made the Recitaleasy for remembrance, so is there anyone to remind himself?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:18: ʻĀddisbelieved, so how were My punishment and My warnings!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:19: Indeed, We sent against them a screaming wind on a day of unrelenting misfortune,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:20: plucking people away as though they were trunks of uprooted palm trees.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:21: So how were My punishment and My warnings!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:22: And most surely We made the Recitaleasy for remembrance, so is there anyone to remind himself?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:24: and said, “Are we to follow a human being from among us? Indeed, we would then be astray and insane!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:25: Has the Reminder been cast to him out of all of us? Rather, he is a wicked sheer liar.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:26: They will knowtomorrow who the wicked sheer liar is.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:27: We are sending the she-camel as a means of trial for them, so watchthem and be patient.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:28: And informthem that the water is to be shared between them; each one should drink in turn.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:29: But they called their fellow, and he dared and hamstrung(it) .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:30: So how were My punishment and My warnings!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:31: Indeed, We sent against them a single Shout, and they ended up like a fence-maker’s dry sticks.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:32: And most surely We made the Recitaleasy for remembrance, so is there anyone to remind himself?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:33: The people of Lot disbelieved in the warnings.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:34: Indeed, We sent against them a shower of stones, except for Lot’s folk–We delivered them at dawn—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:35: a blessing from Us; thus We repay whoever gives thanks.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:36: And most surely hehad warned them of Our onslaught, but they entered into controversies about the warnings.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:37: And most surely they solicited of him his guests, so We obliterated their eyes— “So taste My punishment and My warnings.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:38: And most surely an abiding punishment came upon them in the morning—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:39: “So tasteMy punishment and My warnings.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:40: And most surely We made the Recitaleasy for remembrance, so is there anyone to remind himself?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:41: And most surely the warnings came to Pharaoh’s folk—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:42: they disbelieved all Our signs. So We seized them(with) the seizure of an Almighty, Invincible One.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:43: “Are yourdeniers better than all those? Or do you have immunity in the Books?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:44: Or do they say, “We, all together, will be victorious”?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:45: The multitude will be defeated, and they will turn their backs.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:46: Nay, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more disastrous and more bitter.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:47: Indeed, the criminals are in confusion and insanity.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:48: The day when they are dragged upon their faces into the Fire: “Taste the touch of Saqar.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:49: Indeed, We have created everything in due measure.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:50: And Our command is but once, like the twinkling of an eye.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:51: And most surely We have annihilated yourlikes, so is there anyone to remind himself?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:52: And everything they have done is in the Books—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:53: for everything, small or large, is written down.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:54: Indeed, the mindful(of God) are amidst Gardens and rivers,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.54:55: in a seat of truth, in the presence of an Invincible King.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:5: The sun and the moon move according to plan,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:6: and the plantsand the trees prostrate themselves.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:7: And the sky—He raised it and set up the balance,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:8: so donot exceed in the balance,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:9: but maintain the weights justly and do not fall short in the balance.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:10: And the earth—He set it up for living creatures;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:11: in it are fruits and sheathed palm trees,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:12: and grains in the blades, and fragrant plants.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:13: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:14: He created man from potter’s clay like pottery
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:15: and created the unseen beingfrom a smokeless flame of fire.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:16: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:17: Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:18: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:19: He merged the two waters, converging together;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:20: between them is a barrier which they do not overrun.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:21: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:22: From them come out pearls and corals.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:23: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:24: His are the running ships, whose sails are raised in the sea like banners.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:25: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:26: Everyone upon itis bound to perish,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:27: and all that remains is yourLord’s Countenance, the Possessor of majesty and nobility.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:28: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:29: Everyone in the heavens and the earth asks Him; every day He is bringing about a matter.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:30: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:31: We will attendto you, O two huge communities.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:32: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:33: O society of unseen beings and humans, if youcan penetrate the bounds of the heavens and the earth then go ahead and penetrate; you will never penetrate except with authority.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:34: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:35: Flares of fire, and brass , will be sent upon you, and you will not find help.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:36: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:37: And when the sky ruptures and becomes rose-colored like oil—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:38: so which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:39: On that day neither any human nor unseen beingis asked about his misdeeds.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:40: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:41: The criminals are recognized by their marks then taken by the forelocks and the feet.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:42: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:43: This is Hell in which the criminals disbelieve;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:44: they circulate between it and an intensely scalding water.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:45: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:46: But for whoever feared standing before his Lord there are two Gardens(in Paradise) .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:47: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:49: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:50: In them are two flowing springs.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:51: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:52: In them, of every kind of fruit there is apair.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:53: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:54: Reclining on furnishings lined with brocade, and the yield of the two Gardens are near at hand.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:55: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:56: In them are bashful maidens, untouched before by any human or unseen being.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:57: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:59: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:60: Is the repayment of kindness anything but kindness?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:61: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:62: And beneath them are two gardens.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:63: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:65: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:66: In them are two gushing springs.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:67: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:68: In them are fruits and date-palms and pomegranates.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:69: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:70: In them are good, beautiful ones.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:71: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:72: Spouses with lovely wide eyes, secluded in pavilions.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:73: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:74: Untouched before by any human or unseen being.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:75: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:76: Reclining on green cushions and exquisite carpets.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:77: So which of your Lord’s marvels do youdisbelieve in?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.55:78: Supremely Blessed be the Name of yourLord,the Possessor ofmajesty and nobility.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:2: no disbelief will there be about its befalling,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:4: When the earth is shaken violently,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:5: and mountains are crushed and crumbled
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:8: the fellows of the rightness; what of the fellows of the rightness!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:9: And the fellows of the ill-omened; what of the fellows of the ill-omened!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:11: those are the ones brought near(to God)
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:14: and a small band from the latecomers,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:16: leaning on them, facing one another.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:17: Serving them will be immortal youths
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:18: with glasses, and pitchers, and a cup from a flowing spring,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:19: causing them neither headache nor intoxication ,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:21: and meat of any bird they may desire.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:22: And(in it are) spouses with lovely wide eyes,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:24: as a repayment on account of what they used to do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:25: Therein they will hear no idle talk and no recrimination
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:27: And the fellows of the right—what of the fellows of the right?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:38: for the fellows of the right—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:40: and a throng from the latecomers.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:41: And the fellows of the left—what of the fellows of the left?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:42: Amid searing wind and scalding water
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:43: and a shadow of thick smoke,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:45: They had lived before that indulging in affluence,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:46: and they used to insist on great violation,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:47: and they used to say, “Can it be that when we have died and become dust and bones—can it be that we will really be resurrected?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:49: Say, “Indeed, the ancients and the latecomers
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:50: will be gathered for the appointment of a well-known day!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:51: Then indeed all of you, O misguided disbelievers,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:52: will certainly be eating from the trees of Zaqqum
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:53: and filling your bellies with it
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:54: and will be drinking on top of it scalding water,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:55: thus drinking as a thirst-mad camel drinks.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:56: That is their hospitality on the Day of Recompense.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:57: We have created you; if only you would believe!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:58: Have youseen what you ejaculate?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:59: Is it youwho create it or are We the Creators?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:60: We have decreed death among you, and We will not be outstripped
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:61: in replacing you with your likes and transforming you into what you do not know.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:62: And youhave certainly known the first formation; if only you would remind yourselves!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:63: Have youseen what you cultivate?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:64: Is it you who plant it or are We the Planters?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:65: If We will, We can turn it into rubble, then youwill lament,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:68: Have youseen the water you drink?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:69: Is it you who sent it down from the rainclouds or are We the Senders?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:70: If We will, We can make it salty. Will younot be thankful?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:71: Have you seen the fire you kindle?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:72: Is it you who produced the tree for it, or are We the Producers?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:73: We have made it a reminding and a comfort for the travelers.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:74: So highly exalt the Name of yourLord, the Great.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:75: I swear by the locations of the stars—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:76: and it is certainly a great oath if only youwere to know.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:77: It is indeed a Noble Recital
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:79: None touches it except the cleansed,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:80: a bestowal from on high by the Lord of all realms.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:81: Is it this discourse that youtake so lightly?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:82: And you render due thanks for being provided with it by disbelieving in it?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:83: So when ithas reached the throat,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:84: and you are at that moment looking on,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:85: and We are nearer to him than you are, but you do not see—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:86: why, if you are not to be held to account,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:87: do you not bring itback if you are truthful?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:88: Yet, if he is one of those brought near(to God) ,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:89: then serenity andfragrant plants and a Garden of Bliss.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:90: And if he is one of the fellows of the right,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:91: then, “Peace for you,” from the fellows of the right.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:92: But if he is one of the misguided disbelievers,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:93: then the welcome will be scalding water
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:95: Indeed, this is surely the truth of certitude.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.56:96: So highly exalt the Name of yourLord, the Great.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:1: Whatever is in the heavens and the earth has been highly exalting Allah, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:2: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He gives life and causes death, for He is All-Powerful over everything.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:3: He is the First and the Last and the Manifest and the Innermost, and He is All-Knowing of everything.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:4: It is He Who created the heavens and the earth in six daysthen settled over the Throne. He knows what penetrates the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends to it, for He is with youwherever you may be. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:5: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:6: He causes the night to penetrate the day and He causes the day to penetrate the night, and He is All-Knowing of what lies within the chests.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:7: Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and spend of that over which He has made you trustees, for those of you who have attained faith and spent—for them is a supreme reward.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:8: And what is the matter with youthat you do not believe in Allah when the Messenger calls you to believe in your Lord—when He has taken your pledge — if you are believers?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:9: It is He who bestows upon His servant evident signs from on highto bring youout of darkness(es) into light. And towards you Allah is truly Compassionate, Bestowing of mercy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:10: And why is it that youdo not spend in the way of Allah when to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth? Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and combated; those are higher in degrees(of rank) than those who spent afterwards and combated, yet to each Allah has promisedthe best(reward) , and Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:11: Who is it that will lend Allah a good loan, that He may multiply it for him, and for him is a noble reward?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:12: On the day when yousee the believing men and believing women with their light radiating ahead of them and to their right: “Glad tidings for you today: Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein; it is that which is the great triumph.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:13: On the day when the hypocritical men and hypocritical women say to those who believed, “Wait for us so that we may borrow from your light.” They were told: “Go back behind you and seek light.” Then a wall with a door was raised between them: within it is mercy and outside of it is punishment.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:14: Theycall to them, “Were we not with you?” They said, “Yes, but you tempted yourselves and waited and doubted and became deceived by fancies until the command of Allah arrived, and the deceiverdeceived you regarding Allah.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:15: So today no ransom is accepted from younor from those who have denied. The Fire is your shelter; it is your patron—and what a miserable destiny!”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:16: Is it not time for those who have attained faith: that their hearts should become reverent towards Allah’s Reminder and to that which came down of the truth, and not be like those who were given the Scripture previously, but for whom time became prolonged so that their hearts hardened, and many of them are defiantly disobedient?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:17: Know that Allah revives the earth after its death; We have made the signs evident for you, that you may reason.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:18: Indeed, charitable men and charitable women who have loaned Allah a good loan—it will be multiplied for them, and for them is a noble reward.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:19: And as for those who have attained faith in Allah and His messengers—those are the unwavering believers and the witnesseswho will come as witnesses with their Lord; for them is their reward and their light. But as for those who denied and rejected Our signs—those are the fellows of purgatory.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:20: Knowthat the Earlier Life is only a game and a distraction and an adornment and boasting among you and rivalry in wealth and children: like a rainfall producing plants that delighted the farmers, then it withers and you see it yellowing, then it becomes debris. But in the Hereafter is severe punishment and forgiveness from Allah and(His) good pleasure, for the Earlier Life is nothing but the enjoyment of deception.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:21: Race towards forgiveness from yourLord and a Garden(of Paradise) whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth—prepared for those who have attained faith in Allah and His messengers. That is Allah’s grace; He bestows it upon whomever He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great grace.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:22: No calamity occurs on earth or among yourselves but it is already written in a Recordbefore We make it— indeed, that is easy for Allah—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:23: so that youdo not grieve over what you have missed nor exult over what He has given you. And Allah does not love every self-admiring boaster—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:24: those who are miserly and command mankind to miserliness. And whoever turns away—indeed, it is Allah who is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:25: And We certainly sent Our messengers with evident proofs, and We sent down with them the Scripture and the Balance, that mankind may uphold justice. And We sent down iron in which there is intense force and benefits for humanity, and that Allah may know who supports Him and His messengers, though unseen. Indeed, Allah is All-Powerful, Almighty.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:26: And We certainly sent Noah and Abraham and established Prophethood and Scripture among their offspring, so some of them are rightly guided, while many of them are defiantly disobedient.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:27: Then We sent in their wake Our messengers and followed them with Jesus, son of Mary, and We gave him the Gospel and instilled in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy. But the monasticism which they invented was only to seek Allah’s good pleasure—We did not ordain it for them— yet they did not observe it with its due observance. So We gave those of them who attained faith their reward, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:28: O you who have attained faith, be mindful of Allah and believe in His Messenger: He shall(then) bring you a double share of His mercy and shall make for you a light by which you walk and shall forgive you, for Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.57:29: So that the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power whatsoever over Allah’s grace and that all grace is in Allah’s hand; He brings it to whomever He wills, for Allah is the Possessor of great grace.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:1: Allah has surely heard the statement of she who argues with youconcerning her spouse and complains to Allah, and Allah hears yourconversation; indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:2: Those of you who estrange their wives by equating them with their mothers—they are not their mothers; their mothers are only those who gave birth to them. And indeed, what they say is truly a deplorable thing to say and a blatant lie. But indeed, Allah is Pardoning, Oft-Forgiving.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:3: And those who estrange their wives by equating them with their mothers then go back on what they have said—a slave must be set free before they may touch one another. With this youare admonished, and Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:4: But whoever cannot find the means must fast for two consecutive months before they may touch one another, and if he is unable—then the feeding of sixty destitute people. This is to affirm yourfaith in Allah and His Messenger, and these are the limits of Allah. And for the deniers is a painful punishment.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:5: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger have been subdued as those before them were subdued. And we have certainly sent down evident signs. And for the deniersis a demeaning punishment
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:6: on the day when Allah resurrects them all and informs them of what they did. Allah has kept count of it, but they have forgotten it, and Allah is Witness over all things.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:7: Have younot seen that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth? There is no secret conversation between three but He is their fourth, nor between five but He is their sixth, nor less than that nor more but He is with them wherever they may be. Then on the Day of Resurrection He will inform them of what they did; indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of everything.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:8: Have younot seen those who were prohibited from conversing secretly but then revert to what they were prohibited from? They converse secretly in sin and hostility and(in) disobedience to the Messenger. And when they come to youthey greet you with a greeting that Allah never greeted you with, and they say within themselves, “Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?” Hell is enough for them; they will roast in it—so what a miserable destiny!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:9: O you who have attained faith, when you converse secretly, do not converse secretly in sin and hostility and(in) disobedience to the Messenger, but converse in virtue and mindfulness(of God) , and be mindful of Allah to Whom you will be herded.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:10: Indeed,(malicious) private conversations are from Satan, that those who have attained faith may be sad . But he cannot harm them at all except by Allah’s leave. And in Allah let the believers place their trust.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:11: O you who have attained faith, when you are told, “Make room for one another in assemblies ,” then make room so that Allah makes room for you. And when you are told, “Arise,” then arise. Allah elevates by degrees those of you who have attained faith and those given knowledge. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:12: O you who have attained faith, when you converse privately with the Messenger, give a donation ahead of your private conversation. That is better for you and cleaner. But if you do not find the means, then Allah is indeed Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:13: Are youreluctant to give donations before your private conversation? If you do not do so and Allah pardons you, then establish the prayer and bringthe purifying charityand obey Allah and His Messenger. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:14: Have younot seen those who allied themselves with a people upon whom is Allah’s wrath? They are neither of younor of them, and they swear to lies while they know(the truth) .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:15: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment; evil indeed is what they used to do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:16: They took their oaths as a cover and barred(others) from the way of Allah, so for them is a demeaning punishment.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:17: Neither their possessions nor their children will avail them anything against Allah. Those are the fellows of the Fire; therein they abide.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:18: On the day when Allah resurrects them all together, they swear to Him as they swear to you, thinking that they are(standing) upon something. Undoubtedly, it is indeed they themselves who are the liars.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:19: Satan has taken hold of them and so has caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah. Those are the party of Satan. Undoubtedly, it is indeed the party of Satan who are the losers.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:20: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are among the most humiliated.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:21: Allah has prescribed: “I will most surely overcome, I and My messengers.” Indeed, Allah is All-Powerful, Almighty.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.58:22: Youwill not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers or their sons or their brethren or their kinsfolk. Those—He has prescribed faith in their hearts and has aided them with a spirit from Him, and He will enter them into Gardens(of Paradise) beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide. Allah became well pleased with them and they became well pleased with Him. Those are the party of Allah. Undoubtedly, it is indeed the party of Allah who are the successful.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:1: Whatever is in the heavens and in the earth has been highly exalting Allah, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:2: It is He who evicted those who denied among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first exodus. Youdid not think they would depart, and they thought their fortresses would protect them from Allah, but Allah came at them from where they never expected and threw terror into their hearts. Theywreck their houses with their own hands and by the hands of the believers. So take a lesson, O you who are endowed with sight(s) .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:3: Had Allah not prescribed evacuation for them, He would have punished them in the Earlier(Life) , and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:4: That is because they went against Allah and His Messenger, and whoever goes against Allah—indeed, Allah is stern in retribution.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:5: Whatever palm tree youcut down or left standing on its roots, then that was by Allah’s leave and that He may disgrace those who are defiantly disobedient.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:6: And whatever Allah has turned over to His Messenger from them, you have spurred neither horse nor camel for them, but Allah gives authority to His messengers over whomever He wills, and Allah is All-Powerful over everything.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:7: Whatever Allah has turned over to His Messenger from the people of the towns, then that is for Allah and for the Messenger and for the relative and the orphans and the destituteand to the traveler in need, so that it does notcirculate exclusively between the wealthy among you. And whatever the Messenger brings you—accept it, and whatever he forbids you—abstain from it. And be mindful of Allah; indeed, Allah is stern in retribution.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:8: (It is) for the poor immigrantswho were evicted from their homes and their possessions, seeking grace from Allah, and(His) good pleasure, and supporting Allah and His Messenger— those are the sincere.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:9: And(for) those who,before them,had settled in the homeland and(adopted) the faith—theylove those who emigrated to them and find no need in their chests for what has been brought to them, and they give them priority over themselves even if they themselves are needy. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his(inner) self—then it is thosewho are the successful.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:10: And those who came after them, saying, “Our Lord, forgive us and our brethren who precededus in faith, and leave no malice in our hearts towards those who have attained faith. Our Lord, You are indeed Compassionate, Bestowing of mercy.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:11: Have younot seen those who became hypocrites, saying to their brethren who denied among the People of the Scripture, “Indeed, if you are evicted, we will certainly depart with you and not obey anyone against you, ever, and should anyone combat you, we will certainly support you”? But Allah bears witness that they are certainly liars.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:12: Indeed, if they are evicted, they will not depart with them; and indeed, if anyone combats them, they will not support them. And(even) if they do support them, they will(then) certainly turn their backs, then they will not be supported.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:13: Indeed, fear of youis surely more intense in their chests than fear of Allah; that is because they are people who do not comprehend.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:14: They do not combat youall together except from fortified strongholds or from behind walls . Their hostility towards each other is severe. Youwould think them united, but their hearts are diverse; that is because they are people who do not reason.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:15: Like those who shortly before them tasted the grievous consequences of their affairs, and for them is a painful punishment.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:16: Like the example of Satan when he said to man, “Deny,” but when he had denied, he said, “I disown you; I fear Allah, Lord of all realms.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:17: So the consequence for both of them wasthat they arein the Fire, abiding therein, and such is the repayment of the unjust.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:18: O you who have attained faith, be mindful of Allah, and let every soul look what it has put forth for tomorrow, and be mindful of Allah; indeed, Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:19: And donot be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves; those are the defiantly disobedient.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:20: Not equal are the fellows of the Fire and the fellows of the Garden(of Paradise) ; it is the fellows of the Garden who are the triumphant ones.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:21: Had We sent this Recitaldown upon a mountain, youwould have seen it(trembling) in reverence, crumbling in awe of Allah. And these parables We set forth for mankind, that they may reflect.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:22: He is Allah, besides Whom there is no god, the Knower of the hidden realm and the manifest; He is the All-Merciful, the Bestower of mercy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:23: He is Allah, besides Whom there is no god, the King, the Holy, the Peace(Giver) , the Believer, the Overseer, the Almighty, the Irresistible, the Sublime; Highly Exalted is Allah beyond what they associate.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.59:24: He is Allah, the Creator, the Maker, the Designer; His are the Most Beautiful Names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth highly exalts Him, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.60:1: O you who have attained faith, do not take My enemies and your enemies as guardians, extending love towards them when they have denied what has come to you of the truth, evicting the Messenger and yourselves because you believe in Allah, your Lord—if you have set out to strive in My way and to seek My pleasure. How can you secretly express love towards them while I know better what you have hidden and what you have made public? And whoever of you does that has certainly strayed from the right way.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.60:2: If they encounter you, they are enemies to you and they extend their hands and tongues against you with malice, for they would love that you become deniers.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.60:3: Neither your relativesnor your children will benefit you; on the Day of Resurrection Hewill decide betweenyou, for Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.60:4: Surely, there has always been an excellent role model for youin Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, “We disown you and what you worship apart from Allah. We have disbelievedin you, and enmity and hatred have surfaced between us and you forever until you believe in Allah alone.” Except for the words of Abraham to his father, “I will ask forgiveness for you, though I cannot protect you from Allah.” “Our Lord, in You we have placed our trust, and to You we have turned penitent, for to You is the destiny.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.60:5: Our Lord, do not make us a means of trial for those who have denied, and forgive us, our Lord; You are indeed the Almighty, the All-Wise.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.60:6: Indeed, there has always been an excellent role model in them for you(and) for anyone who has been putting hope in Allah and(expecting) the Last Day. But whoever turns away—indeed, Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.60:7: Hopefully, Allah will produce love between you and those of them whom you took for enemies, for Allah is All-Powerful, and Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.60:8: Allah does not forbid youfrom those who have neither combated you over religion nor evicted you from your homes—that you deal with them very kindly and equitably. Indeed, Allah loves the equitable.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.60:9: Rather, Allah forbids youfromthose who combated you over religion and evicted you from your homes and backed up(your enemies) in your eviction. And whoever takes them as guardians—those are the unjust.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.60:10: O you who have attained faith, when believing women come to you immigrating, test them; Allah knows better about their faith. And if youfind them to be faithful, do not send them back to the deniers; they are not lawful for themnor are they lawful for them. But give them what they have spent. And no sin is committed by you if you marry them, provided you give them their compensation. And do not hold on to ties with unbelieving women, but demand what you have spent and let them demand what they have spent. This is Allah’s judgment—He judges among you, for Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.60:11: And if any of yourwives should go over to the deniers and then you punish(them in retaliation) , then give those whose wives have gone away the equivalent of what they had spent. And be mindful of Allah in whom you are believers.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.60:12: O Prophet, if believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor fornicate, nor kill their children, nor commit perjury as to parenthood, nor disobey you in anything righteous—then accept their allegiance and ask Allah’s forgiveness for them; indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.60:13: O you who have attained faith, do not take for guardians people upon whom is Allah’s wrath—they have indeed despaired of the Hereafter as the deniers have despaired of the fellows of the graves.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.61:1: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth has been highly exalting Allah, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.61:2: O you who have attained faith, why do you say what you do not do?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.61:3: It is most loathsome to Allah that yousay what you do not do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.61:4: Indeed, Allah loves those who combat in His way, lining up in ranks as though they were a compact structure.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.61:5: And recall when Moses said to his people, “O my people, why do you hurt me, though you know that I am Allah’s Messenger to you?” And when they swerved, Allah caused their hearts to swerve, for Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.61:6: And recall when Jesus, son of Mary, said, “O Children of Israel, I am Allah’s Messenger to you, confirming what preceded me of the Torah and a bearer of glad tidings of a messenger who comes after me, whose name is Ahmad.” Yet when he came to them with evident proofs, they said, “This is evident sorcery .”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.61:7: And who is more unjust than one who fabricated lies against Allah when he was being invited to Islam? Thus Allah does not guide the unjust people.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.61:8: They want to extinguish Allah’s Light with their mouths, but Allah shall perfect His Light, even though the deniers hate it.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.61:9: It is He who sent His Messenger with the guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion, even though the pagans hate it.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.61:10: O you who have attained faith, shall I inform you of a bargain that will save you from a painful punishment?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.61:11: That youbelieve in Allah and His Messenger, and strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and yourselves; that is better for you, if you only knew—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.61:12: He will forgive youyour misdeeds and will enter you into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, and into beautiful residences in the Gardens of Eden; that is the great triumph.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.61:13: And something else youlove: support from Allah and an imminent conquest. So give glad tidings to the believers.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.61:14: O you who have attained faith, be the supporters ofAllah as Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples, “Who are my supporters towards Allah?” The disciples said, “We are the supporters of Allah.” Then a faction of the Children of Israel attained faith while another faction denied it, and We aided those who had attained faith against their enemy, so they came to prevail.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.62:1: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth highly exalts Allah, the Sovereign, the Holy, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.62:2: It is He who sent among the gentilesa messenger from among themselves, reading His signsto them and purifying them and teaching them the Scripture and wisdom—although they were indeed in evident misguidance before that—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.62:3: and(to) others of them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.62:4: That is Allah’s grace which He brings to whomever He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great grace.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.62:5: The likeness of those who were made to carry(the responsibility of) the Torah but then failed to carry it is as the likeness of the donkey carrying tomes. How miserable is the example of the people who rejected Allah’s signs, for Allah does not guide the unjust people.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.62:6: Say, “O you who have Judaized, if you claim to be the allies of Allah apart from(the rest of) mankind, then wish for death if you are truthful.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.62:7: But they will not wish for it ever due to what their hands have put forth, and Allah is All-Knowing of the unjust.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.62:8: Say, “Indeed, the death from which youflee—it is bound to encounter you, then you will be returned to the Knower of the hidden realm and the manifest, and He will inform you of what you used to do.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.62:9: O you who have attained faith, when the call to prayer is made on Friday, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave aside all selling; that is better for you if you only knew.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.62:10: Then when the prayer is concluded, disperse through the land and seek Allah’s grace and remember Allah much, that youmay succeed.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.62:11: Yet whenever theycome across a bargain or distraction they scramble towards it and leave youstanding. Say, “What is with Allah is better than(any) distraction or bargain, and Allah is the Best of providers.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.63:1: When the hypocrites come to you, they say, “We bear witness that you are most surely Allah’s Messenger.” And Allah knows that you are most surely His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are most surely liars:
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.63:2: they have taken their oaths as a cover, and so they have barred(others) from the way of Allah; indeed, evil is what they have been doing.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.63:3: That is because they believed then they denied, so their hearts were sealed—thus they do not comprehend.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.63:4: Yet when yousee them, their physiques impress you, and when they speak, you listen to what they say. They are like propped-up timber; they think every shout is aimed at them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. MayAllah strike them down! How can they be averted(from the truth) ?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.63:5: And when it is said to them, “Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you,” they keep turning their heads aside and yousee them turning away while acting arrogantly.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.63:6: It is the same for them whether youask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them—Allah will not forgive them; indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.63:7: It is they who say: “Do not spend anything on those who side with Allah’s Messenger, that they may disperse.” And to Allah belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not comprehend.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.63:8: They say, “If we return to al-Madinah, the mightier ones will surely evict the inferior ones.” But might belongs to Allah and His Messenger and the believers, but the hypocrites do not know.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.63:9: O you who have attained faith, let neither your wealth nor your children distract you from the remembrance of Allah, and whoever does that—then those are the losers.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.63:10: And spend from what We have provided for youbefore death approaches one of you, whereupon he says, “My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short while so that I may donate and become of the righteous!”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.63:11: But Allah will not delay a soul when its time has come, for Allah is All-Aware of what youdo .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:1: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth highly exalts Allah; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him all praise is due, and He is All-Powerful over everything.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:2: It is He Who created you: so some of you are deniers and some of you are believers. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:3: He created the heavens and the earth with truth, and He designed youand perfected your designs, and to Him is the destiny.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:4: He knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows whatever youkeep secret and whatever you make public. For Allah is All-Knowing of what lies within the chests.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:5: Has the news not reached youof those who denied before, so they tasted the grievous consequences of their affairs? For for them is a painful punishment.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:6: That is because their messengers came to them with evident proofs, but they said, “Are human beings going to guide us?” So they denied and turned away, but Allah had no need(for anyone) , for Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:7: Those who have denied have claimed that they will not be resurrected. Say, “Yes indeed, by my Lord, youwill be resurrected, then you will be informed of whatever you did, for that is easy for Allah.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:8: So have faith in Allah and His Messenger and the Lightwhich We have sent down. For Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:9: The day when He gathersyoufor the Day of Gathering—that is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain. And whoever attains faith in Allah and acts righteously, He will remit his evil deeds and Hewill enter himinto Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever; that is the great triumph.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:10: But those who denied and rejected Our signs—those are the fellows of the Fire, abiding therein, and what a miserable destiny!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:11: No disaster occurs except by Allah’s leave. And whoever believes in Allah—He guides his heart. For Allah is All-Knowing of everything.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:12: So obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if youturn away, then surely Our Messenger’s onlyduty is evident proclamation.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:13: Allah—there is no god but He. So in Allah let the believers place their trust.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:14: O you who have attained faith, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon and overlook and forgive—then indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:15: Indeed, your wealth and your children are but a means of trial, while with Allah is a great reward.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:16: So be mindful of Allah as much as youcan, and listen and obey and give(in charity) for your own good. For whoever is protected from the stinginess of his(inner) self—those are the successful.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:17: If youlend Allah a good loan, He will multiply it for you and will forgive you, for Allah is Ever Thankful, Forbearing—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.64:18: the Knower of the hidden realm and the manifest, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.65:1: O Prophet, when youdivorcewomen, then divorce them at a time when their(waiting) period can properly start, and calculate the period carefully. And be mindful of Allah, yourLord. Do not evict them from their houses nor shall they depart, unless they have committed an evident obscenity . Those are the limits of Allah, and whoever oversteps Allah’s limits, then he has surely been unjust to himself. Younever know—Allah may afterwards bring about a new matter.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.65:2: Once they have reached their term, either retainthem in accordance with what is fair or separate from them in accordance with what is fair. And call to witness two just people from among you and give upright testimony for Allah. That is to admonish whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, for whoever is mindful of Allah—He will make for him a way out(of every difficulty)
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.65:3: and will provide for him from where he never expects, and whoever places his trust in Allah—He will suffice him. Allah shall indeed conclude His decreed matters; Allah has set a due measure for everything.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.65:4: And those of your womenwho have despaired of(further) menstruation—if you have any doubts, their(waiting) period shall be three months, and also for those who have not menstruated. And those who are pregnant—their term shall be until they have delivered. And whoever is mindful of Allah—He will ease his affairs.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.65:5: That is Allah’s command which He has sent down to you. And whoever is mindful of Allah—He will remit his evil deeds and amplify his reward.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.65:6: Allow themto reside where youhave been residing according to your means, and do not harass them to make things difficult for them. And if they are pregnant, spend for them until they deliver. And if they nurse your infant, pay them their reward and conduct your relation in accordance with what is fair. But if you disagree, then another woman will nurse him.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.65:7: The wealthy one shall spend according to his means, and the one whose resources have been restrained shall spend according to what Allah has given him. Allah never tasks any self beyond what He has brought it; Allah shall bring ease after hardship.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.65:8: And how many a town has defied the command of its Lord and His messengers, so We held it to a strict reckoning and We punished it with a dreadful punishment:
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.65:9: it tasted the grievous consequence of its affairs, and the consequence of its affairs was perdition.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.65:10: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment, so beware of Allah, O you who possess intellect and have attained faith. Allah has sent down to you a Reminder—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.65:11: a messenger who reads to you Allah’s signs,(which are) clarifying , in order to bring out those who have attained faith and have done righteous deeds from darkness into light. And whoever believes in Allah and acts righteously—He will enter himinto Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever; Allah has surely given him an excellent provision.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.65:12: Allah is He Who created seven heavens, and their like of earth. The command descends between them so that youmay know that Allah is Powerful over everything and that Allah has encompassed everything in knowledge.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.66:1: O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has permitted for you,seeking to please your spouses? Yet Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.66:2: Allah has already ordained for youthe dissolution of your oaths, for Allah is your Patron, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.66:3: And recall when the Prophet confided a matter to some of his spouses, then as soon as one(of them) disclosed it(to another wife) and Allah made it known to him, he communicatedpart of it and disregarded another part. Then, when he informed her of it, she said, “Who informed you of this?” He said, “The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.66:4: If yourepentto Allah, then your hearts have listened. But if both of you band together against him, then Allah is his Patron, as are Gabriel and the righteous believers. And, in addition, the angels will back him.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.66:5: Perhaps, if he divorcesyou, his Lord will give him in exchange better spouses than you: Muslim, believing, devout, repentant, given to worshiping, given to fasting—whether previously married or virgins.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.66:6: O you who have attained faith, shield yourselves and your families from a fire whose fuel is people and stones; over it are fierce and powerful angels who never disobey Allah in anything He commands them, and they carry out whatever they are commanded.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.66:7: O you who have denied, make no excuses today; indeed, you are only being repaid for what you used to do.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.66:8: O you who have attained faith, repent to Allah with sincere repentance; hopefully your Lord will remit your evil deeds and enter you into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, on the day when Allah will never disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. With their light streaming before them and to their right, they say, “Our Lord, perfect our light for us and forgive us; You are indeed All-Powerful over everything.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.66:9: O Prophet, strive hard against the deniers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them. And their shelter is Hell, and what a miserable destiny!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.66:10: Allah has set forth a parable for those who denied: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot; they were under two servants of Our righteous servants but they betrayed them, so they availed them nothing against Allah, and it was said, “Enter the Fire with those who are entering.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.66:11: And Allah has set forth a parable for those who have attained faith: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, “My Lord, build for me, with you, a house in the Garden(of Paradise) , and deliver me from Pharaoh and his actions, and deliver me from the unjust people.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.66:12: And Mary, the daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity, and so We breathed into her of Our Spirit, and she believed in her Lord’s Words and His Scriptures and was one of the devout.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:1: Supremely Blessed be He in whose hand is the dominion, and He is All- Powerful over everything;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:2: the One Who created death and life to test youas to which of you is better in conduct, for He is the Almighty, the Oft-Forgiving;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:3: the One Who created seven heavens in layers: yousee no discrepancy in the creation of the All-Merciful. So look again: can you see any splits?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:4: Then look again and again—yoursight will return to you bedazzled and exhausted.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:5: And indeed, We have adorned the lowestheaven with lanterns and made them missiles against the Satans, and We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:6: And for those who have denied their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and what a miserable destiny!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:7: When they are thrown into it, they hear it roaring as it seethes—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:8: it almost bursts with rage. Every time a crowd is thrown into it, its keepers ask them, “Did no warner come to you?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:9: They said, “Yes, a warner did come to us, but we disbelieved and said, ‘Allah did not bestow anything from on high; it is youwho are greatly misguided!’”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:10: And they said, “Had we listened or reasoned, we would not have been among the fellows of the Blaze.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:11: Thus they acknowledged their misdeed, so away with the fellows of the Blaze.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:12: Indeed, for those who fear their Lord though Unseen, there is forgiveness and a supreme reward.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:13: And keep yourwords secret or say them aloud—indeed, He is All-Knowing of what lies within the chests.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:14: Would He not know whomever He has created, while He is the Subtle, the All-Aware?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:15: It is He who made the earth manageable for you, so walk through its regions and eat of His provision, and to Him is the Resurrection.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:16: Are youconfident that the One in heaven will not cause the earth to collapse beneath you as it spins?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:17: Or are you confident that the One in heaven will not unleash against you a violent storm? Then you will know what Mywarning is like.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:18: And surely those before them disbelieved(as well) , so how terrible was My condemnation!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:19: Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading their wings and folding them? None holds them except the All-Merciful; indeed, He is All-Seeing of everything.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:20: Or who is this who is an army for you, supporting you, apart from the All-Merciful? Indeed, the deniers are in nothing but a deception.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:21: Or who is this that will provide for you if He withholds His provision? Rather, they persist in defiance and aversion.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:22: Is one who walks bent on his own face better guided or one who walks upright on a straight path?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:23: Say, “It is He Who initiated youand made for you hearing and sight(s) and burning hearts; rarely do you give thanks.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:24: Say, “It is He Who scattered youon earth, and to Him you will be herded.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:25: And they say, “When will this promise be fulfilled if youare truthful?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:26: Say, “Indeed, knowledge is only with Allah, and indeed, I am only an evident warner.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:27: But when they saw it approaching, the faces of those who had denied turned gloomy, and it was said, “This is what youused to claim (would never happen) .”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:28: Say, “Have you seen: if Allah makes me and those with me perish or has mercy on us, who then will protect the deniers from a painful punishment?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:29: Say, “He is the All-Merciful; we have attained faith in Him, and in Him alone we have placed our trust, and soon youwill know who is in evident misguidance.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.67:30: Say, “Have youseen:if your water drains away, who then will bring you pure running water?”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:1: Nûn. By the pen and all that they inscribe.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:2: YourLord’s blessing does not make you a madman.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:3: And most surely, for youis an unfailing reward.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:4: And very truly, youare of great moral character.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:5: Thus youshall see and they shall see
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:6: which of you is the demented.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:7: Indeed, yourLord is He Who knows better who has strayed from His way, and it is He Who knows better of the rightly guided.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:8: So do not obey the disbelievers;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:9: they would like you to compromise, then they too would compromise.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:10: And do not obey any despicable swearer,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:14: Just because he has money and sons,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:15: when Our signsare read to him, he says, “Legends of the ancients!”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:16: We will brand him on the snout.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:17: Indeed, We have tested them as We tested the fellows of the garden, when they swore to harvest it in the morning
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:19: Then a sweeping visitation from yourLord swept through it while they were asleep,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:20: and in the morning it was as though harvested.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:21: So they called to each other in the early morning:
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:22: “Go early to yourfield if you are going to harvest.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:23: So they set out, murmuring to one another,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:24: “Not one destitute person is to enter it upon youtoday.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:25: And early they went, resolved in intent.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:26: But when they saw it, they said, “Indeed, we are surely misguided;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:28: The most reasonable of them said, “Did I not tell you, ‘if only you would highly exalt(God) ?’”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:29: They said, “Highly Exalted is our Lord; indeed, we were unjust.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:30: Then they turned to each other, blaming one another.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:31: They said, “Woe to us; indeed, we have exceeded all limits.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:32: Perhaps our Lord will give us a better substitute for it. Indeed, to our Lord we turn wishfully.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:33: Such is the punishment(of this world) ; but the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:34: Indeed, for the people who are mindful(of God) are Gardens of Bliss, with their Lord.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:35: Shall We treat the Muslimslike the criminals?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:36: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:37: Or do you have a scripture in which you study,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:38: wherein there is whatever you choose?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:39: Or do you have oaths from Us, binding until the Day of Resurrection, that you will have whatever you demand?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:40: Askthem which of them guarantees that.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:41: Or do they have associates? Then let them bring their associates if they are truthful.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:42: On the day when the shin is exposedand they are called to prostrate themselves, but theyare unable to.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:43: Their sight(s) (subdued) in reverence, humiliation overwhelms them, for they had been called to prostrate themselves when they were sound.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:44: So leaveMe to those who reject this discourse; We will draw them forth gradually(to punishment) from where they do not know.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:45: And I will give them respite. Indeed, My plot is firm.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:46: Or do youask them for a reward, so they are burdened with debt?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:47: Or do they have(knowledge of) the hidden realm and they are writing it down?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:48: So wait patiently for the Decree of yourLord, and do not be like the Fellow of the Whale, who cried out in despair.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:49: Were it not for his Lord’s favor that reached him, he would have been thrown into the wilderness, fully despised.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:50: But his Lord chose him and made him one of the righteous.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:51: Those who have denied almost stab youwith their sight(s) when they hear the Reminder, and say, “He is indeed a madman!”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.68:52: But it is nothing other than a Reminder to(all creatures of) all realms.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:3: And what can make yourealize what the Reality is?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:4: Thamûd and ʻĀd disbelieved in  the Shocking Event.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:5: So as for Thamûd, they were annihilated by the Overwhelming.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:6: And as for ʻĀd, they were annihilated by a furious, roaring wind
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:7: which He unleashed upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so youcould see the people tossed around as though they were stumps of hollow palm trees.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:8: So can yousee any remnant of them?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:9: Then Pharaoh and whoever was before him and the Overturned Citiescame up with grave offenses
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:10: and disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with an overpowering grip.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:11: Indeed, when the waters overflowed We carried youin the running ship,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:12: making it a lesson for you—so that an attentive ear may take heed.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:13: Then, when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:14: and the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with a single crush—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:15: on that day, the Inevitable Event shall come to pass
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:16: and the heaven shall crack, for on that day it shall be frail.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:17: And the angels are ranged around its borders, while eight carry the Throne of yourLord above them on that day.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:18: On that day youare presented, and no hidden secret of yours remains hidden.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:19: So as for the one who was given his recordin his right hand, he says, “Here, take my record and read it.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:20: Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my reckoning.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:21: So he will be in a well-pleasing living,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:22: in a lofty Garden(of Paradise) ,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:24: “Eat and drink with satisfaction on account of what youdidin the days gone by.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:25: But as for the one who was given his recordin his left hand, he says, “I wish I was never given my record
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:26: and never knew what my reckoning was.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:27: If only it was the end!
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:29: my power has vanished from me.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:32: then in a chain whose length is seventy cubits tie him up.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:33: For he would not believe in Allah, the Great,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:34: nor would he urge(others to serve) food to the destitute.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:35: So he has no intimate(friend) here today,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:37: which none eats except the wrongdoers.”
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:38: So I swear by what yousee
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:39: and what you do not see:
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:40: it is indeed the wordof a noble messenger
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:41: and in no way is it the word of a poet—little do youbelieve ,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:42: nor is it the speech of a soothsayer—little do you remind yourselves .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:43: (It is) a bestowal from on high by the Lord of all realms.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:44: And had he falsely attributed some statements to Us,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:45: We would certainly have seized him strongly,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:46: then We would certainly have slashed his aorta,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:47: and in no way could any of you have defended him.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:48: And indeed, it is a reminding for the mindful(of God) .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:49: And indeed, We do know that some of you are disbelievers.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:50: And indeed, it is surely a source of grief for the deniers.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:51: And indeed, it is surely the truth of certitude.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.69:52: So highly exalt the name of yourLord, the Great.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:1: An asker asked abouta punishment sure to come
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:2: for the deniers, that none can repel—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:3: from Allah, Lord of the Ways of Ascent.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:4: Unto Him the angels and the Spirit ascend on a day the duration of which is fifty thousand years.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:5: So bepatient with beautiful patience.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:8: on the day when the sky is like molten brass,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:9: and the mountains are like tufted wool,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:10: and no intimate(friend) asks his intimate(friend) —
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:11: though they are shown each other. The criminal wishes he could be redeemed from the punishment of that day by sacrificing his children
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:12: and his female companion and his brother
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:13: and his kinsfolk who shelter him
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:14: and everyone on earth, so it would then save him.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:15: But no! It is a raging fire
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:17: inviting the one who had retreated and turned away
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:20: when touched by adversity he is impatient,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:21: and when touched by good he is ungenerous;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:24: and those in whose wealth is a rightfully acknowledged share
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:25: for the asker and the deprived;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:26: and those who believe in the Day of Recompense;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:27: and those who fear their Lord’s punishment—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:28: indeed, none can feel secure from their Lord’s punishment;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:29: and those who preserve their private parts,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:30: except from their spouses or those whom they rightfully possess—for then they are indeed not blameworthy.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:31: But whoever seeks to go beyond that, then those are the transgressors;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:32: and those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenant;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:33: and those who stand by their testimonies ;
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:34: and those who preserve their prayers—
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:35: those are honored in Gardens(of Paradise) .
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:36: So what is with those who have denied, craning their necks towards you,
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:37: from the right and from the left, banding together?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:38: Does every one of them ardently hope to be entered into a Garden of Bliss?
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:39: But no! Indeed, We created them from what they know.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:40: So I swear by the Lord of the Easts and the Wests that We are surely able
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:41: to replace them with better than them, and We cannot be outstripped.
Fadel Soliman, Bridges’ translation.70:42: So letthem blunder and play until they meet their day which they are promised—
