T. Usmani.18:58: Your Lord is the Most Forgiving, the Lord of Mercy. If He seizes them for what they did, He may cause the punishment to befall them sooner, but there is an appointed time for them, from which they can never find a place of refuge.
T. Usmani.18:59: These are the towns that We destroyed when they (i.e. their people) transgressed, and We had appointed a time for their destruction.
T. Usmani.18:60: (Recall) when Mūsā said to his young man, “I shall not give up until I reach the meeting point of the two seas, or else I shall go on traveling for years.”
T. Usmani.18:61: So, when they reached the meeting point of the two seas, they forgot their fish, and it made its way into the sea as in a tunnel.
T. Usmani.18:62: When they went further, he said to his young man, “Bring us our morning meal; we have, indeed, had much fatigue from this journey of ours.”
T. Usmani.18:63: He said, “You see, when we stayed at the rock, I forgot the fish. It was none but Satan who made me forget it to tell you about it - and it made its way into the sea in an amazing manner.”
T. Usmani.18:64: He said, “That was what we were looking for.” So they returned, retracing their footsteps.
T. Usmani.18:65: Then they found one of Our servants whom We blessed with mercy from Us and whom We gave knowledge, a knowledge from Our own.
T. Usmani.18:66: Mūsā said to him, “May I have your company so that you teach me some of the rightful knowledge you have been given.”
T. Usmani.18:67: He said, “You can never bear with me patiently.
T. Usmani.18:68: And how would you keep patient over something your comprehension cannot grasp?”
T. Usmani.18:69: He (Mūsā) said, “You will find me patient, if Allah wills, and I shall not disobey any order from you.”
T. Usmani.18:70: He said, “Well, if you follow me, do not ask me about anything unless I myself start telling you about it.”
T. Usmani.18:71: So, they both moved ahead, until when they boarded a boat, he sliced it (by removing one of its planks). He (Mūsā) said, “Did you slice it to drown its people? In fact, you have done a terrible act.”
T. Usmani.18:72: He said, “Did I not say that you can never bear with me patiently?”
T. Usmani.18:73: He (Mūsā) said, “Do not hold me punishable for what I forgot, and do not make my course too difficult for me.”
T. Usmani.18:74: So, they moved ahead until when they met a boy, he killed him (the boy). He (Mūsā) said, “Did you kill an innocent soul while he did not kill anyone? You have committed a heinous act indeed.”
T. Usmani.18:75: He said, “Did I not tell you that you can never bear with me patiently?”
T. Usmani.18:76: He (Mūsā) said, “If I ask you about something after this, do not allow me your company. You have now reached a point where you have a valid excuse (to part with me) from my own side. “
T. Usmani.18:77: Then, they moved ahead until they came to the people of a town; they asked its people for food, and they refused to host them. Then, they found there a wall tending to fall down. So he (KhaDir) set it right. He (Mūsā) said, “If you wished, you could have charged a fee for this.”
T. Usmani.18:78: He said, “Here is the point of parting ways between me and you. I shall now explain to you the reality of things about which you could not remain patient.
T. Usmani.18:79: As for the boat, it belonged to some poor people who worked at sea. So I wanted to make it defective, as there was a king across them who used to usurp every boat by force.
T. Usmani.18:80: As for the boy, his parents were believers. We apprehended that he would impose rebellion and infidelity upon them.
T. Usmani.18:81: We, therefore, wished that their Lord would replace him with someone better than him in piety, and more akin to affection.
T. Usmani.18:82: As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was a treasure beneath it belonging to them, and their father was a pious man. So your Lord willed that they should reach their maturity and dig out their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. I did not do it on my own accord. This is the reality of things about which you could not remain patient.”
T. Usmani.18:83: They ask you about Dhul-Qarnain. Say, “I shall now recite to you an account of him.”
T. Usmani.18:84: Surely, We gave him power on earth and gave him means to (have) everything (he needs).
T. Usmani.18:86: until when he reached the point of sunset, he found it setting into a miry spring, and found a people near it. We said, “O Dhul-Qarnain, either punish them or adopt good behavior with them.”
T. Usmani.18:87: He said, “As for him who does wrong, we shall punish him, then he will be sent back to his Lord, and He will punish him with a severe punishment.
T. Usmani.18:88: As for the one who believes and acts righteously, he will have the best (life) as reward, and we shall speak to him politely in our directions.”
T. Usmani.18:90: until when he reached the point of sunrise, he found it rising over a people for whom We did not make any shelter against it.
T. Usmani.18:91: Thus it was, and Our knowledge fully comprehends whatever (wealth and equipment) he had with him.
T. Usmani.18:93: until when he reached between the two mountains, he found by them a people who were almost unable to understand anything said.
T. Usmani.18:94: They said, “O Dhul-Qarnain, the (tribes of) Ya’jūj and Ma’jūj (Gog and Magog) are mischief-makers on the earth. So, should we assign a tax for you on condition that you make a barrier between us and them?”
T. Usmani.18:95: He said, “What my Lord has (already) given in my control is better enough (for me than the tax you are offering to me), so help me (only) with some (man) power, and I shall make a rampart between you and them.
T. Usmani.18:96: Bring me big pieces of iron.” (They proceeded accordingly) until when he leveled up (the gap) between the two cliffs, he said, “Blow.” (They complied) until when he made it (like) fire, he said, “Bring me molten copper, and I will pour it upon this.”
T. Usmani.18:97: So they (Ya’jūj and Ma’jūj) were not able to climb it, nor were they able to make a hole in it.
T. Usmani.18:98: He said, “This is a mercy from my Lord. Then, when the promise of my Lord will come, He will make it leveled to the ground. The promise of my Lord is true.”
T. Usmani.18:99: And on that day, (i.e. the Doomsday) We will leave them (all the people including Ya’jūj and Ma’jūj) surging over one another. And the Horn shall be blown, then We shall gather them together.
T. Usmani.18:100: And on that day We will bring Jahannam fully exposed before the infidels
T. Usmani.18:101: whose eyes were under a cover against My reminders, and they were not able to listen.
T. Usmani.18:102: Do, then, the disbelievers deem (it fit) that they take My servants as patrons beside Me? Surely, We have prepared Jahannam as entertainment for the disbelievers.
T. Usmani.18:103: Say, “Shall We tell you about the greatest losers in respect of (their) deeds?
T. Usmani.18:104: Those are the ones whose effort in the worldly life has gone in vain, while they think they are doing well.
T. Usmani.18:105: Those are the ones who rejected the signs of their Lord and (the concept of) meeting with Him, so their deeds have gone to waste, and We shall assign to them no weight at all.
T. Usmani.18:106: That is their punishment, the Jahannam , for they disbelieved and made My signs and My messengers a mockery.
T. Usmani.18:107: Surely those who believed and did righteous deeds, theirs are the Gardens of Firdaus as entertainment
T. Usmani.18:108: where they will live forever, and will not wish to move from there.”
T. Usmani.18:109: Say, “If the ocean were to be ink for (writing) the Words of my Lord, the ocean would have been consumed before the Words of my Lord are exhausted, even though we were to bring another (ocean) like it in addition.”
T. Usmani.18:110: Say, “Surely, I am but a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your God is the One God. So the one who hopes to meet his Lord must do righteous deed and must not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord.”
T. Usmani.19:2: This is a narration of your Lord’s mercy to His servant Zakariyyā,
T. Usmani.19:3: When he called his Lord in a low voice.
T. Usmani.19:4: He said, “My Lord, I am in a state that bones in my body have turned feeble, and the head has flared up grey with old age, and I never remained, My Lord, unanswered in my prayer to You.
T. Usmani.19:5: I fear (my) kinsmen after me, and my wife is barren, so bless me with an heir, from Your own side,
T. Usmani.19:6: who inherits me and inherits the house of Ya‘qūb. And make him, My Lord, a favourite one.”
T. Usmani.19:7: (Allah said) “O Zakariyyā, We give you the good news of a boy whose name is YaHyā. We did not create any one before him of the same name.”
T. Usmani.19:8: He Said, “My Lord, how shall there be a boy for me while my wife is barren, and I have reached the extreme of old age?”
T. Usmani.19:9: He said, “So it is; your Lord said ‘it is easy for Me, and I did create you before, when you were nothing.’”
T. Usmani.19:10: He said, “My Lord, make for me a sign.” He said, “Your sign is that you will not (be able to) speak to the people for three (consecutive) nights, even though you will be sound in health.”
T. Usmani.19:11: Then he came out to his people from the place of prayer, and directed them by gestures to proclaim the purity of Allah at morning and evening.
T. Usmani.19:12: (When the child was born, Allah said to him,) “O YaHyā, hold on to the Book firmly.” And We gave him wisdom, while he was still a child,
T. Usmani.19:13: and (blessed him with) love from our own, and purity; and he was God-fearing,
T. Usmani.19:14: and he was good to his parents; and he was not oppressive (or) disobedient.
T. Usmani.19:15: Peace on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he will be raised alive.
T. Usmani.19:16: And mention in the Book (the story of) Maryam, when she secluded herself from her people to a place towards East,
T. Usmani.19:17: then she used a barrier to hide herself from them. Then, We sent to her Our Spirit, (Jibra’īl) and he took before her the form of a perfect human being.
T. Usmani.19:18: She said, “I seek refuge with the All-Merciful (Allah) against you, if you are God-fearing.”
T. Usmani.19:19: He said, “I am but a message-bearer of your Lord (sent) to give you a boy, purified.”
T. Usmani.19:20: She said, “How shall I have a boy while no human has ever touched me, nor have I ever been unchaste?”
T. Usmani.19:21: He said, “So it is; your Lord said, ‘It is easy for Me, and (We will do this) so that We make it a sign for people and a mercy from Us, and this is a matter already destined.’”
T. Usmani.19:22: So she conceived him, and went in seclusion with him to a remote place.
T. Usmani.19:23: Then the labour pains brought her to the trunk of a palm-tree. She said “O that I would have died before this, and would have been something gone, forgotten.”
T. Usmani.19:24: Then he called her from beneath her: “Do not grieve; your Lord has placed a stream beneath you.
T. Usmani.19:25: Shake the trunk of the palm-tree towards yourself and, it will drop upon you ripe fresh dates.
T. Usmani.19:26: So eat, drink and cool your eyes. Then if you see any human being, say (to him), “I have vowed a fast (of silence) for the All-Merciful (Allah,) and therefore, I shall never speak to any human today.”
T. Usmani.19:27: Then she came to her people carrying him (the baby). They said, “O Maryam you have committed something grave indeed.
T. Usmani.19:28: O sister of Hārūn, neither your father was a man of evil nor was your mother unchaste.”
T. Usmani.19:29: So, she pointed towards him (the baby). They said, “How shall we speak to someone who is still a child in the cradle?”
T. Usmani.19:30: Spoke he (the baby), “Verily I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Book, and made me a prophet,
T. Usmani.19:31: and He has made me a blessed one wherever I be, and has enjoined Salāh and Zakāh upon me as long as I am alive,
T. Usmani.19:32: and (He has made me) good to my mother, and he did not make me oppressive (or) ill-fated.
T. Usmani.19:33: And peace is upon me the day I was born, the day I shall die, and the day I shall be raised alive again.”
T. Usmani.19:34: That is ‘Īsā, the son of Maryam, to say the truth in which they (Christians) are disputing.
T. Usmani.19:35: It is not for Allah to have a son. Pure is He. When He decides a thing, He simply says to it, “Be” and it comes to be.
T. Usmani.19:36: And (O Prophet, say to the people,) “Allah is surely my Lord and your Lord. So, worship Him. This is the straight path.”
T. Usmani.19:37: Then the groups among them fell in dispute. So, how evil is the fate of the disbelievers when they have to face the Great Day.
T. Usmani.19:38: How strong will their hearing be, and how strong their vision, the day they will come to Us! But today the transgressors are straying in clear error.
T. Usmani.19:39: Warn them of The Day of Remorse when the whole thing will be settled, while they are heedless and do not believe.
T. Usmani.19:40: Surely We, only We, shall be the ultimate owner of the earth and all those on it, and to Us they will be returned.
T. Usmani.19:41: And mention in the Book (the story of) Ibrāhīm. Indeed, he was Siddīq (a man of truth), a prophet,
T. Usmani.19:42: when he said to his father, “My dear father, why do you worship something that does neither hear nor see, nor help you in any way?
T. Usmani.19:43: My dear father, indeed there has come to me a knowledge that has not come to you; so, follow me, and I shall lead you to a straight path.
T. Usmani.19:44: My dear father, do not worship the Satan. The Satan is surely rebellious to the All-Merciful, (Allah).
T. Usmani.19:45: My dear father, I fear lest a punishment from the All- Merciful (Allah) should afflict you, and you become a companion of Satan.”
T. Usmani.19:46: He said, “Are you averse to my gods O Ibrāhīm? Should you not stop, I will definitely stone you. And leave me for good.”
T. Usmani.19:47: He said, “Peace on you. I shall seek forgiveness for you from my Lord. He has always been gracious to me.
T. Usmani.19:48: And I go away from you and what you invoke besides Allah. And I shall invoke my Lord. Hopefully I shall not be a loser by invoking my Lord.”
T. Usmani.19:49: So, when he went away from them and what they worshipped besides Allah, We blessed him with IsHāq (Isaac) and Ya‘qūb (Jacob) and We made each one of them a prophet,
T. Usmani.19:50: and We bestowed on them (a great deal) of our mercy, and caused them to have a good name at a high level.
T. Usmani.19:51: And mention in the Book (the story of) Mūsā. Indeed he was a chosen one and was a messenger, a prophet.
T. Usmani.19:52: And We called him from the right side of the mount Tūr (Sinai), and We brought him close to communicate in secret.
T. Usmani.19:53: And, out of Our mercy, We granted him his brother Hārūn as a prophet.
T. Usmani.19:54: And mention in the Book (the story of) Ismā‘īl. He was indeed true to his promise, and was a messenger, a prophet.
T. Usmani.19:55: He used to enjoin Salāh and Zakāh upon his family, and was favourite to his Lord.
T. Usmani.19:56: And mention in the Book (the story of) Idrīs. He was indeed a Siddīq (man of truth), a prophet.
T. Usmani.19:57: We raised him to a high place.
T. Usmani.19:58: Those are the people whom Allah has blessed with bounties, the prophets from the progeny of ’Ādam, and of those whom We caused to board (the Ark) along with NūH, and from the progeny of Ibrāhīm and Isrā’īl (Jacob), and from those whom We guided and selected. When the verses of The RaHmān (The All-Merciful) were recited before them, they used to fall down in Sajdah (prostration), while they were weeping.
T. Usmani.19:59: Then came after them the successors who neglected Salāh and followed (their selfish) desires. So they will soon face (the outcome of their) deviation,
T. Usmani.19:60: except those who repent and believe and do good deeds, and therefore they will enter the Paradise and will not be wronged at all.
T. Usmani.19:61: (They will enter) the Gardens of eternity, promised by the All-Merciful (Allah) to His servants, in the unseen world. They will surely reach (the places of) His promise.
T. Usmani.19:62: They will not hear anything absurd therein, but a word of peace, and there they will have their provision at morn and eve.
T. Usmani.19:63: That is the Paradise We will give as inheritance to those of Our servants who have been God-fearing.
T. Usmani.19:64: (Jibra’īl X said to the Holy Prophet) “We do not descend but with the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is in front of us and what is behind us and what is in between; and your Lord is not the One who forgets.
T. Usmani.19:65: (He is) the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever lies between them. So, worship Him and persevere in His worship. Do you know any one worthy of His name?”
T. Usmani.19:66: Man says, “Is it that, once I die, I shall be brought forth alive?”
T. Usmani.19:67: Does not the man remember that We created him before, when he was nothing?
T. Usmani.19:68: So, by your Lord, We will definitely gather them together, and the devils as well; then We will definitely make them present around the Jahannam , fallen on their knees.
T. Usmani.19:69: Then, out of every group, We will certainly draw out those who were more rebellious against the All-Merciful (Allah).
T. Usmani.19:70: Then of course, We are most aware of those who are more deserving to enter it (the Jahannam ).
T. Usmani.19:71: There is none among you who does not have to arrive at it. This is undertaken by your Lord as an absolute decree, bound to be enforced.
T. Usmani.19:72: Then We will save those who feared Allah, and will leave the wrongdoers in it, fallen on their knees.
T. Usmani.19:73: When Our verses are recited to them in all their clarity, the disbelievers say to the believers, “Which of the two groups is superior in its place and better in its assembly?”
T. Usmani.19:74: How many a generation We have destroyed before them who were better in assets and outlook!
T. Usmani.19:75: Say, “Whoever stays straying, let his term be extended by the All-Merciful (Allah) still longer, until when they will see what they are being warned of: either the punishment or the Hour (of Doom), then they will know who was worse in his place and weaker in his forces.
T. Usmani.19:76: Allah makes those on the right path excel in guidance. And the everlasting virtues are better with your Lord in respect of reward and better in their return.
T. Usmani.19:77: Have you, then, seen him who rejected Our verses and said, “I shall certainly be given wealth and children”?
T. Usmani.19:78: Has he peeped into the Unseen or taken a covenant with the All-Merciful (Allah)?
T. Usmani.19:79: Never! We will write what he says and extend for him the punishment extensively.
T. Usmani.19:80: And We will inherit from him what he is talking about, and he will come to Us all alone.
T. Usmani.19:81: They have taken gods other than Allah, so that they may be a source of might for them.
T. Usmani.19:82: Never! They (their fabricated deities) will soon reject their having worshipped them, and they will be just the opposite for them.
T. Usmani.19:83: Have you not seen that We have sent the devils onto the disbelievers inciting them with all their incitements.
T. Usmani.19:84: So make no hurry about them; We are but counting for them a count down.
T. Usmani.19:85: The day We will assemble the God-fearing before the All-Merciful (Allah) as guests,
T. Usmani.19:86: and will drive the sinners towards the Jahannam as herds of cattle (are driven) towards water,
T. Usmani.19:87: none will have power to intercede, except the one who has entered into a covenant with the All-Merciful (Allah).
T. Usmani.19:88: They say, “The All-Merciful (Allah) has got a son.”
T. Usmani.19:89: Indeed you have come up with such an abominable statement
T. Usmani.19:90: that the heavens are well-nigh to explode at it, and the earth to burst apart, and the mountains to fall down crumbling,
T. Usmani.19:91: for they have ascribed a son to the All-Merciful (Allah),
T. Usmani.19:92: while it does not behove the All-Merciful to have a son.
T. Usmani.19:93: There is none in the heavens and the earth, but bound to come to the All-Merciful as a slave.
T. Usmani.19:94: He has fully encompassed them and precisely calculated their numbers,
T. Usmani.19:95: and each one of them is bound to come to Him on the Day of Judgment, all alone.
T. Usmani.19:96: Surely, those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them the All-Merciful (Allah) will create love.
T. Usmani.19:97: So We have made it (the Qur’ān) easy through your tongue, so that you give with it the good news to the God-fearing, and warn with it an obstinate people.
T. Usmani.19:98: And how many a generation We have destroyed before them! Do you sense (the presence of) any one of them, or hear from them even a whisper?
T. Usmani.20:2: We did not reveal the Qur’ān to you to (make you) face hardship
T. Usmani.20:3: rather to remind him who has the fear (of Allah),
T. Usmani.20:4: it being a revelation from the One Who created the earth, and high heavens.
T. Usmani.20:5: The RaHmān (Allah, the All-Merciful) has positioned Himself on the Throne.
T. Usmani.20:6: To Him belongs all that is in the heavens, all that is in the earth and whatever lies between them and whatever lies beneath the soil.
T. Usmani.20:7: If you pronounce the word aloud, then (it makes no difference, for) He certainly knows the secret and what is even more hidden.
T. Usmani.20:8: (Such is) Allah. There is no god but He. For Him are the Beautiful Names.
T. Usmani.20:9: Has there come to you the story of Mūsā?
T. Usmani.20:10: When he saw a fire and said to his family, “Stay here. I have noticed a fire. Perhaps I can bring you an ember from it, or find some guidance by the fire.”
T. Usmani.20:11: So when he came to it, he was called, “O Mūsā,
T. Usmani.20:12: it is Me, your Lord, so remove your shoes; you are in the sacred valley of Tuwā.
T. Usmani.20:13: I have chosen you (for prophet-hood), so listen to what is revealed:
T. Usmani.20:14: Surely, I AM ALLAH. There is no god but Myself, so worship Me, and establish Salāh for My remembrance.
T. Usmani.20:15: Surely, the Hour (i.e. the Day of Judgment) has to come. I would keep it secret, so that everyone is given a return for the effort one makes.
T. Usmani.20:16: So the one who does not believe in it and follows his desires must not make you neglectful of it, otherwise you will perish.
T. Usmani.20:17: And what is that in your right hand, O Mūsā?”
T. Usmani.20:18: He said, “It is my staff. I lean on it, and I beat down leaves with it for my sheep, and I have many other uses for it.”
T. Usmani.20:19: He said, “Throw it down O Mūsā”.
T. Usmani.20:20: So, he threw it down, and suddenly it was a snake, running around.
T. Usmani.20:21: He said, “Pick it up, and be not scared. We shall restore it to its former state.
T. Usmani.20:22: And press your hand under your arm, and it will come out (brightly) white without any disease, as another sign,
T. Usmani.20:23: so that We may show you some of Our great signs.
T. Usmani.20:24: Go to Pharaoh. He has really exceeded all bounds.”
T. Usmani.20:25: He said, “My Lord, put my heart at peace for me,
T. Usmani.20:26: and make my task easy for me
T. Usmani.20:27: and remove the knot from my tongue,
T. Usmani.20:28: so that they may understand my speech.
T. Usmani.20:29: And make for me an assistant from my own family,
T. Usmani.20:32: and make him share my task,
T. Usmani.20:33: so that we proclaim Your purity in abundance
T. Usmani.20:35: You are certainly watchful over us.”
T. Usmani.20:36: He said, “You have been granted your request O Mūsā.
T. Usmani.20:37: And We had bestowed Our favour on you another time,
T. Usmani.20:38: when We revealed to your mother what was to be revealed,
T. Usmani.20:39: that is, ‘Put him (the baby) in the chest, then cast it into the river, then let the river throw it by the shore, and it will be picked up by one who is enemy to Me and enemy to him.’ And I had cast love on you from Myself (so that you might be favourite of all), and that you might be brought up under My eye.
T. Usmani.20:40: (Remember) when your sister was going (to the family of Pharaoh) and was saying, ‘Shall I lead you to one who nurses him?’ Thus We brought you back to your mother, so that her eyes might have comfort and she might not grieve. And you had killed a person, then We brought you out of the trouble; and We tested you with a great ordeal. Then you lived a number of years amidst the people of Madyan. After all this, you came O Mūsā, to a destined point of time.
T. Usmani.20:41: I have fashioned you for Myself.
T. Usmani.20:42: Go, you and your brother, with My signs, and do not be slack in My remembrance.
T. Usmani.20:43: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh; he has indeed transgressed all limits.
T. Usmani.20:44: So speak to him in soft words. May be, he accepts the advice or fears (Allah)”.
T. Usmani.20:45: They said, “Our Lord, we fear that he will hasten against us, or will become (more) rebellious (against You).”
T. Usmani.20:46: He said, “Do not be afraid. I AM surely with you both. I hear and I see.
T. Usmani.20:47: So, come to him and say, ‘We are the messengers of your Lord. So, let the children of Isrā’īl go with us, and do not persecute them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord; and peace be upon the one who follows the guidance.
T. Usmani.20:48: Verily, it has been revealed to us that the punishment is for the one who denies and turns away.’”
T. Usmani.20:49: He (Pharaoh) said, “Who then is the Lord of you two, O Mūsā?”
T. Usmani.20:50: He (Mūsā) said, “Our Lord is the One who gave everything its due shape, then guided it.”
T. Usmani.20:51: He said, “Then, what is the status of the earlier generations?”
T. Usmani.20:52: He replied, “The knowledge about those is with my Lord in a Book. My Lord does neither err nor forget.”
T. Usmani.20:53: (He is) the One who made the earth a cradle for you, and made in it pathways for you to move, and sent down water from the heavens; and We brought forth with it pairs of different vegetations :
T. Usmani.20:54: Eat, and graze your cattle. Surely, in that there are signs for the people of understanding.
T. Usmani.20:55: From this (dust) We created you, and in this we shall put you back, and from this We shall raise you up once again.
T. Usmani.20:56: And We showed him (Pharaoh) all Our signs, yet he rejected and refused.
T. Usmani.20:57: Said he, “Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your sorcery, O Mūsā?
T. Usmani.20:58: We will, then, bring to you a similar sorcery. So, make an appointment between you and us for an even place, not to be backed out, neither by us nor by you.”
T. Usmani.20:59: He (Mūsā) said, “Your appointment is the festival day, and the people should be assembled at forenoon.”
T. Usmani.20:60: So, Pharaoh turned back, and put his plot together, then came.
T. Usmani.20:61: Mūsā said to them, “Pity on you, do not fabricate a lie against Allah, lest He should destroy you with a punishment. And loser is he who fabricates a lie.”
T. Usmani.20:62: Then, they disputed among themselves in their matter, and kept their talk secret.
T. Usmani.20:63: Said they, “Certainly, these two are sorcerers who wish to drive you out from your land, and do away with your excellent way of life.
T. Usmani.20:64: So, make your plot firm and come forth in one row. Successful today is the one who prevails.”
T. Usmani.20:65: They said, “O Mūsā, either you throw (first), or shall we be first to throw?”
T. Usmani.20:66: He said, “Rather, you throw.” Then, suddenly their ropes and sticks seemed to him, due to their magic, as if they were running.
T. Usmani.20:67: So, Mūsā concealed some fear in his heart.
T. Usmani.20:68: We said, “Do not be scared. Certainly, you are to be the upper most.
T. Usmani.20:69: And throw what is in your right hand, and it will devour what they have concocted. What they have concocted is but a sleight of a magician. And the magician does not succeed wherever he comes from.”
T. Usmani.20:70: So, the magicians were led (by the truth) to fall in prostration. They said, “We have (now) believed in the Lord of Hārūn and Mūsā.”
T. Usmani.20:71: He (Pharaoh) said, “You have believed in him before I permit you. This man is in fact your master who has taught you the magic. So I will certainly cut off your hands and your legs from opposite sides, and will crucify you on the trunks of palm-trees, and you shall know whose punishment, out of us, is more severe and more lasting.”
T. Usmani.20:72: They said, “We will never prefer you over the clear signs that have come to us, and over Him who has created us. So, decide whatever you have to decide. You will decide only for this worldly life.
T. Usmani.20:73: We have put our faith in our Lord, so that He forgives us for our sins and for the magic you compelled us to perform. And Allah is the Best and Everlasting.”
T. Usmani.20:74: Surely whoever comes to his Lord as a sinner, for him there is Jahannam in which he neither will die nor will live (a happy life).
T. Usmani.20:75: And whoever will come to Him as believer, having done righteous deeds, for such people there are the highest ranks,
T. Usmani.20:76: the eternal gardens beneath which rivers flow, in which they shall live for ever. That is the reward for the one who has purified himself.
T. Usmani.20:77: And We revealed to Mūsā saying, “Set out with my servants at night, then make for them a dry path across the sea (with the strike of your staff), neither fearing to be caught up, nor having any fear (of drowning).”
T. Usmani.20:78: Then Pharaoh chased them with his troops. So, they were encircled by that (huge wave) from the sea which overwhelmed them.
T. Usmani.20:79: Pharaoh held his people astray, and did not show them the right path.
T. Usmani.20:80: O children of Isrā’īl , We delivered you from your enemy and appointed for you the right side of the mount Tūr (Sinai), and sent down for you the Mann and Salwā :
T. Usmani.20:81: Eat from the good things We have provided to you, and do not exceed the limits in it, lest My wrath should descend on you. The one upon whom My wrath descends certainly falls into destruction.
T. Usmani.20:82: Surely I am the Most-Forgiving for him who repents and believes and acts righteously, then follows the right path.
T. Usmani.20:83: “What has caused you to hurry before your people, O Mūsā?”
T. Usmani.20:84: He said, “Here they are just behind me, and I hurried towards You, my Lord, so that You be pleased.”
T. Usmani.20:85: He said, “We have then put your people to test after you (left them) and Sāmiriyy has misguided them.”
T. Usmani.20:86: So, Mūsā went back to his people, angry and sad. He said, “O my people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise? Did then the time become too long for you, or did you wish that wrath from your Lord befalls you, and hence you broke your promise to me?”
T. Usmani.20:87: They said, “We did not break our promise to you of our own accord, but we were burdened with loads from the ornaments of the people;so we threw them, and thus did Sāmiriyy cast.”
T. Usmani.20:88: Then he brought forth for them a calf, which was (merely) a body with a lowing sound. Then they said, “This is your god and the god of Mūsā, and he (Mūsā) erred.”
T. Usmani.20:89: Have they not been seeing that it did not respond to them (even) with a word, nor did it have power to harm or benefit them?
T. Usmani.20:90: Hārūn had already said to them, “O my people, you have only been led astray with it, and your Lord is the RaHmān (All-Merciful). So follow me and obey my command.”
T. Usmani.20:91: They said, “We will never cease to stay with it in devotion, until Mūsā returns to us.”
T. Usmani.20:92: He (Mūsā) said, “O Hārūn, what did prevent you from following me when you saw them going astray?
T. Usmani.20:93: Did you then disobey my command?”
T. Usmani.20:94: He said, “O son of my mother, do not hold me by my beard, nor by my head. I feared that you would say, ‘You have caused discord among the children of Isrā’īl and did not observe my advice.’”
T. Usmani.20:95: He (Mūsā) said, “What then is your case, O Sāmiriyy?”
T. Usmani.20:96: He said, “I perceived something they did not perceive. So I picked up a handful from under the footstep of the messenger. Then, I cast it. And thus my inner self tempted me.”
T. Usmani.20:97: He (Mūsā) said, “Then go away; it is destined for you that, throughout your life, you will say: ‘Do not touch me’. And, of course, you have another promise that will not be broken for you. And look at your god to which you stayed devoted. We will certainly burn it, then we will scatter it thoroughly in the sea.
T. Usmani.20:98: Your God is Allah other than whom there is no god. He encompasses everything with knowledge.”
T. Usmani.20:99: This is how We narrate to you certain events of what has passed, and We have given to you, from Ourself, a (book of) advice.
T. Usmani.20:100: Whoever turns away from it shall certainly bear a heavy burden on Doomsday,
T. Usmani.20:101: all such people living under it forever. And how evil for them will be that burden on the Doomsday!
T. Usmani.20:102: The Day when the Horn (Sūr) will be blown, and We shall gather them together while they will have turned blue on that day,
T. Usmani.20:103: and will be whispering among themselves, “You did not remain (in graves) more than ten (days)”.
T. Usmani.20:104: We know very well what they say, when the best of them in his ways will say, “You did not remain more than one day.”
T. Usmani.20:105: They ask you about the mountains. So, say (to them), “My Lord will crush them into dust thoroughly,
T. Usmani.20:106: then will turn them into a leveled plain
T. Usmani.20:107: in which you will see neither a curve nor an uneven place.”
T. Usmani.20:108: That day they will follow the caller who will find no deviation (from anyone). And the voices will turn low in awe for the RaHmān (All-Merciful, Allah). So, you will hear not but whispering.
T. Usmani.20:109: That day no intercession will be of any use to anyone, except the one whom the RaHmān (All-Merciful, Allah) has permitted and was pleased with his word.
T. Usmani.20:110: He knows what is in front of them and what is behind them, and they do not encompass Him in (their) knowledge.
T. Usmani.20:111: All faces will be humbled before (Allah,) the Ever-Alive, the All-Sustaining; and the loser will be the one who bears (the burden of his) injustice.
T. Usmani.20:112: But whoever does righteous deeds, while he is a believer, shall fear neither injustice nor curtailment (of his rewards).
T. Usmani.20:113: And in this way We have sent it down to you as an Arabic Qur’ān, and have detailed in it some warnings in various ways, so that they may fear, or it may produce a lesson for them.
T. Usmani.20:114: So High above all is Allah, the True King! And do not hasten with (reciting) the Qur’ān before its revelation to you is concluded, and say, “My Lord, improve me in knowledge.”
T. Usmani.20:115: We had given a directive to ’Ādam earlier, then he forgot, and We did not find in him a firm resolve.
T. Usmani.20:116: When We said to the angels, “Prostrate yourselves to ’Ādam”. So, all of them fell prostrate, except Iblīs , who refused.
T. Usmani.20:117: So, We said “’Ādam, this is an enemy to you and to your wife. So let him not expel you from Paradise, lest you should get into trouble.
T. Usmani.20:118: Here you have the privilege that you will not be hungry nor will you be unclad,
T. Usmani.20:119: and you will not be thirsty, nor will you be exposed to sun.”
T. Usmani.20:120: Then the Satan instigated him. He said, “’Ādam, shall I guide you to the tree of eternity and to an empire that does not decay?”
T. Usmani.20:121: So, both of them Ādam and Hawwā’ (Eve)] ate from it, and their parts of shame were exposed to them, and they started stitching on themselves some of the leaves of Paradise. And ’Ādam disobeyed his Lord, and erred.
T. Usmani.20:122: Thereafter his Lord chose him. So He accepted his repentance and gave (him) guidance.
T. Usmani.20:123: He said (to ’Ādam and Iblīs), “Go down from here, all of you, some of you enemies of some others. Then, should some guidance come to you from Me, the one who follows My guidance shall not go astray, nor shall he be in trouble.
T. Usmani.20:124: As for the one who turns away from My message, he shall have a straitened life, and We shall raise him blind on the Day of Judgment.”
T. Usmani.20:125: He will say, “My Lord, why did you raise me blind while I was sighted?”
T. Usmani.20:126: He will say, “In the similar manner as Our signs came to you, and you had ignored them. In the same way you will be ignored today.”
T. Usmani.20:127: Thus We recompense him who exceeds the limits and does not believe in the signs of his Lord. Certainly the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting.
T. Usmani.20:128: Did it give them no guidance (to realize) how many generations We have destroyed prior to them in whose dwellings they (often) walk around? Surely, in this there are signs for the men of reason.
T. Usmani.20:129: But for a word from your Lord that had passed earlier, and an appointed time that had been fixed, it (the punishment) would have been inevitable (for them).
T. Usmani.20:130: So, (O messenger,) endure with patience what they say, and proclaim the purity and praise of your Lord before sunrise and before sunset. And in some hours of night, proclaim His purity, and at points of the day as well, so that you may be pleased.
T. Usmani.20:131: Never stretch your eyes towards the things We have given to some groups of them to enjoy, so that We put them to test thereby, it being merely glamour of the worldly life. And the bounty of your Lord is much better and more lasting.
T. Usmani.20:132: Bid your family to perform Salāh, and adhere to it yourself. We ask no provision from you. We give provision to you. And the ultimate end is in favour of Taqwā (God-fearing, and piety).
T. Usmani.20:133: They say, “Why does he not bring to us a sign from his Lord?” Has there not come to them the clear sign of what is contained in the earlier Scriptures?
T. Usmani.20:134: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, “Our Lord, why did you not send a messenger to us, so that we might have followed Your signs before we were humiliated and put to disgrace?”
T. Usmani.20:135: Say, “Everyone is waiting. So wait, then you will know who the people of the straight path are and who has followed the right guidance.”
T. Usmani.21:1: The reckoning of the people has drawn near to them, while they are in negligence, turning away (from its signs).
T. Usmani.21:2: No fresh message of advice comes to them from their Lord, but they listen to it as if they were playing,
T. Usmani.21:3: their hearts paying no heed. And the wrongdoers whisper in secret, “This one is nothing but a mortal like you. Would you then go along with sorcery while you can see (the reality)?”
T. Usmani.21:4: He (the prophet) said, “My Lord knows all that is spoken in the heavens and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.”
T. Usmani.21:5: Further they said, “(The Qur’ān is) a mixture of jumble dreams. Rather, he (the prophet) has fabricated it. Rather, he is a poet. So, let him bring a sign to us, as the earlier ones were sent with.”
T. Usmani.21:6: Not a single town from those whom We destroyed came to believe before them. So, will they believe?
T. Usmani.21:7: And We did not send before you messengers except men whom We inspired with revelation. So, ask the people (having the knowledge) of the Message, if you do not know.
T. Usmani.21:8: We did not make them such bodies as ate no food, nor were they immortal.
T. Usmani.21:9: Then We caused the promise to come true for them, so We saved them and those whom We willed, and destroyed the transgressors.
T. Usmani.21:10: Surely, We have sent down to you (O people of Arabia) a book having a good counsel for you. So, do you not understand?
T. Usmani.21:11: How many a town, that were unjust, have We crushed and raised up after them another people!
T. Usmani.21:12: So, as soon as they sensed Our punishment (approaching them), they started fleeing from it.
T. Usmani.21:13: (It was said to them,) “Do not flee, and go back to the luxuries you were made to enjoy, and to your dwellings. May be you are asked questions.”
T. Usmani.21:14: They said, “Alas for us! We were wrongdoers indeed.”
T. Usmani.21:15: Then, this continued to be their cry till We turned them into stubble, totally extinguished.
T. Usmani.21:16: We did not create the heavens and the earth and what lies between them for play.
T. Usmani.21:17: Had We intended to have a pastime, We would have had it from Our own, if We were ever to do so.
T. Usmani.21:18: Instead, We launch the truth against falsehood, which gets it smashed, and in no time it is gone. Alas to you for what you describe!
T. Usmani.21:19: To Him belong all those in the heavens and the earth. And those who are near to Him are not arrogant against His worship, nor are they sluggish.
T. Usmani.21:20: They proclaim His purity night and day, never slackening.
T. Usmani.21:21: Or have they adopted gods from the earth, who raise the dead?
T. Usmani.21:22: Had there been gods beside Allah, in the heavens and the earth, both of them would have fallen in disorder. So pure is Allah, the Lord of the Throne, from what they describe.
T. Usmani.21:23: He is not questioned of what He does, and they are questioned.
T. Usmani.21:24: Is it that they have adopted gods besides Him? Say, “Bring your proof.” Here is the (book carrying) advice for those with me, and the (books carrying) advice for those before me. Yet most of them do not know the truth, and therefore they are averse.
T. Usmani.21:25: We did not send before you any messenger but We revealed to him that there is no god but I, so worship Me.”
T. Usmani.21:26: They said, “The RaHmān (the All-Merciful, Allah) has taken children for Himself.” Pure is He (from having children). They are but (His) honored servants.
T. Usmani.21:27: They do not precede Him in speech, and only under His command they act.
T. Usmani.21:28: He knows what is in front of them and what is behind them, and they make recommendation for none but for whom He likes, and in awe of Him they are fearful.
T. Usmani.21:29: Should any one of them say, “I am god besides Him”, We will recompense him with Jahannam (Hell). This is how We recompense the transgressors.
T. Usmani.21:30: Did the disbelievers not observe that the heavens and the earth were closed, then We opened them? And We created from water every living thing. Would they still not believe?
T. Usmani.21:31: And We created mountains on the earth, lest it should shake with them, and We have made therein paths and ways, so that they are guided.
T. Usmani.21:32: We made the sky a protected roof; and they are averse to its signs.
T. Usmani.21:33: He is the One who has created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, each floating in an orbit.
T. Usmani.21:34: We did not assign immortality to any human (even) before you. So, if you die, will they live for ever?
T. Usmani.21:35: Every one has to taste death, and We test you through bad and good (situations) with a trial, and to Us you are to be returned.
T. Usmani.21:36: When disbelievers see you, they do nothing but take you in jest (saying to one another,) “Is this the one who talks of your gods?” - while they themselves reject even talking of the RaHmān (All-Merciful).
T. Usmani.21:37: Man is made of haste. I shall show you My signs, so do not seek haste from Me.
T. Usmani.21:38: They say, “When will this promise be (fulfilled), if you are true?”
T. Usmani.21:39: Only if the disbelievers were to know the time when they will not (be able to) keep off the fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped.
T. Usmani.21:40: Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and will baffle them. So they will not be able to turn it back, nor will they be given respite.
T. Usmani.21:41: In fact, messengers have been mocked at prior to you. So those who laughed at them were besieged by what they used to ridicule.
T. Usmani.21:42: Say, “Who will guard you, during night and day, against the RaHmān (All-Merciful, Allah)?” Rather, to the remembrance of their Lord they are averse.
T. Usmani.21:43: Or do they have gods who protect them besides Us? They are not able to help even themselves, nor will they have anyone to side with them against Us.
T. Usmani.21:44: But We have given benefits to these and their fathers until life was prolonged for them. So do they not see that We are coming to the land narrowing it down from all its sides? Then, are they the ones to prevail?
T. Usmani.21:45: Say, “I warn you only by revelation, but the deaf do not listen to the call when they are warned.”
T. Usmani.21:46: If a whiff of your Lord’s torment were to touch them, they would certainly say, “Alas to us! We were wrongdoers indeed.”
T. Usmani.21:47: We shall place scales to do justice on the Day of Judgment. So no one shall be wronged in the least. Even if it (a deed) is to the measure of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth, and We are enough to take account.
T. Usmani.21:48: And We gave Mūsā and Hārūn the Criterion, and a light and an advice for the God-fearing,
T. Usmani.21:49: - those who have awe of their Lord without having seen Him, and are fearful of the Hour (of Judgment).
T. Usmani.21:50: And this is a blessed advice We have sent down. Are you still rejecting it?
T. Usmani.21:51: Even earlier We had given Ibrāhīm his right course, and We knew him well
T. Usmani.21:52: when he said to his father and his people, “What are these statues you are devoted to?”
T. Usmani.21:53: They said, “We found our fathers worshipping them,”
T. Usmani.21:54: He said, “Surely you and your fathers have been in open error.”
T. Usmani.21:55: They said, “Did you come to us with truth or are you one of the triflers?”
T. Usmani.21:56: He said, “No, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who has created them, and I am one of those who bear witness to it.
T. Usmani.21:57: And I swear by Allah that I will devise something against your idols after you have gone away turning your backs.”
T. Usmani.21:58: Then, he turned all of them into pieces, except the big one of them, so that they may come back to it.
T. Usmani.21:59: They said, “Who has done this to our gods? He is one of the wrongdoers indeed.”
T. Usmani.21:60: Some of them said, “We have heard a youth talking about them. He is called Ibrāhīm.”
T. Usmani.21:61: They said, “Then, bring him before the eyes of the people, so that they may see”.
T. Usmani.21:62: They said, “Is it you O Ibrāhīm who has done this to our gods?”
T. Usmani.21:63: He said, “Rather, this is done by this chief of theirs. So, ask them if they can speak.”
T. Usmani.21:64: So they turned to one another and said, “In fact, you yourselves are the wrongdoers.”
T. Usmani.21:65: Then, hanging their heads they reversed their position (and replied to Ibrāhīm,) “You already knew that they do not speak.”
T. Usmani.21:66: He said, “Do you then worship, beside Allah, what does neither benefit you in the least nor harm you?
T. Usmani.21:67: Fie upon you and upon what you worship other than Allah. Do you then not understand?”
T. Usmani.21:68: They said, “(O people) burn him and help your gods, if you are to take action.”
T. Usmani.21:69: We said, “O fire, be cold and safe for Ibrāhīm.”
T. Usmani.21:70: And they intended to harm him, but We made them the worst losers.
T. Usmani.21:71: And We rescued him and LūT towards the land we blessed for all the worlds.
T. Usmani.21:72: And We blessed him with IsHāq and Ya‘qūb as gift, and each one of them We made righteous.
T. Usmani.21:73: And We made them the Imams who guided (people) under Our command, and We inspired them to do good deeds and to establish Salāh and pay Zakāh, and Us alone they worshipped.
T. Usmani.21:74: As for LūT, We gave him wisdom and knowledge, and We delivered him from the town that used to do dirty deeds. Indeed, they were the people of evil, the sinners.
T. Usmani.21:75: And We admitted him to Our mercy. Indeed, He was of the righteous.
T. Usmani.21:76: And (remember) NūH, when he called (for help) earlier, so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the terrible agony,
T. Usmani.21:77: and helped him against the people who gave the lie to Our verses. Indeed, they were the people of evil, therefore, We drowned them all.
T. Usmani.21:78: And (remember) Dawūd (David) and Sulaimān (Solomon), when they were adjudicating about the tillage in which the goats of other people wandered at night (and trampled it), and We were witness to their judgment.
T. Usmani.21:79: So, We enabled Sulaimān to understand it. And to each one of them We gave wisdom and knowledge. And with Dawūd We subjugated the mountains that pronounced tasbīH (Allah’s purity), and the birds as well. And We were the One who did (it).
T. Usmani.21:80: We taught him the skill of making armor as dress for you to protect you from what may harm you (in combat). So are you grateful?
T. Usmani.21:81: And for Sulaimān, (We subjugated) the violent wind that blew under his command to the land in which We placed Our blessings. And We were the One who knew everything.
T. Usmani.21:82: And from the devils, (We subjugated for him) those who dived in water for him and did jobs other than that. And We were the One who kept watch over them.
T. Usmani.21:83: And (remember) Ayyūb (Job), when he called his Lord saying, “Here I am, afflicted by pain and You are the most merciful of all the merciful.”
T. Usmani.21:84: So, We answered his prayer and removed whatever pain he had, and gave him (back) his family and the like thereof along with them, as a mercy from Our own Self and as a lesson for the worshippers.
T. Usmani.21:85: And (remember) Ismā‘īl and Idrīs and Dhul-Kifl. Each one of them was of those who observed patience.
T. Usmani.21:86: And We admitted them to Our mercy. Surely, they were of the righteous.
T. Usmani.21:87: And (remember) Dhunnūn (the man of the fish, namely Yūnus X), when he walked away in anger and thought that We would never put him to trouble. Then, he called (Us) in depths of darkness saying, “There is no god but You. Pure are You. Indeed I was among the wrongdoers”.
T. Usmani.21:88: So We responded to him and rescued him from the distress. And this is how We rescue the believers.
T. Usmani.21:89: And (remember) Zakariyyā when he called his Lord, “My Lord, do not leave me alone and You are the best of inheritors.”
T. Usmani.21:90: So, We responded to him and gave him YaHyā and made his wife good for him. They used to race towards the good deeds and call Us with hope and fear; and they were humble to Us.
T. Usmani.21:91: And (remember) her who protected her private part (that is, Maryam). So, We blew in her (a life) through Our Spirit, and made her and her son (‘Īsā X) a sign for all the worlds.
T. Usmani.21:92: Surely, this is the fraternity of your Faith, a single Faith, and I am your Lord; so worship Me.
T. Usmani.21:93: But they have separated their ways from one another. All of them have to return to Us.
T. Usmani.21:94: So, whoever does righteous deeds, while he is a believer, his effort will not be rejected, and We are to put it on record.
T. Usmani.21:95: It is banned for (the people of) a town that We destroyed that they come back
T. Usmani.21:96: until when the Ya’jūj and Ma’jūj (Gog and Magog) are released, while they run down from every height,
T. Usmani.21:97: and the True Promise draws near, then it will so happen that the eyes of the disbelievers shall remain upraised (in terror, and they will say,) “Alas to us! We were in negligence about this; rather we were transgressors.”
T. Usmani.21:98: Surely, you and whatever you worship other than Allah are the fuel of Jahannam.. There you will have to arrive.
T. Usmani.21:99: Had they been gods, they would not have arrived at it, and all of them will remain there forever.
T. Usmani.21:100: For them, there will be screams in it and they will not hear.
T. Usmani.21:101: As for those for whom the good (news) from Us has come earlier, they will be kept far away from it.
T. Usmani.21:102: They will not hear the slightest of its sound, and they will remain forever in what their souls desire.
T. Usmani.21:103: They shall not be grieved by the Biggest Panic, and the angels shall receive them (saying), “This is your day that you had been promised”
T. Usmani.21:104: - the Day when We roll up the sky like a scroll rolls up the writings. Just as We originated the first creation, so We shall bring it back again - a promise (undertaken to be binding) on Us. We are sure to do it.
T. Usmani.21:105: And We have written in Zabūr (Psalms) after the advice that the land will be inherited by My righteous slaves.
T. Usmani.21:106: Surely, in this (Qur’ān) there is a message conveyed to a people who worship (Allah).
T. Usmani.21:107: And We have not sent you but as mercy for all the worlds.
T. Usmani.21:108: Say, “What is revealed to me is simply that your God is One God. So do you submit?”
T. Usmani.21:109: But, if they turn away, then say (to them), “I have warned you all alike, and I do not know whether what you have been warned of is near or far.
T. Usmani.21:110: Surely, He knows what is spoken openly and He knows what you conceal.
T. Usmani.21:111: And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a while.”
T. Usmani.21:112: He (Our Messenger) said, “My Lord, judge with truth. And Our Lord is the RaHmān (All-Merciful), the One whose help is sought against what you describe.
T. Usmani.22:1: O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed the quake of the (destined) Hour is something terrible.
T. Usmani.22:2: The day you will see it, every suckling female will forget that which she suckles, and every female having pregnancy shall abort her fetus, and you will see people as if they are drunk, while they are not drunk, but Allah’s torment is (so) severe.
T. Usmani.22:3: Among the people there is one who debates about Allah without knowledge, and follows every rebellious Satan,
T. Usmani.22:4: about whom it is destined that if someone takes him for friend, he will misguide him and lead him to the torment of the Fire.
T. Usmani.22:5: O mankind, if you are in doubt about Resurrection, then (recall that) We created you from dust, then from a drop of semen, then from a clot, then from a piece of flesh, either shaped or unshaped, so that We manifest (Our power) to you.We retain in the wombs whatever We will to a specified term. Then We bring you out as babies, then (We nourish you) so that you reach your maturity. And among you there is one who dies, and among you there is one who is carried to the worst part of the age, so that he knows nothing even after having knowledge.And you see the land dry. Then once We send down water on it, it stirs and swells and puts forth every pleasant pair (of vegetation).
T. Usmani.22:6: That is because Allah is the truth, and that He gives life to the dead, and that He is powerful to do everything,
T. Usmani.22:7: and that the Hour (of Doom) has to come, in which there is no doubt, and that Allah will raise again all those in the graves.
T. Usmani.22:8: Among men there is one who debates about Allah with no knowledge, no guidance and no enlightening book,
T. Usmani.22:9: turning his side away to lead (people) astray from the way of Allah. For him there is disgrace in this world, and We will have him taste the punishment of Fire on the Day of Judgment
T. Usmani.22:10: (and will say to him) “All this is due to what your hands sent ahead, and that Allah is not unjust to His servants.”
T. Usmani.22:11: And among men there is one who worships Allah (standing) on the verge: so if some good thing happens to him, he is satisfied with it, and if a trial befalls him, he turns his face back. He loses both this world and the Hereafter. That is the manifest loss.
T. Usmani.22:12: He prays to someone, instead of Allah, who can neither harm him nor benefit him. That is the error that takes him too far from the right path.
T. Usmani.22:13: He, rather, prays to someone whose harm is more likely than his benefit. Wretched is such a patron and wretched is such a companion.
T. Usmani.22:14: Surely, Allah will admit those who believe and do good deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. Surely Allah does what He intends.
T. Usmani.22:15: If someone thinks that Allah will never help him (the prophet) in this world and in the Hereafter, he should stretch a rope to the sky, then cut (Allah’s communication) off (from the prophet) and see whether his effort can really remove what irritates (him).
T. Usmani.22:16: And this is how We have sent it (the Qur’ān) down as clear signs, and the fact is that Allah leads whom He wills to the right path.
T. Usmani.22:17: As for those who believe and the Jews and the Sabians and the Christians and the Magians and those who ascribe partners to Allah, Allah will judge between them on the Day of Judgment. Surely Allah is witness to every thing.
T. Usmani.22:18: Have you not seen that to Allah prostrate all those in the skies and all those on the earth, and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the animals and many from mankind? And there are many on whom punishment has become due. And the one whom Allah puts to disgrace, there is none to give him respect. Surely Allah does what He wills.
T. Usmani.22:19: These are two opponents who have disputed about their Lord. As for those who disbelieve, garments from fire shall be tailored for them, and boiling water shall be poured from over their heads
T. Usmani.22:20: whereby everything in their bellies, as well as the skins, will be melted.
T. Usmani.22:21: And for them there are hooked rods of iron.
T. Usmani.22:22: Whenever, in their anguish, they will intend to come out of it (the fire), they will be turned back to it, and (it will be said to them,) “Taste the punishment of burning”.
T. Usmani.22:23: Surely Allah will admit those who believe and do good deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and with pearls, and their dress therein will be (of) silk.
T. Usmani.22:24: Guided they were to the good word (of faith) and guided they were to the path of (Allah,) the Praised One.
T. Usmani.22:25: Surely (We will punish) those who disbelieve and prevent (people) from the way of Allah and from Al-Masjid-ul-Harām (the Sacred Mosque), which We have made for all men, where residents and visitors are all equal. And whoever intends therein to commit deviation with injustice, We will make him taste a painful punishment.
T. Usmani.22:26: And (remember) when We pointed out for Ibrāhīm the place of the House (of Allah) saying, “Do not associate anything with Me as My partner, and purify My House for those who make Tawāf (circumambulation around it), and those who perform Qiyām (standing up in worship) and those who perform Rukū‘ (bowing down) and Sujūd (prostration),
T. Usmani.22:27: and announce among people about (the obligation of) Hajj, so that they should come to you on foot, and on every camel turned lean, traveling through every distant hilly pathway,
T. Usmani.22:28: so that they witness benefits for them, and recite Allah’s name in specified days, over the provision He gave them from the cattle. “So, eat thereof and feed the distressed, the poor.”
T. Usmani.22:29: Then, they must remove their dirt, and fulfill their vows, and make Tawāf of the Ancient House.”
T. Usmani.22:30: Having said that, whoever observes reverence of the things sanctified by Allah, it is good for him with his Lord. And permitted to you are the cattle, except those mentioned to you through recitation (of the verses). So refrain from the filth of the idols and refrain from a word of falsehood,
T. Usmani.22:31: standing upright for (the obedience of) Allah, not ascribing any partner to Him. Whoever ascribes a partner to Allah, it is as if he falls down from the sky, and either the birds snatch him, or the wind drives him away to a far off place.
T. Usmani.22:32: Having said that, if one observes the sanctity of the symbols of Allah, then such things emanate from the piety of the hearts.
T. Usmani.22:33: And for you there are benefits in them (the cattle) up to a specified time. Then their place of sacrifice is by the Ancient House.
T. Usmani.22:34: For every Ummah (religious community) We prescribed the act of sacrifice, so that they recite Allah’s name over the provision He gave them from the cattle. So, your God is One God. Therefore, to Him alone you must submit. And give good news to those who turn to Him with humbleness -
T. Usmani.22:35: those whose hearts are filled with awe when Allah is remembered, and who observe patience against whatever befalls them, and who are steadfast in Salāh, and who spend (in the way of Allah) out of what We have given to them.
T. Usmani.22:36: The big animals of sacrifice (like camels and cows) are made by Us among the symbols of Allah for you, in which there is much good for your benefit. So recite the name of Allah over them as they are lined up (for sacrifice). Then, once their flanks fall down (after slaughter), eat of them and feed the one who is content and the one who wishes to receive. Thus We have made them (the animals) subjugated to you, so that you may be grateful.
T. Usmani.22:37: It is neither their flesh nor their blood that reaches Allah, but what does reach Him is the taqwā (the sense of obedience) on your part. Thus He has made them (the animals) subjugated to you, so that you proclaim Allah’s glory for the guidance He gave you. And give good news to those who are good in their deeds.
T. Usmani.22:38: Surely, Allah defends those who believe. Allah does not love any treacherous, ungrateful.
T. Usmani.22:39: Permission (to fight) is given to those against whom fighting is launched, because they have been wronged, and Allah is powerful to give them victory.
T. Usmani.22:40: (They are) the ones who were expelled from their homes without any just reason, except that they say “Our Lord is Allah.” Had Allah not been repelling some people by means of some others, the monasteries, the churches, the synagogues and the mosques where Allah’s name is abundantly recited would have been demolished. Allah will definitely help those who help Him (by defending the religion prescribed by Him.) Surely Allah is Powerful, Mighty.
T. Usmani.22:41: (The ones who help Allah are) those who, when We give them power in the land, establish Salāh, pay Zakāh, bid what is Fair and forbid what is Unfair. And with Allah lies the fate of all matters.
T. Usmani.22:42: And if they reject you, so did reject the people of NūH (Noah) and ‘Ād and Thamūd,
T. Usmani.22:43: and the people of Ibrāhīm and the people of LūT (Lot),
T. Usmani.22:44: and the people of Madyan as well. Mūsā was (also) rejected. So, I gave some respite to the disbelievers, then seized them. So how was My censure?
T. Usmani.22:45: How many towns have We destroyed, as they were wrongdoers! So, they are fallen down on their roofs, and (how many a) deserted well and (how many a) well-built castle!
T. Usmani.22:46: Have they not, then, traveled on earth so that they should have had hearts to understand with, or ears to listen with? The fact is that it is not the eyes that turn blind, but what turns blind is the hearts contained in the chests.
T. Usmani.22:47: They ask you to bring the punishment sooner, while Allah will never go back on His promise. In fact, one day with your Lord is like one thousand years according to your calculation.
T. Usmani.22:48: And how many towns were there to whom I allowed respite, while they were wrongdoers, then I seized them. And to Me is the final return.
T. Usmani.22:49: Say, “O people, I am no more than a plain warner for you.
T. Usmani.22:50: So those who come to believe and do good deeds, for them there is forgiveness and dignified provision.
T. Usmani.22:51: As for those who strive against Our signs, trying to defeat (the prophet or the believers), they are the people of the Fire.”
T. Usmani.22:52: We did not send any messenger before you nor a prophet, but (he faced a situation that) when he recited (the revelation), the Satan cast (doubts in the hearts of his opponents) about what he recited. So, Allah nullifies what the Satan casts, then Allah makes His verses firm, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise
T. Usmani.22:53: (All this is allowed to be done) so that He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts there is a disease, and whose hearts are hard;-and surely the wrongdoers are in the utmost antagonism-
T. Usmani.22:54: and so that those who have been given knowledge may know that it (i.e. the revelation recited by the prophet) is the truth from your Lord, and they may believe in it and their hearts may become humble towards it. Allah is the Guide of the believers to the straight path.
T. Usmani.22:55: Those who disbelieve will remain in doubt about it (the Qur’ān) forever, until the Hour (of Judgment) comes upon them suddenly, or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day.
T. Usmani.22:56: The kingdom, on that day, is for Allah. He will judge between them. So, those who believed and did good deeds shall be in gardens of bliss.
T. Usmani.22:57: As for those who disbelieved and rejected Our signs, they are the ones for whom there is a humiliating punishment.
T. Usmani.22:58: Those who left their homeland in the way of Allah, then were slain or died, Allah will certainly give them a good provision, and surely, Allah is the best provider.
T. Usmani.22:59: He will definitely admit them to an entrance they will be pleased with, and Allah is surely All-Knowing, Forbearing.
T. Usmani.22:60: Having said this, whoever afflicts (someone) with a punishment equal to what he was afflicted with (by the latter), and still he (the former) is (again) subjected to aggression (by the latter), Allah will certainly help him. Indeed, Allah is Most-Pardoning, Most-Forgiving.
T. Usmani.22:61: That is because Allah makes night enter into the day and makes day enter into the night and that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
T. Usmani.22:62: That is because Allah is the truth and that whatever they invoke beside Him is false and that Allah is the High, the Great.
T. Usmani.22:63: Did you not see that Allah has sent down water from the sky, whereby the land becomes green? Surely, Allah is All-Kind, All-Aware.
T. Usmani.22:64: To Him belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth, and surely Allah is the All-Independent, Ever-Praised.
T. Usmani.22:65: Did you not see that Allah has subjugated to you everything on the earth, and the ships that sail at sea with His command? And He holds the sky so as it cannot fall on the earth except with His permission. Surely Allah is Very-Kind to the people, Very-Merciful.
T. Usmani.22:66: He is the One who gave life to you, then He brings death to you, then He will give you life (again). Surely, man is very ungrateful.
T. Usmani.22:67: For every Ummah (religious community) We have appointed a way of worship they are to observe. Therefore, they should never quarrel with you in the matter. And do call (them) to your Lord. Surely, you are on straight Guidance.
T. Usmani.22:68: And if they dispute with you, say (to them), “Allah is the best aware of what you do.”
T. Usmani.22:69: Allah will judge between you, on the Day of Judgment, about what you used to dispute.
T. Usmani.22:70: Do you not know that Allah knows all that is in the sky and the earth? Surely, that is contained in a Book. Indeed it is so easy for Allah.
T. Usmani.22:71: They worship, besides Allah, the objects for which He did never send down an authority (or proof) and about which they have no knowledge. And for the wrongdoers there is no helper.
T. Usmani.22:72: When Our verses are recited to them in all their clarity, you (can) recognize disgust on the faces of the disbelievers. They seem to attack those who recite to them Our verses. Say, “Shall I, then, tell you about something more disgusting than that? The Fire! Allah has promised it to those who disbelieve. And it is an evil end.”
T. Usmani.22:73: O people, here is a parable set forth to you, so listen to it carefully: All those whom you invoke besides Allah can never create (even) a fly, even though they all join hands together for that. And if a fly snatches something away from them, they cannot release it from its possession. (Equally) feeble are the invoker and the invoked.
T. Usmani.22:74: They did not recognize Allah in His true esteem. Indeed Allah is Powerful, Mighty.
T. Usmani.22:75: Allah chooses messengers from angels and from men. Surely, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
T. Usmani.22:76: He knows what is in front of them and what is behind them, and to Allah all matters are to be returned.
T. Usmani.22:77: O you who believe, bow down in Rukū‘ and bow down in Sajdah, and worship your Lord and do good deeds, so that you achieve success.
T. Usmani.22:78: Struggle for (seeking the pleasure of) Allah, a struggle that is owed to Him. He has chosen you and did not impose any hardship on you in the religion, the faith of your father Ibrāhīm. He (Allah) named you as Muslims earlier and also in this (Qur’ān), so that the Messenger becomes a witness to you, and you become witnesses to (other) people. So establish Salāh, pay Zakāh and hold fast to Allah. He is your patron. So, how excellent He is as a patron, and how excellent as a supporter!
T. Usmani.23:1: Success is really attained by the believers
T. Usmani.23:2: who concentrate their attention in humbleness when offering Salāh (prayers)
T. Usmani.23:3: and who keep themselves away from vain things,
T. Usmani.23:4: and who are performers of Zakāh ,
T. Usmani.23:5: and who guard their private parts
T. Usmani.23:6: except from their wives or from those (bondwomen who are) owned by their hands, as they are not to be blamed.
T. Usmani.23:7: However, those who seek (sexual pleasure) beyond that are the transgressors
T. Usmani.23:8: - and (success is attained) by those who honestly look after their trusts and covenant,
T. Usmani.23:9: and who consistently observe their prayers.
T. Usmani.23:11: who will inherit Firdaus (the Paradise). They will be there forever.
T. Usmani.23:12: We have created man from an extract of clay.
T. Usmani.23:13: Then We made him a sperm-drop in a firm resting place.
T. Usmani.23:14: Then We turned the sperm-drop into a clot, then We turned the clot into a fetus-lump, then We turned the fetus-lump into bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh; thereafter We developed it into another creature. So, glorious is Allah, the Best of the creators.
T. Usmani.23:15: Then, after all this, you are to die.
T. Usmani.23:16: Then you are to be raised again on the Day of Judgment.
T. Usmani.23:17: And We created above you seven paths (heavens), and We were never neglectful of the creation.
T. Usmani.23:18: And We sent down water from the sky in due measure, then We lodged it in the earth, and of course, We are able to take it away.
T. Usmani.23:19: Then We produced with it gardens of date-palms and vines for your benefit. For you there are many fruits in them, and of them you eat
T. Usmani.23:20: - and (We produced) a tree (of olive) that comes forth from the (mount) Tūr of Sinai, which grows with oil and with a dressing for those who eat.
T. Usmani.23:21: And indeed there is a sure lesson in the cattle for you. We give you a drink from that which lies in their bellies, and for you there are many benefits in them, and of them you eat,
T. Usmani.23:22: and on them and on the boats you are transported.
T. Usmani.23:23: Surely, We sent NūH to his nation. So he said, “My people, worship Allah. You have no god whatsoever other than Him. So, do you not fear Allah?”
T. Usmani.23:24: So, said the disbelieving chiefs from among his nation, “This (man) is nothing but a human being like you. He wishes to impose his superiority over you. Had Allah willed, He would have sent down angels (instead of him). We have not heard of such a thing among our forefathers.
T. Usmani.23:25: He is none but a man suffering from madness; so wait for (what happens to) him until some time”
T. Usmani.23:26: He said, “My Lord, help me, for they have rejected me.”
T. Usmani.23:27: So, We sent Our revelation to him, saying, “Make the ship under Our eyes and Our revelation. So, when Our command will come, and the oven will gush forth, take on its board a pair of two from each (species) along with your family, except those of them against whom the word has already come to pass. And do not speak to Me (in favor) of those who have done wrong. They are sure to be drowned.
T. Usmani.23:28: So, when you and those with you are well seated in the ship, say, ‘Praise is for Allah who saved us from the wrongdoing people.’
T. Usmani.23:29: And say, ‘My Lord, make me land a blessed landing, and You are the best of those who bring (someone) to land’”.
T. Usmani.23:30: Surely, there are signs in it, and We do always test (people).
T. Usmani.23:31: Then after them We created another generation,
T. Usmani.23:32: and sent among them a messenger from themselves (to convey the message): “Worship Allah; you have no god whatsoever other than Him. So do you not fear Allah?”
T. Usmani.23:33: Then said the chiefs of his nation who were disbelievers and who denied facing the Hereafter and whom We made affluent in the worldly life, “This (man) is nothing but a human being. He eats from what you eat from, and drinks from what you drink.
T. Usmani.23:34: If you obey a human like yourselves, then you will be absolute losers.
T. Usmani.23:35: Does he promise you that, when you die and are turned into dust and bones, you are to be brought forth?
T. Usmani.23:36: Far too improbable is what you are being promised.
T. Usmani.23:37: There is nothing but our worldly life. We die and we live, and we are not to be raised again.
T. Usmani.23:38: He is nothing but a man who has forged a lie against Allah, and we are not going to believe in him.”
T. Usmani.23:39: He said, “My Lord, help me, for they have rejected me.”
T. Usmani.23:40: He (Allah) said, “In a little while they will have to be remorseful.”
T. Usmani.23:41: So the Cry seized them according to the true (promise), and We turned them in to scum. So, away with the wrongdoing people.
T. Usmani.23:42: Then, after them, We created another generation.
T. Usmani.23:43: No community can go ahead of its appointed time, nor can they become late.
T. Usmani.23:44: Thereafter, We sent Our messengers successively. Whenever its messenger came to a community, they rejected him. Then We made some of them follow others (in destruction) and turned them into tales (of history). So, away with a people who do not believe.
T. Usmani.23:45: Thereafter, We sent Mūsā and his brother Hārūn with Our signs and a clear proof
T. Usmani.23:46: towards Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) and his advisors. But they showed arrogance and they were haughty people.
T. Usmani.23:47: So they said, “shall we believe in two humans who are like ourselves and whose people are serving us as slaves?”
T. Usmani.23:48: Thus they rejected both of them and were among the destroyed.
T. Usmani.23:49: And, of course, We gave Mūsā the Book, so that they may take the right path.
T. Usmani.23:50: And We made the son of Maryam (Mary) and his mother a sign, and gave them shelter on a height, having a place of rest and running springs.
T. Usmani.23:51: O messengers, eat from the good things, and act righteously. Of whatever you do, I am fully aware.
T. Usmani.23:52: Surely, this is your creed, a single creed, and I am your Lord. So fear Me.
T. Usmani.23:53: But they split up ways from one another (dividing themselves) into factions, each faction happy with what lies before it.
T. Usmani.23:54: So leave them in their negligence for some time.
T. Usmani.23:55: Do they think that by consistently providing them with wealth and children,
T. Usmani.23:56: We are accelerating the (real) good things to them? The fact, however, is that they do not understand (the reality).
T. Usmani.23:57: (Contrarily) those who are anxious out of awe of their Lord,
T. Usmani.23:58: and those who believe in the verses of their Lord
T. Usmani.23:59: and those who do not associate any partner to their Lord,
T. Usmani.23:60: And those who give whatever they give, with their hearts full of fear that to their Lord they are to return
T. Usmani.23:61: - those people are accelerating towards the (real) good things, and they are the foremost to attain them.
T. Usmani.23:62: We do not place a burden on anyone except according to his ability. With Us there is a book which speaks with truth, and they shall not be wronged.
T. Usmani.23:63: But their hearts are in ignorance about this, and they have deeds, other than that, which they are continuously doing.
T. Usmani.23:64: Until when We will seize their affluent ones with punishment, they will suddenly start crying.
T. Usmani.23:65: (Then it will be said to them,) “Do not cry today. You will not be helped by Us.
T. Usmani.23:66: My verses used to be recited to you, but you used to turn back on your heels
T. Usmani.23:67: in arrogance, making it a subject of tales at night, talking nonsense (about it).”
T. Usmani.23:68: Then, is it that they did not ponder over the Word (of Allah), or there has come to them something that did not come to their forefathers?
T. Usmani.23:69: Or did they not recognize their messenger and therefore they denied him?
T. Usmani.23:70: Or do they say, “He is suffering from madness?” No, but he has come to them with truth, but it is the truth that most of them dislike.
T. Usmani.23:71: Had the truth followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and all those therein would have fallen in total disorder. However, We have brought to them their advice, but it is their advice that they are averse to.
T. Usmani.23:72: Or is it that you (O Prophet) demand remuneration from them? But the remuneration from your Lord is best, and He is the best of all givers.
T. Usmani.23:73: Surely you are inviting them to a straight path,
T. Usmani.23:74: and those who do not believe in the Hereafter are surely the deviators from the Path.
T. Usmani.23:75: And if We have mercy on them and remove whatever distress they have, they would still persist obstinately in their rebellion, wandering blindly (in disbelief).
T. Usmani.23:76: We have already seized them with punishment, but they did not turn humble to their Lord, nor do they supplicate in humility,
T. Usmani.23:77: until when We will open against them the door of a severe punishment, they will be taken aback in despair.
T. Usmani.23:78: He is the One who created for you ears and eyes and hearts. Little you are grateful.
T. Usmani.23:79: And He is the One who created you on the earth, and it is He unto whom you will be gathered together.
T. Usmani.23:80: And He is the One who gives life and brings death, and it is He who controls the alternation of night and day. So, do you not understand?
T. Usmani.23:81: But they say as the earlier people had said.
T. Usmani.23:82: They said, “Is it that, when we will die and become dust and bones - is it that we will be raised again?
T. Usmani.23:83: This is what has been promised to us and to our fathers before. It is nothing but the tales of the ancients.”
T. Usmani.23:84: Say, “Whose is the earth and all those therein if you have knowledge?”
