A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:83: Whenever We bestow favours upon man, he arrogantly turns away and draws aside; and whenever evil visits him, he is in utter despair.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:84: Say, (O Prophet): "Each one acts according to his own manner. Your Lord knows well who is best-guided to the Right Path."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:85: They ask you about "the spirit". Say: "The spirit descends by the command of my Lord, but you have been given only a little knowledge."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:86: Had We willed, We could take away what We have revealed to you, then you would find none to help you in recovering it from Us.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:87: (Whatever you have received) is nothing but grace from your Lord. Indeed His favour to you is great.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:88: Say: "Surely, if mankind and jinn were to get together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they will never be able to produce the like of it, howsoever they might help one another."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:89: We have explained things for people in this Qur'an in diverse ways to make them understand the Message, yet most people obstinately persist in unbelief.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:90: They said: "We shall not accept your Message until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:91: or that there be a garden of palms and vines for you and then you cause rivers to abundantly flow forth through them;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:92: or cause the sky to fall on us in pieces as you claimed, or bring Allah and the angels before us, face to face;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:93: or that there come to be for you a house of gold, or that you ascend to the sky - though we shall not believe in your ascension (to the sky) - until you bring down a book for us that we can read." Say to them, (O Muhammad): "Holy is my Lord! Am I anything else than a human being, who bears a Message (from Allah)?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:94: Whenever Guidance came to people, nothing prevented them from believing except that they said: "Has Allah sent a human being as a Messenger?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:95: Say: "Had angels been walking about in peace on the earth, We would surely have sent to them an angel from the heavens as Messenger."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:96: Tell them, (O Prophet): "Allah suffices as a witness between me and you. Allah is well aware and fully observes everything pertaining to His servants."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:97: Whomsoever Allah guides is rightly guided; and whomsoever Allah lets go astray, you shall find none - apart from Him - who could protect him. We shall muster them all on the Day of Resurrection, on their faces - blind and dumb and deaf. Hell shall be their refuge. Every time its Fire subsides, We will intensify for them its flame.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:98: That will be their recompense because they disbelieved in Our Signs and said: "What, when we shall be reduced to bones and particles (of dust), shall we be raised again as a new creation?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:99: Have they not perceived that Allah, Who has created the heavens and the earth, has the power to create the like of them? He has fixed a term for them about which there is no doubt. And yet the wrong-doers obstinately persist in unbelief.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:100: Tell them, (O Prophet): "Even if you owned the treasures of my Lord's Mercy you would have held them back for fear of spending them." Man is indeed ever niggardly.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:101: We granted Moses nine clear signs. Ask the Children of Israel about that: when these signs came forth, Pharaoh said to him: "Moses, I think that you are bewitched."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:102: Moses replied: "You know well that no one but the Lord of the heavens and the earth has sent these as eye-opening proofs. I truly think, O Pharaoh, that you are indeed doomed."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:103: At last Pharaoh decided to uproot Moses and the Children of Israel from the land, but We drowned him together with all who were with him;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:104: and thereafter We said to the Children of Israel: "Now dwell in the land, but when the promised time of the Hereafter comes, We shall bring you all together."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:105: We have sent down the Qur'an with the Truth, and it is with the Truth that it has descended. And We have not sent you but to proclaim good news and to warn.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:106: We have revealed the Qur'an in parts that you may recite it to people slowly and with deliberation; and (for that reason) We have revealed it gradually (to suit particular occasions).
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:107: Tell them, (O Prophet): "Whether you believe in it, or do not believe," but when it is recited to those who were given the knowledge before its revelation, they fall down upon their faces in prostration
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:108: and say: "Glory be to our Lord. Surely the promise of our Lord was bound to be fulfilled."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:109: And they fall down upon their faces, weeping, and their humility increases when (the Qur'an) is recited to them.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:110: Say to them (O Prophet!): "Call upon Him as Allah or call upon Him as al-Rahman; call Him by whichever name you will, all His names are beautiful. Neither offer your Prayer in too loud a voice, nor in a voice too low; but follow a middle course."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).17:111: And say: "All praise be to Allah Who has neither taken to Himself a son, nor has He any partner in His kingdom, nor does He need anyone, out of weakness, to protect Him." So glorify Him in a manner worthy of His glory.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:1: Praise be to Allah Who has revealed to His servant the Book devoid of all crookedness;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:2: an unerringly Straight Book, meant to warn of a stern punishment from Allah, and to proclaim, to those who believe and work righteous deeds, the tiding that theirs shall be a good reward
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:3: wherein they shall abide for ever;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:4: and also to warn those who say: "Allah has taken to Himself a son,"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:5: a thing about which they have no knowledge, neither they nor their ancestors. Dreadful is the word that comes out of their mouths. What they utter is merely a lie.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:6: (O Muhammad), if they do not believe in this Message, you will perhaps torment yourself to death with grief, sorrowing over them.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:7: Surely We have made all that is on the earth an embellishment for it in order to test people as to who of them is better in conduct.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:8: In the ultimate, We shall reduce all that is on the earth to a barren plain.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:9: Do you think that the people of the Cave and the Inscription were one of Our wondrous signs?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:10: When those youths sought refuge in the Cave and said: "Our Lord! Grant us mercy from Yourself and provide for us rectitude in our affairs."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:11: We lulled them to sleep in that cave for a number of years
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:12: and then roused them so that We might see which of the two parties could best tell the length of their stay.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:13: We narrate to you their true story. They were a party of young men who had faith in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:14: and strengthened their hearts when they stood up and proclaimed: "Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We shall call upon no other god beside Him; (for if we did so), we shall be uttering a blasphemy."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:15: (Then they conferred among themselves and said): "These men, our own people, have taken others as gods beside Him: why do they not bring any clear evidence that they indeed are gods? Who can be more unjust than he who foists a lie on Allah?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:16: And now that you have dissociated yourselves from them and from whatever they worship beside Allah, go and seek refuge in the Cave. Your Lord will extend His mercy to you and will provide for you the means for the disposal of your affairs."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:17: Had you seen them in the Cave it would have appeared to you that when the sun rose, it moved away from their Cave to the right; and when it set, it turned away from them to the left, while they remained in a spacious hollow in the Cave. This is one of the Signs of Allah. Whomsoever Allah guides, he alone is led aright; and whomsoever Allah lets go astray, you will find for him no guardian to direct him.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:18: On seeing them you would fancy them to be awake though they were asleep; and We caused them to turn their sides to their right and to their left, and their dog sat stretching out its forelegs on the threshold of the Cave. Had you looked upon them you would have certainly fled away from them, their sight filling you with terror.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:19: Likewise, We roused them in a miraculous way that they might question one another. One of them asked: "How long did you remain (in this state)?" The others said: "We remained so for a day or part of a day." Then they said: "Your Lord knows better how long we remained in this state. Now send one of you to the city with this coin of yours and let him see who has the best food, and let him buy some provisions from there. Let him be cautious and not inform anyone of our whereabouts.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:20: For if they should come upon us, they will stone us to death or force us to revert to their faith whereafter we shall never prosper."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:21: Thus did We make their case known to the people of the city so that they might know that Allah's promise is true, and that there is absolutely no doubt that the Hour will come to pass. But instead of giving thought to this, they disputed with one another concerning the People of the Cave, some saying: "Build a wall over them. Their Lord alone knows best about them." But those who prevailed over their affairs said: "We shall build a place of worship over them."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:22: Some will say concerning them: "They were three and their dog, the fourth"; and some will say: "They were five, and their dog, the sixth" � all this being merely guesswork; and still others will say: "They were seven, and their dog, the eighth." Say: "My Lord knows their number best. Only a few know their correct number. So do not dispute concerning their number, but stick to what is evident, and do not question anyone about them."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:23: And never say about anything: "I shall certainly do this tomorrow"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:24: unless Allah should will it. And should you forget (and make such a statement), remember your Lord and say: "I expect my Lord to guide me to what is nearer to rectitude than this."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:25: They remained in the Cave for three hundred years; and others added nine more years.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:26: Say: "Allah knows best how long they remained in it, for only He knows all that is hidden in the heavens and the earth. How well He sees; how well He hears! The creatures have no other guardian than Him; He allows none to share His authority."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:27: (O Prophet), recite to them from the Book of your Lord what has been revealed to you for none may change His words; (and were you to make any change in His words) you will find no refuge from Him.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:28: Keep yourself content with those who call upon their Lord, morning and evening, seeking His pleasure, and do not let your eyes pass beyond them. Do you seek the pomp and glitter of the world? Do not follow him whose heart We have caused to be heedless of Our remembrance, and who follows his desires, and whose attitude is of excess.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:29: And proclaim: "This is the Truth from your Lord. Now let him who will, believe; and let him who will, disbelieve. We have prepared a Fire for the wrong-doers whose billowing folds encompass them. If they ask for water, they will be served with a drink like dregs of oil that will scald their faces. How dreadful a drink, and how evil an abode!
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:30: As for those who believe and do good We shall not cause their reward to be lost.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:31: They shall dwell in the Gardens of Eternity, beneath which streams flow. There they will be adorned with bracelets of gold, will be arrayed in green garments of silk and rich brocade, and will recline on raised couches. How excellent is their reward, and how nice their resting-place!"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:32: (O Muhammad), propound a parable to them. There were two men of whom We bestowed upon one of the two vineyards, surrounding both of them with date-palms and putting a tillage in between.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:33: Both the vineyards yielded abundant produce without failure and We caused a stream to flow in their midst
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:34: so the owner had fruit in abundance and he said to his neighbour, while conversing with him: "I have greater wealth than you and I am stronger than you in numbers."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:35: Then he entered his vine-yard and said, wronging himself: "Surely, I do not believe that all this will ever perish.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:36: Nor do I believe that the Hour of Resurrection will ever come to pass. And even if I am returned to my Lord, I shall find a better place than this."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:37: While conversing with him his neighbour exclaimed: "Do you deny Him Who created you out of dust, then out of a drop of sperm, and then fashioned you into a complete man?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:38: As for myself, Allah alone is my Lord, and I associate none with my Lord in His Divinity.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:39: When you entered your vineyard, why did you not say: 'Whatever Allah wills shall come to pass, for there is no power save with Allah!' If you find me less than yourself in wealth and children
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:40: it may well be that my Lord will give me something better than your vineyard, and send a calamity upon your vineyard from the heavens and it will be reduced to a barren waste,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:41: or the water of your vineyard will be drained deep into the ground so that you will not be able to seek it out."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:42: Eventually all his produce was destroyed and he began to wring his hands in sorrow at the loss of what he had spent on it, and on seeing it fallen down upon its trellises, saying: "Would I had not associated anyone with my Lord in His Divinity."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:43: And there was no host, beside Allah, to help him, nor could he be of any help to himself.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:44: (Then he knew) that all power of protection rests with Allah, the True One. He is the best to reward, the best to determine the end of things.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:45: (O Prophet), propound to them the parable of the present life: it is like the vegetation of the earth which flourished luxuriantly when it mingled with the water that We sent down from the sky, but after that the same vegetation turned into stubble which the winds blew about. Allah alone has the power over all things.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:46: Wealth and children are an adornment of the life of the world. But the deeds of lasting righteousness are the best in the sight of your Lord in reward, and far better a source of hope.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:47: Bear in mind the Day when We shall set the mountains in motion and you will find the earth void and bare. On that Day We shall muster all men together, leaving none of them behind.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:48: They shall be brought before your Lord, all lined up, and shall be told: "Now, indeed, you have come before Us in the manner We created you in the first instance, although you thought that We shall not appoint a tryst (with Us)."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:49: And then the Record of their deeds shall be placed before them and you will see the guilty full of fear for what it contains, and will say: "Woe to us! What a Record this is! It leaves nothing, big or small, but encompasses it." They will find their deeds confronting them. Your Lord wrongs no one.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:50: And recall when We said to the angels: "Prostrate yourselves before Adam"; all of them fell prostrate, except Iblis. He was of the jinn and so disobeyed the command of his Lord. Will you, then, take him and his progeny as your guardians rather than Me although they are your open enemies? What an evil substitute are these wrong-doers taking!
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:51: I did not call them to witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor in their own creation. I do not seek the aid of those who lead people astray.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:52: What will such people do on the Day when the Lord will say: "Now call upon all those whom you believed to be My partners?" Thereupon they will call upon them, but they will not respond to their call; and We shall make them a common pit of doom,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:53: and the guilty shall behold the Fire and know that they are bound to fall into it, and will find no escape from it.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:54: And surely We have explained matters to people in the Qur'an in diverse ways, using all manner of parables. But man is exceedingly contentious.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:55: What is it that prevented mankind from believing when the guidance came to them, and from asking forgiveness of their Lord, except that they would like to be treated as the nations of yore, or that they would like to see the scourge come upon them face to face?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:56: We raise Messengers only to give good news and to warn. But the unbelievers resort to falsehood in order to rebut the truth with it, and scoff at My revelations and My warnings.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:57: Who is more wicked than the man who, when he is reminded by the revelations of his Lord, turns away from them and forgets (the consequence of) the deeds wrought by his own hands? We have laid veils over their hearts lest they understand the message of the Qur'an, and We have caused heaviness in their ears. Call them as you may to the Right Path, they will not be ever guided aright.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:58: Your Lord is All-Forgiving, full of mercy. Had He wished to take them to task for their doings, He would have hastened in sending His scourge upon them. But He has set for them a time-limit which they cannot evade.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:59: All the townships afflicted with scourge are before your eyes. When they committed wrong, We destroyed them. For the destruction of each We had set a definite term.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:60: (And recount to them the story of Moses) when Moses said to his servant: "I will journey on until I reach the point where the two rivers meet, though I may march on for ages."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:61: But when they reached the point where the two rivers meet, they forgot their fish, and it took its way into the sea, as if through a tunnel.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:62: When they had journeyed further on, Moses said to his servant: "Bring us our repast. We are surely fatigued by today's journey."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:63: The servant said: "Did you see what happened? When we betook ourselves to the rock to take rest, I forgot the fish � and it is only Satan who caused me to forget to mention it to you � so that it made its way into the sea in a strange manner."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:64: Moses said: "That is what we were looking for." So the two turned back, retracing their footsteps,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:65: and there they found one of Our servants upon whom We had bestowed Our mercy, and to whom We had imparted a special knowledge from Ourselves.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:66: Moses said to him: "May l follow you that you may teach me something of the wisdom which you have been taught?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:67: He answered: "You will surely not be able to bear with me.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:68: For how can you patiently bear with something you cannot encompass in your knowledge?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:69: Moses replied: "You shall find me, if Allah wills, patient; and I shall not disobey you in anything."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:70: He said: "Well, if you follow me, do not ask me concerning anything until I myself mention it to you."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:71: Then the two went forth until, when they embarked on the boat, he made a hole in it, whereupon Moses exclaimed: "Have you made a hole in it so as to drown the people in the boat? You have certainly done an awful thing."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:72: He replied: "Did I not tell you that you will not be able to patiently bear with me?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:73: Moses said: "Do not take me to task at my forgetfulness, and do not be hard on me."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:74: Then the two went forth until they met a lad whom he slew, whereupon Moses exclaimed: "What! Have you slain an innocent person without his having slain anyone? Surely you have done a horrible thing."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:75: He said: "Did I not tell you that you will not be able to patiently bear with me?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:76: Moses said: "Keep me no more in your company if I question you concerning anything after this. You will then be fully justified."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:77: Then the two went forth until when they came to a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to play host to them. They found in that town a wall that was on the verge of tumbling down, and he buttressed it, whereupon Moses said: "If you had wished, you could have received payment for it."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:78: He said: "This brings me and you to a parting of ways. Now I shall explain to you the true meaning of things about which you could not remain patient.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:79: As for the boat it belonged to some poor people who worked on the river, and I desired to damage it for beyond them lay the dominion of a king who was wont to seize every boat by force.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:80: As for the lad, his parents were people of faith, and we feared lest he should plague them with transgression and disbelief,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:81: and we desired that their Lord should grant them another in his place, a son more upright and more tender hearted.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:82: As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and under it there was a treasure that belonged to them. Their father was a righteous man and your Lord intended that they should come of age and then bring forth their treasure as a mercy from your Lord; I did not do this of my own bidding. This is the true meaning of things with which you could not keep your patience."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:83: (O Muhammad), they ask you about Dhu al-Qarnayn. Say: "I will give you an account of him."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:84: We granted him power in the land and endowed him with all kinds of resources.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:85: He set out (westwards) on an expedition,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:86: until when he reached the very limits where the sun sets, he saw it setting in dark turbid waters; and nearby he met a people. We said: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, you have the power to punish or to treat them with kindness."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:87: He said: "We will chastise him who does wrong, whereafter he will be returned to his Lord and He will chastise him grievously.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:88: But as for him who believes and acts righteously, his will be a goodly reward and we shall enjoin upon him only mild commands."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:89: Then he set out on another expedition
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:90: until he reached the limit where the sun rises and he found it rising on a people whom We had provided no shelter from it.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:91: Thus was the state of those people, and We encompassed in knowledge all concerning Dhu al- Qarnayn.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:92: Then he set out on another expedition
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:93: until when he reached a place between the two mountains, he found beside the mountains a people who scarcely understood anything.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:94: They said: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, Gog and Magog are spreading corruption in this land. So shall we pay you taxes on the understanding that you will set up a barrier between us and them?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:95: He answered: "Whatever my Lord has granted me is good enough. But help me with your labour and I will erect a rampart between you and them.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:96: Bring me ingots of iron." Then after he had filled up the space between the two mountain-sides, he said: "(Light a fire) and ply bellows." When he had made it (red like) fire, he said: "Bring me molten copper which I may pour on it."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:97: Such was the rampart that Gog and Magog could not scale, nor could they pierce it.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:98: Dhu al-Qarnayn said: "This is a mercy from my Lord: but when the time of my Lord's promise shall come, He will level the rampart with the ground. My Lord's promise always comes true."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:99: And on that Day We shall let some of them surge like waves against others, and the Trumpet shall be blown. Then We shall gather them all together.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:100: That will be the Day We shall place Hell before the unbelievers
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:101: whose eyes had become blind against My admonition and who were utterly disinclined to hear it.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:102: Do the unbelievers, then, believe that they can take any of My creatures as their guardians beside Me? Verily We have prepared Hell to welcome the unbelievers.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:103: Say, (O Muhammad): "Shall We tell you who will be the greatest losers in respect of their works?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:104: It will be those whose effort went astray in the life of the world and who believe nevertheless that they are doing good.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:105: Those are the ones who refused to believe in the revelations of their Lord and that they are bound to meet Him. Hence, all their deeds have come to naught, and We shall assign no weight to them on the Day of Resurrection.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:106: Hell is their recompense for disbelieving and their taking My revelations and My Messengers as objects of jest.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:107: As for those who believe and do good works, the Gardens of Paradise shall be there to welcome them;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:108: there they will abide for ever, with no desire to be removed from there."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:109: Say: "If the sea were to become ink to record the Words of my Lord, indeed the sea would be all used up before the Words of my Lord are exhausted, and it would be the same even if We were to bring an equal amount of ink."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).18:110: Say (O Muhammad): "I am no more than a human being like you; one to whom revelation is made: 'Your Lord is the One and Only God.' Hence, whoever looks forward to meet his Lord, let him do righteous works, and let him associate none with the worship of his Lord."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:2: This is an account of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zechariah
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:3: when he cried to his Lord in secret.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:4: He said: "Lord! My bones have grown feeble and my head is glistening with age; yet, never have my prayers to You, my Lord, been unfruitful.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:5: I fear evil from my kinsmen after I am gone; and my wife is barren, so grant me an heir out of Your special grace,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:6: one that might be my heir and the heir of the house of Jacob; and make him, Lord, one that will be pleasing to You.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:7: (He was told): "Zechariah, We bring you the good news of the birth of a son whose name shall be Yahya (John), one whose namesake We never created before."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:8: He said: "My Lord! How can I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached an extremely old age?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:9: He answered: "So shall it be." Your Lord says: "It is easy for Me," and then added: "For beyond doubt, I created you earlier when you were nothing."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:10: Zechariah said: "Lord, grant me a Sign." Said He: "Your Sign is that you shall not be able to speak to people for three nights, though you will be otherwise sound."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:11: Thereupon Zechariah came out from the sanctuary and directed his people by gestures to extol His glory by day and by night.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:12: "O John! Hold the Book with all your strength." We had bestowed wisdom upon him while he was still a child;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:13: and We also endowed him with tenderness and purity, and he was exceedingly pious
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:14: and cherishing to his parents. Never was he insolent or rebellious.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:15: Peace be upon him the day he was born, and the day he will die, and the day he will be raised up alive.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:16: (O Muhammad), recite in the Book the account of Mary, when she withdrew from her people to a place towards the east;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:17: and drew a curtain, screening herself from people whereupon We sent to her Our spirit and he appeared to her as a well-shaped man.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:18: Mary exclaimed: "I surely take refuge from you with the Most Compassionate Lord, if you are at all God-fearing."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:19: He said: "I am just a message-bearer of your Lord, I have come to grant you a most pure boy."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:20: Mary said: "How can a boy be born to me when no man has even touched me, nor have I ever been unchaste?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:21: The angel said: "Thus shall it be. Your Lord says: 'It is easy for Me; and We shall do so in order to make him a Sign for mankind and a mercy from Us. This has been decreed.' "
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:22: Then she conceived him and withdrew with him to a far-off place.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:23: Then the birth pangs drove her to the trunk of a palm-tree and she said: "Oh, would that I had died before this and had been all forgotten."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:24: Thereupon the angel below her cried out: "Grieve not, for your Lord has caused a stream of water to flow beneath you.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:25: Shake the trunk of the palm-tree towards yourself and fresh and ripe dates shall fall upon you.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:26: So eat and drink and cool your eyes; and if you see any person say to him: 'Verily I have vowed a fast to the Most Compassionate Lord, and so I shall not speak to anyone today.' "
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:27: Then she came to her people, carrying her baby. They said: "O Mary! You have committed a monstrous thing.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:28: O sister of Aaron! Your father was not an evil man, nor was your mother an unchaste woman."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:29: Thereupon Mary pointed to the child. They exclaimed: "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a mere child?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:30: The child cried out: "Verily I am Allah's servant. He has granted me the Book and has made me a Prophet
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:31: and has blessed me wherever I might be and has enjoined upon me Prayer and Zakah (purifying alms) as long as I live;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:32: and has made me dutiful to my mother. He has not made me oppressive, nor bereft of God's blessings.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:33: Peace be upon me the day I was born and the day I will die, and the day I will be raised up alive."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:34: This is Jesus, the son of Mary; and this is the truth about him concerning which they are in doubt.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:35: It does not befit Allah to take for Himself a son. Glory be to Him! When He decrees a thing He only says: "Be" and it is.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:36: (Jesus had said): "Indeed Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so serve Him alone. This is the Straight Way."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:37: But different parties began to dispute with one another. A dreadful woe awaits on that great Day for those that reject the Truth.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:38: How well shall they hear and how well shall they see on the Day they come to Us! But today the evil-doers are in manifest error.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:39: (O Muhammad), warn those who are steeped in heedlessness and are obstinately rejecting the truth that the Day shall come when things will be finally decided and they shall be left with utter remorse.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:40: Ultimately, We shall inherit the earth and whatever is on it; to Us shall they be returned.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:41: (O Muhammad), recite in the Book the account of Abraham. Most surely he was a man of truth, a Prophet.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:42: (And remind people) when he said to his father: "Father! Why do you worship that which neither sees nor hears, and which can be of no avail to you?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:43: Father, a knowledge that has not reached you has come to me. So follow me that I may guide you to a Straight Way.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:44: Father, do not serve Satan, for Satan has indeed been a persistent rebel against the Most Compassionate Lord.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:45: Father, I fear that a punishment from the Most Compassionate Lord might strike you and you may end up as one of Satan's companions?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:46: The father said: "Abraham, have you turned away from my gods? If you do not give this up, I shall stone you to death. Now begone from me forever."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:47: Abraham answered: "Peace be upon you. I shall seek pardon for you from my Lord. My Lord has always been kind to Me.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:48: I shall withdraw from you and all that you call upon beside Allah. I shall only call upon my Lord. I trust the prayer to my Lord will not go unanswered."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:49: Thereupon Abraham dissociated himself from his people and the deities they worshipped instead of Allah, and We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob and made each of them a Prophet;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:50: and We bestowed on them Our mercy, and granted them a truly lofty renown.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:51: And recite in the Book the account of Moses. He was a chosen one, a Messenger, a Prophet.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:52: We called out to him from the right side of the Mount, and We drew him near to Us by communing to him in secret,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:53: and out of Our mercy We appointed his brother Aaron, a Prophet (that he may assist him).
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:54: And recite in the Book the account of Ishmael. He was ever true to his promise, and was a Messenger, a Prophet.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:55: He enjoined his household to observe Prayer and to give Zakah (purifying alms); and his Lord was well pleased with him.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:56: And recite in the Book the account of Idris. He was a man of truth, a Prophet;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:57: and We exalted him to a lofty position.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:58: These are the Prophets upon whom Allah bestowed His favour from the seed of Adam, and from the seed of those whom We carried (in the Ark) with Noah, and from the seed of Abraham and Israel. They were those whom We guided and chose (for an exalted position). They were such that when the words of the Most Compassionate Lord were recited to them, they fell down in prostration, weeping.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:59: They were succeeded by a people who neglected the Prayers and pursued their lusts. They shall presently meet with their doom,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:60: except those who repent and believe and act righteously. Such shall enter Paradise and shall not be wronged at all.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:61: Theirs shall be everlasting Gardens which the Most Compassionate Lord has promised His servants in a realm which is beyond the ken of perception. Surely His promise shall he fulfilled.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:62: They shall not hear in it anything vain; they shall hear only what is good; and they shall have their provision in it, morning and evening.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:63: Such is the Paradise which We shall cause those of Our servants who have been God-fearing to inherit.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:64: (The angels will say): "(O Muhammad!) We descend not except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs all that is before us and all that is behind us, and all that is in between. Your Lord is not forgetful in the least.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:65: He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is in between. Serve Him, then, and be constant in serving Him. Do you know anyone that might be His compeer?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:66: Man is prone to say: "Shall I be raised to life after I die?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:67: Does man not remember that We created him before when he was nothing?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:68: By your Lord, We will surely muster them and the devils together. Then We will surely bring them all, on their knees, around Hell,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:69: and then We will draw aside from each party those who were most rebellious against the Most Compassionate Lord,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:70: and then We shall know well all those most worthy to be cast in Hell.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:71: There is not one of you but shall pass by Hell. This is a decree which your Lord will fulfil.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:72: Then We shall deliver those that feared Allah and leave the wrong-doers there on their knees.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:73: When Our clear revelations are recited to those who deny the Truth they are wont to say to those who have faith: "Which of the two groups has a better status and whose assemblies are grander?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:74: How numerous are the peoples We destroyed before them - those that were more resourceful and grander in outward appearance!
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:75: Say: "The Most Compassionate Lord grants respite to those who stray into error, until they behold what they had been threatened with, either God's chastisement (in the world) or the Hour (of Resurrection)" - then they fully know whose station is worse, and who is weaker in hosts!
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:76: (On the contrary), Allah increases in guidance those who follow the Right Way. Lasting acts of righteousness are better in the sight of your Lord as reward and conducive to a better end.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:77: Have you seen him who rejected Our signs and said: "Surely I shall continue to be favoured with riches and children."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:78: Has he obtained knowledge of the Unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Compassionate Lord?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:79: By no means! We shall write down all what he says; and We shall greatly prolong his chastisement,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:80: and We shall inherit all the resources and hosts of which he boasts, and he will come to Us all alone.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:81: They have taken other gods instead of Allah that they may be a source of strength for them.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:82: By no means! They shall soon deny their worship and shall become their adversaries instead.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:83: Do you not see that We have sent devils upon the unbelievers who greatly incite them (to oppose the Truth)?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:84: Therefore, do not hasten (in seeking a scourge against them). We are counting their days.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:85: The Day shall soon come when We shall bring together the God-fearing to the Most Compassionate Lord, as honoured guests;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:86: and We shall drive the guilty ones to Hell as a thirsty herd.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:87: On that Day none will have the power to intercede for them except those who received a sanction from the Most Compassionate Lord.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:88: They claim: "The Most Compassionate Lord has taken a son to Himself."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:89: Surely you have made a monstrous statement.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:90: It is such a monstrosity that heavens might well-nigh burst forth at it, the earth might be cleaved, and the mountains fall
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:91: at their ascribing a son to the Most Compassionate Lord.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:92: It does not befit the Most Compassionate Lord that He should take a son.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:93: There is no one in the heavens and the earth but he shall come to the Most Compassionate Lord as His servant.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:94: Verily He encompasses them and has counted them all.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:95: On the Day of Resurrection each one of these will come to Him singly.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:96: Indeed, the Most Compassionate Lord will soon create enduring love for those who believe and do righteous works.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:97: Therefore, We have revealed the Qur'an in your tongue and made it easy to understand that you may give glad tidings to the God-fearing and warn a contentious people.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).19:98: How numerous are the peoples that We destroyed before them! Do you now perceive any one of them, or hear even their whisper?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:2: We did not reveal the Qur'an to you to cause you distress;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:3: it is only a reminder for him who fears Allah;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:4: a revelation from Him Who created the earth and the high heavens.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:5: The Most Compassionate Lord is settled on the Throne (of the Universe).
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:6: To Him belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth, and all that is in between, and all that is beneath the soil.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:7: Whether you speak out aloud (or in a low voice), He knows what is said secretly, and even that which is most hidden.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:8: Allah - there is no god but He. His are the most excellent names.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:9: Has the story of Moses reached you?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:10: When he saw a fire and said to his family: "Hold on! I have just perceived a fire; perhaps I will bring a brand from it for you, or I will find some guidance at the fire about the way to follow."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:11: When he came to it, a voice called out: "Moses!
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:12: Verily I am your Lord! Take off your shoes. You are in the sacred valley, Tuwa!
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:13: I Myself have chosen you; therefore, give ear to what is revealed.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:14: Verily I am Allah. There is no god beside Me. So serve Me and establish Prayers to remember Me.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:15: The Hour of Resurrection is coming. I have willed to keep the time of its coming hidden so that everyone may be recompensed in accordance with his effort.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:16: Let him who does not believe in it and follows his lust not turn your thought away from it, lest you are ruined.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:17: And what is in your right hand, O Moses?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:18: Moses answered: "This is my staff. I lean on it (when I walk), and with it I beat down leaves for my flock, and I have many other uses for it."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:20: So he threw it down, and lo! it was a rapidly moving snake.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:21: Then He said: "Seize it and have no fear. We shall restore it to its former state.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:22: And place your hand in your armpit, it will come forth shining white, without blemish. This is another Sign of Allah,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:23: for We shall show you some of Our greatest Signs.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:24: And go to Pharaoh now for he has transgressed all bounds."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:25: Moses said: "Lord! Open my breast for me;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:26: and ease my task for me,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:27: and loosen the knot from my tongue
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:28: so that they may understand my speech;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:29: and appoint for me, from my household, someone who will help me bear my burden -
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:32: and let him share my task
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:33: that we may abundantly extol Your glory;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:35: Verily, You have always watched over us."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:36: He said: "Moses, your petition is granted.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:37: We have again bestowed Our favour upon you.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:38: Recall, when We indicated to your mother through inspiration:
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:39: 'Put the baby into a chest and then throw him in the river. The river will throw him up on the shore, and then an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his will take him.' And I spread My love over you in order that you might be reared in My sight.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:40: Recall, when your sister went along, saying: 'Shall I direct you to one who will take charge of him?' Thus We brought you back to your mother so that her heart might be gladdened and she might not grieve. Moses, recall when you slew a person. We delivered you from distress and made you go through several trials. Then you stayed for several years among the people of Midian, and now you have come at the right moment as ordained.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:41: I have chosen you for My service.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:42: So go forth, both you and your brother, with My Signs, and do not slacken in remembering Me.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:43: Go both of you to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed all bounds,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:44: and speak to him gently, perhaps he may take heed or fear (Allah)."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:45: The two said:" Lord! We fear he may commit excesses against us, or transgress all bounds."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:46: He said: "Have no fear. I am with you, hearing and seeing all.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:47: So, go to him, and say: 'Behold, both of us are the Messengers of your Lord. Let the Children of Israel go with us, and do not chastise them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord; and peace shall be for him who follows the true guidance.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:48: It has been revealed to us that chastisement awaits those who called the lie to the truth and turned away from it.' "
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:49: Pharaoh said:" Moses! Who is the Lord of the two of you?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:50: He said: "Our Lord is He Who gave everything its form and then guided it."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:51: Pharaoh asked: "Then, what is the state of the former generations?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:52: Moses said: "Its knowledge is with my Lord, recorded in the Book. My Lord does not err, nor does He forget."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:53: He it is Who spread the earth for you; and made in it paths for you, and sent down water from the sky, and then through it We brought forth many species of diverse plants.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:54: So eat yourself and pasture your cattle. Surely there are many Signs in this for people of understanding.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:55: From this very earth We created you and to the same earth We shall cause you to return, and from it We shall bring you forth to life again.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:56: Indeed We showed Pharaoh Our Signs, all of them, but he declared them to be false and rejected them.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:57: He said: "Have you come to us to drive us out of our land by your sorcery?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:58: We shall confront you with a sorcery like your own. So appoint a day when both of us might meet face to face in an open space; an appointment which neither we nor you shall fail to keep."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:59: Moses said: "The appointment to meet you is on the Day of the Feast and let all people come together before noon."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:60: Pharaoh went back and concerted all his stratagem and returned for the encounter.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:61: (At the time of the encounter) Moses said to them: "Woe to you! Do not invent falsehoods against Allah lest He destroy you with a scourge. Surely those who invent lies shall come to grief."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:62: Thereupon they wrangled among themselves about the matter and conferred in secret.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:63: Some of them said: "These two are magicians, who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and to destroy your excellent way of life.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:64: So muster all your stratagem and come forth in a row. Whoever prevails today shall triumph."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:65: The magicians said: "Moses, will you throw down or shall we be the first to throw?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:66: Moses replied: "No, let it be you to throw first." Then suddenly it appeared to Moses, owing to their magic, as if their ropes and staffs were running.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:67: So Moses' heart was filled with fear.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:68: We said to him: "Have no fear; for it is you who will prevail.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:69: And throw down what is in your right hand; it will swallow up all that they have wrought. They have wrought only a magician's stratagem. A magician cannot come to any good, come whence he may."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:70: Eventually the magicians were impelled to fall down prostrate and said: "We believe in the Lord of Moses and Aaron."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:71: Pharaoh said: "What! Did you believe in Him even before I permitted you to do so? Surely, he must be your chief who taught you magic. Now I will certainly cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and will crucify you on the trunks of palm-trees, and then you will come to know which of us can inflict sterner and more lasting torment."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:72: The magicians answered: "By Him Who has created us, we shall never prefer you to the Truth after manifest Signs have come to us. So decree whatever you will. Your decree will pertain, at the most, to the present life of the world.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:73: We believe in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and also forgive us the practice of magic to which you had compelled us. Allah is the Best and He alone will abide."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:74: The truth is that Hell awaits him who comes to his Lord laden with sin; he shall neither die in it nor live.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:75: But he who comes to Him with faith and righteous works shall be exalted to high ranks,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:76: and shall live for ever in everlasting Gardens beneath which rivers flow. Such will be the reward of those who purify themselves.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:77: Most certainly We revealed to Moses: "Proceed with My servants in the night and strike for them a dry path in the sea. Have no fear of being overtaken, nor be afraid of treading through the sea."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:78: Pharaoh pursued them with his hosts, but they were fully overwhelmed by the sea.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:79: Pharaoh led his people astray; he did not guide them aright.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:80: Children of Israel! We saved you from your enemy and made a covenant with you on the right side of the Mount and sent down on you manna and quails,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:81: saying: "Partake of the good things that We have provided for you, but do not transgress lest My wrath fall upon you; for he upon whom My wrath falls is ruined.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:82: But I am indeed Most Forgiving to him who repents and believes and does righteous works and keeps to the Right Way."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:83: "But, O Moses, what has made you come in haste from your people?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:84: He said: "They are close behind me, and I hastened to You, Lord, that You may be pleased with me."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:85: Said He: "Verily We tested your people in your absence and the Samiri led them astray."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:86: Moses returned to his people full of wrath and grief, and said: "My people! Has your Lord not made good an excellent promise He made to you? And has a long time passed since those promises were fulfilled? Or was it to incur the wrath of your Lord that you broke your promise with me?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:87: They answered: "We did not break our promise with you out of our own volition; but we were laden with the load of people's ornaments, and we simply threw them down(into the fire), and the Samiri also threw down something,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:88: and brought out of there (from the molten gold) the effigy of a calf that lowed." The people cried out: "This is your deity and the deity of Moses, whom Moses has forgotten."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:89: Did they not see that it did not return a word to them, and had no power either to hurt them or to cause them any benefit?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:90: Certainly Aaron had said to them even before (the return of Moses): "My people, you were fallen into error because of the calf. Surely your Lord is Most Compassionate; so follow me and obey my command."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:91: But they answered: "By no means shall we cease to worship it until Moses returns to us."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:92: (After rebuking his people) Moses turned to Aaron and said: "Aaron! What prevented you, when you saw them going astray,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:93: from following my way? Have you disobeyed my command?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:94: Aaron answered: "Son of my mother! Do not seize me with my beard, nor by (the hair of) my head. I feared that on returning you might say: 'You sowed discord among the Children of Israel, and did not pay heed to my words.'"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:95: Moses said: "What, then, is your case, O Samiri?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:96: He answered: "I saw what the people did not see. So I took a handful of dust from the trail of the Messenger, and I flung it (into the fire). Thus did my mind prompt me."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:97: Moses said: "Be gone, then. All your life you shall cry: 'Untouchable.' There awaits a term for your reckoning that you cannot fail to keep. Now look at your god that you devotedly adored: We shall burn it and scatter its remains in the sea.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:98: Your God is none else than Allah, beside Whom there is no god. His knowledge embraces everything."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:99: (O Muhammad), thus do We recount to you the events of the past, and We have bestowed upon you from Ourself an admonition.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:100: He who turns away from it will surely bear a heavy burden on the Day of Resurrection,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:101: and will abide under this burden for ever. Grievous shall be the burden on the Day of Resurrection,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:102: the Day when the Trumpet shall be sounded and We shall muster the sinners, their eyes turned blue with terror.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:103: They shall whisper among themselves: "You stayed on the earth barely ten days."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:104: We know well what they will say to one another: We also know that even the most cautious in his estimate will say: "You lived in the world no more than a day."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:105: They ask you concerning the mountains: "Where will they go?" Say: "My Lord will scatter them like dust,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:106: and leave the earth a levelled plain
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:107: in which you shall find no crookedness or curvature.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:108: On that Day people shall follow straight on to the call of the summoner, no one daring to show any haughtiness. Their voices shall be hushed before the Most Compassionate Lord, so that you will hear nothing but a whispering murmur.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:109: On that Day intercession shall not avail save of him whom the Most Compassionate Lord permits, and whose word of intercession is pleasing to Him.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:110: He knows all that is ahead of them and all that is behind them, while the others do not know.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:111: All faces shall be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting Lord, and he who bears the burden of iniquity will have failed;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:112: but whosoever does righteous works, being a believer, shall have no fear of suffering wrong or loss."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:113: (O Muhammad), thus have We revealed this as an Arabic Qur'an and have expounded in it warning in diverse ways so that they may avoid evil or become heedful.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:114: Exalted is Allah, the True King! Hasten not with reciting the Qur'an before its revelation to you is finished, and pray: "Lord! Increase me in knowledge."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:115: Most certainly We had given Adam a command before, but he forgot. We found him lacking in firmness of resolution.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:116: Recall when We said to the angels: "Prostrate yourselves before Adam"; all prostrated themselves save Iblis. He refused.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:117: Then We said: "Adam! He is an enemy to you and to your wife. So let him not drive both of you out of Paradise and plunge you into affliction,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:118: (for in Paradise) neither are you hungry nor naked,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:119: nor face thirst or scorching heat."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:120: But Satan seduced him, saying: "Adam! Shall I direct you to a tree of eternal life and an abiding kingdom?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:121: Then the two of them ate the fruit of that tree and their shameful parts became revealed to each other, and they began to cover themselves with the leaves from the Garden. Thus Adam disobeyed his Lord and strayed into error.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:122: Thereafter his Lord exalted him, accepted his repentance, and bestowed guidance upon him,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:123: and said: "Get down, both of you, (that is, man and Satan), and be out of it; each of you shall be an enemy to the other. Henceforth if there comes to you a guidance from Me, then whosoever follows My guidance shall neither go astray nor suffer misery.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:124: But whosoever turns away from this Admonition from Me shall have a straitened life; We shall raise him blind on the Day of Resurrection,"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:125: where-upon he will say: "Lord! Why have You raised me blind when I had sight in the world?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:126: He will say: "Even so it is. Our Signs came to you and you ignored them. So shall you be ignored this Day."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:127: Thus do We requite him who transgresses and does not believe in the signs of your Lord (during the life of the world); and surely the punishment of the Hereafter is even more terrible and more enduring.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:128: Did they not find any guidance in the fact that We destroyed many nations in whose ruined dwelling-places they now walk about? Surely there are many Signs in them for people endowed with wisdom.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:129: Were it not for a word already gone from your Lord, the decree (of their destruction) would have come to pass.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:130: So bear patiently with what they say. Glorify your Lord, praising Him before sunrise and before sunset, and in the watches of the night, and glorify Him and at the ends of the day that you may attain to happiness.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:131: Do not turn your eyes covetously towards the embellishments of worldly life that We have bestowed upon various kinds of people to test them. But the clean provision bestowed upon you by your Lord is better and more enduring.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:132: Enjoin Prayer on your household, and do keep observing it. We do not ask you for any worldly provision; rather, it is We Who provide you, and ultimately the pious will end up the best.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:133: They ask: "Why does he not bring us a (miraculous) sign from his Lord?" Has there not come to them a Book containing the teachings of the previous scriptures?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:134: Had We destroyed them through some calamity before his coming, they would have said: "Our Lord! Why did You not send any Messenger to us that we might have followed Your signs before being humbled and disgraced?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).20:135: Tell them, (O Muhammad): "Everyone is waiting for his end. Wait, then, and you will soon know who are the people of the Right Way, and are rightly-guided."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:1: The time of people's reckoning has drawn near, and yet they turn aside in heedlessness.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:2: Whenever any fresh admonition comes to them from their Lord they barely heed it and remain immersed in play,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:3: their hearts being set on other concerns. The wrong-doers whisper to one another: "This person is no more than a mortal like yourselves. Will you, then, be enchanted by sorcery while you see?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:4: He said: "My Lord knows well all that is spoken in the heavens and the earth. He is All-Hearing, All- Knowing."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:5: They say: "Nay, these are confused dreams; nay, he has forged it; nay, he is a poet. So let him bring us a sign, even as the Messengers of the past were sent with signs."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:6: Not one township that We destroyed before them believed. Would they, then, believe?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:7: (O Muhammad), even before you We never sent any other than human beings as Messengers, and to them We sent revelation. Ask the People of the Book if you do not know.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:8: We did not endow the Messengers with bodies that would need no food; nor were they immortals.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:9: Then We fulfilled the promise We had made to them: We rescued them and those whom We wished, and We destroyed those who exceeded all bounds.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:10: We have bestowed upon you a Book that mentions you. Do you not understand?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:11: How many a wrong-doing town did We shatter and then raise up another people.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:12: Then, when they perceived Our chastisement they took to their heels and fled.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:13: (They were told): "Flee not, but return to your comforts and to your dwellings. You are likely to be questioned."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:14: They said: "Woe to us; surely we were wrong-doers."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:15: They did not cease to cry this until We reduced them to stubble, still and silent.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:16: We did not create in sport the heavens and the earth and all that lies between the two.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:17: Had it been Our will to find a pastime, We would have found one near at hand; if at all We were inclined to do so.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:18: Nay, We hurl the Truth at falsehood so that the Truth crushes falsehood, and lo! it vanishes. Woe to you for what you utter!
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:19: To Him belongs whosoever dwells in the heavens and on earth. Those (angels) that are with Him neither disdain to serve Him out of pride, nor do they weary of it.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:20: They glorify Him night and day, without flagging.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:21: Have they taken earthly gods who are such that they raise up the dead to life?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:22: Had there been any gods in the heavens and the earth apart from Allah, the order of both the heavens and the earth would have gone to ruins. Glory be to Allah, the Lord of the Throne, Who is far above their false descriptions of Him.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:23: None shall question Him about what He does, but they shall be questioned.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:24: Have they taken gods other than Him? Say, (O Muhammad): "Bring forth your proof! Here is the Book with admonition for those of my time and there are also scriptures with admonition for people before me." But most people do not know the Truth, and have, therefore, turned away from it.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:25: Never did We send any Messenger before you to whom We did not reveal: "There is no god but Me. So serve Me alone."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:26: They say: "The Most Compassionate Lord has taken to Himself a son." Glory be to Him! Those whom they so designate are only His honoured servants.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:27: They do not outstrip Him in speech and only act as He commands.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:28: He knows whatever is before them and whatsoever is remote from them and they do not intercede except for him, intercession on whose behalf pleases Him, and they stand constantly in awe of Him.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:29: And if anyone of them were to claim: "Indeed I am a god apart from Him," We shall recompense both with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrong-doers.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:30: Did the unbelievers (who do not accept the teaching of the Prophet) not realize that the heavens and the earth were one solid mass, then We tore them apart, and We made every living being out of water? Will they, then, not believe (that We created all this)?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:31: And We placed firm mountains on earth lest it should sway with them, and We made wide paths in them that they may find their way;
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:32: and We made the sky a secure canopy; and yet they turn away from these Signs.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:33: It is He Who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon. Each of them is floating in its orbit.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:34: (O Muhammad), We did not grant everlasting life to any human being even before you. If you were to die, will they live for ever?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:35: Every living being shall taste death and We shall subject you to ill and good by way of trial, and to Us shall all of you be eventually sent back.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:36: When the unbelievers see you they make you an object of fun, saying: "Is he the one who mentions your gods?" They say so, and yet they reject with disdain the very mention of the Most Compassionate Lord.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:37: Man is hasty by nature. I shall certainly show you My Signs. Do not ask Me to be hasty.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:38: They say: "(Tell us) when will the threat of punishment come to pass if you are truthful?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:39: If only the unbelievers knew of the Hour when they shall not be able to keep off the Fire from their faces, nor from their backs; nor shall they be helped.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:40: That will suddenly come upon them and stupefy them. They shall not be able to ward it off, nor shall they be granted any respite.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:41: Other Messengers before you were also mocked, but those who scoffed at the Messengers were overtaken by the same scourge that they had scoffed at.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:42: Tell them, (O Muhammad): "Who protects you, during the night or the day from the Most Compassionate Lord?" And yet they turn away from the Admonition of their Lord.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:43: Do they have any gods who would protect them against Us? They have no power even to help themselves; nor do they enjoy Our support.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:44: Nay, We generously provided them and their fathers, and they enjoyed Our provision for long. Do they not see that We are now advancing into their territory, diminishing it from different sides? Is it they, then, who will triumph?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:45: Tell them: "I only warn you by the Revelation." But the deaf do not hear the cry when they are warned.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:46: Were only the slightest whiff from your Lord's punishment to touch them, they would cry out: "Woe to us; we were indeed wrong-doers."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:47: We shall set up just scales on the Day of Resurrection so that none will be wronged in the least. (We shall bring forth the acts of everyone), even if it be the weight of a grain of mustard seed. We shall suffice as Reckoners.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:48: Surely We had granted to Moses and Aaron the Criterion (between right and wrong), and Light and Admonition for the good of the God-fearing,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:49: for those who fear their Lord without seeing Him and dread the Hour (of Reckoning).
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:50: This is a Blessed Admonition that We have revealed. Are you, then, going to reject it?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:51: Surely We had bestowed wisdom upon Abraham even earlier, and We knew him well.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:52: Recall, when he said to his father and his people: "What are these images to which you are devoutly clinging?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:53: They answered: "We found our fathers worshipping them."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:54: He said: "Certainly you and your fathers have all been in manifest error."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:55: They said: "Are you expressing your true ideas before us or are you jesting?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:56: He said: "Nay, but your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth which He created and to that I bear witness before you.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:57: By Allah, I shall certainly carry out my plan against your gods after you are gone."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:58: Then he broke them all into pieces, sparing only the supreme one among them that they may possibly return to him.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:59: (When they saw the idols in this state) they said: "Who has done this to our gods? Surely he is one of the wrong-doers."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:60: Some of them said: "We heard a youth called Abraham speak (ill) of them."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:61: The others said: "Bring him, then, before the eyes of the people that they may see (what will be done to him)."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:62: (On Abraham's arrival) they said: "Abraham, are you he who has done this to our gods?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:63: He answered: "Rather it was this supreme one who has done it. So ask them, if they can speak."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:64: Thereupon they turned to their (inner) selves and said (to themselves): "Surely it is you who are the wrong-doers."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:65: Then their minds were turned upside down, and they said: "You know well that they do not speak."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:66: Abraham said: "Do you, then, worship beside Allah a thing that can neither benefit you nor hurt you?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:67: Fie upon you and upon all that you worship beside Allah. Do you have no sense?"
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:68: They said: "Burn him, and come to the support of your gods, if you are going to do anything."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:69: We said: "O fire, become coolness and safety for Abraham."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:70: They had sought to do evil to him, but We caused them to be the worst losers,
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:71: and We saved him and Lot and brought him to the land upon which We had bestowed Our blessings for all the people of the world.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:72: And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift, making each of them righteous.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:73: And We made them into leaders to guide people in accordance with Our command, and We inspired them to good works, and to establish Prayers and to give Zakah. They worshipped Us alone.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:74: We bestowed upon Lot sound judgement and knowledge, and We delivered him from the city that was immersed in foul deeds. They were indeed a wicked people, exceedingly disobedient.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:75: And We admitted him into Our mercy. Verily he was of the righteous.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:76: We bestowed the same favour upon Noah. Recall, when he cried to Us before; We accepted his prayer and delivered him and his household from the great distress
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:77: and We helped him against a people who rejected Our signs as false. They were indeed an evil people and so We drowned them all.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:78: We bestowed the same favour upon David and Solomon. Recall, when they gave judgement regarding a tillage into which the sheep of some people had strayed at night, and We were witnesses to their judgement.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:79: We guided Solomon to the right verdict, and We had granted each of them judgement and knowledge. We made the mountains and the birds celebrate the praise of Allah with David. It was We Who did all this.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:80: It was We Who taught him the art of making coats of mail for your benefit so that it may protect you from each other's violence. Do you, then, give thanks?
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:81: And We subdued the strongly raging wind to Solomon which blew at his bidding towards the land We blessed. We know everything.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:82: And We subdued many devils who dived (into the sea) for him and carried out other jobs besides that. We kept watch over all of them.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:83: We bestowed (the same wisdom, judgement and knowledge) upon Job. Recall, when he cried to his Lord: "Behold, disease has struck me and You are the Most Merciful of those that are merciful."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:84: We accepted his prayer and removed the affliction from him, and We not only restored to him his family but as many more with them as a mercy from Us and as a lesson to the worshippers.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:85: And (We bestowed the same favour) upon Ishmael, Idris and Dhu al-Kifl, for they were all steadfast.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:86: And We admitted them into Our mercy, for they were of the righteous.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:87: And We bestowed Our favour upon Dhu al-Nun. Recall, when he went forth enraged, thinking We have no power to take him to task. Eventually he cried out in the darkness:" There is no god but You. Glory be to You! I have done wrong."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:88: Thereupon We accepted his prayer, and rescued him from grief. Thus do We rescue the believers.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:89: And We bestowed favour upon Zechariah, when he cried to his Lord: "Lord! Leave me not solitary (without any issue). You are the Best Inheritor."
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:90: So We accepted his prayer and bestowed upon him John, and We made his wife fit (to bear a child). Verily they hastened in doing good works and called upon Us with longing and fear, and humbled themselves to Us.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:91: And also recall the woman who guarded her chastity: We breathed into her of Our spirit, and made her and her son a Sign to the whole world.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:92: Verily this community of yours is a single community, and I am your Lord; so worship Me.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:93: But they tore asunder their faith into many parts. But to Us they are bound to return.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:94: Then whosoever does righteous works, while believing, his striving will not go unappreciated. We record them all for him.
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:95: It has been ordained against every town that We ever destroyed that they shall not return (to enjoy a new lease of life)
A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary).21:96: until Gog and Magog are let loose, and begin swooping from every mound,
